--- SOURCE 1: 北京大学校史馆 ---
URL: https://www.xsg.pku.edu.cn/details/1595.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the Peking University (北京大学) History Museum website is a biographical article titled "北大的才女——冯沅君（北大第一位女研究生）" (A Talented Woman of Peking University — Feng Yuanjun, the First Female Graduate Student of Peking University), published on 2020-03-30 and written by 谢宁.

**Overview:** Feng Yuanjun (冯沅君, 1900-1974), originally named Feng Shulan, was a renowned literary historian, drama historian, and writer from Tanghe, Henan Province. She was among the first influential female writers of post-May Fourth Movement new literature, ranked alongside celebrated writers Bing Xin (冰心) and Lu Yin (庐隐). She graduated from Beijing Women's Higher Normal School in 1922, became Peking University's first female graduate student at the Institute of National Studies in 1925, and earned a PhD in literature from the University of Paris in 1935. She taught at Jinling Women's University, Fudan University, Sun Yat-sen University, Wuhan University, and Shandong University, where she later became vice president.

**Key biographical events (chronological):**
- **1900 (Sept 4):** Born in Qiyi Town, Tanghe County, Henan, into a wealthy official family. Her grandfather Feng Yuwen was a poet; her father Feng Taiyi was a Qing Dynasty jinshi who served under Governor-General Zhang Zhidong and later became magistrate of Chongyang County, Hubei.
- **Early education:** Showed exceptional literary talent from age 5, memorizing Tang poems while listening to her brothers' lessons. Her mother Wu Qingzhi was supportive of her education.
- **1917:** Persuaded her mother to let her attend Beijing Women's Higher Normal School, famously declaring she would give up her dowry money for tuition. She passed the entrance exam (a single composition test) easily.
- **May Fourth Movement (1919):** Actively participated, famously leading students to smash a lock on the school gate to protest the principal's restrictions, and drafted a petition to President Xu Shichang on behalf of 15 women's schools. She also adapted "孔雀东南飞" (Peacock Flying Southeast) into a play and performed the role of the villainous mother-in-law.
- **1922:** Graduated and enrolled at Peking University's Institute of National Studies as its first female graduate student.
- **1923-1926:** Published short stories under the pen name "淦女士" including 《隔绝》、《隔绝之后》、《慈母》、《旅行》, later collected as 《卷葹》(Juanshi). These works dealt with women's pursuit of marriage freedom and individual liberty. Lu Xun praised her work and included 《卷葹》 in his "乌合丛书" (Motley Collection), noting that "卷葹" is a small grass that survives even when its heart is pulled out.
- **1924-1926:** Became a contributor to 《语丝》 magazine, later changing her pen name to "沅君" (derived from Qu Yuan's "Nine Songs"). Her stories included 《劫灰》、《贞妇》、《缘法》.
- **1926:** Met her future husband Lu Kanru (陆侃如), a fellow classical literature scholar from Peking University, three years her junior.
- **1931:** Published 《中国诗史》(History of Chinese Poetry) with her husband Lu Kanru, praised as "取材审慎，要言不烦" (carefully selected material, concise and to the point) — the only poetry history work of its time. Lu Xun recommended it alongside works by major scholars.
- **1932:** Traveled to France with her husband, both enrolling in the doctoral program at the University of Paris. They joined the anti-war, anti-fascist alliance organized by Henri Barbusse.
- **1935:** Earned her doctorate from the University of Paris and returned to China. Taught at Yenching University (husband) and Hebei Women's Normal School.
- **1937:** Composed poems protesting the Marco Polo Bridge Incident (July 7 Incident) and Japan's invasion.
- **1938-1945:** Wartime years of displacement across Yunnan, Guangdong, Sichuan. Published collections 《四余诗稿》、《四余词稿》、《四余续稿》. In 1942, organized the "中华文艺界抗敌协会" (China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Resistance Association) Sichuan Northern Branch in Santai with her husband at the request of Lao She. Wrote important academic works 《古剧说汇》、《古优解》 during this period.
- **Post-war:** Taught at Shandong University in Qingdao from 1947.
- **Post-1949:** Served as professor, then vice president of Shandong University (appointed 1963). Was elected to the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd National People's Congresses. Co-authored (with Lu Kanru) the revised 《中国文学简史》, translated into English and Czech, which Mao Zedong kept on his desk as a favorite book.
- **1957:** Her husband was labeled a "rightist" (右派). When pressured to denounce him, she famously replied: "我大半辈子与'老虎'同寝共枕，竟无察觉，是得了神经麻痹症吧？" ("I've slept with a 'tiger' for most of my life without noticing — am I suffering from nerve paralysis?")
- **1958:** Herself became a target of the "white flag" campaign, forced to crush ore on Qianfo Mountain.
- **Cultural Revolution:** Persecuted as a "reactionary academic authority," forced to clean corridors and toilets, fell from a platform during a struggle session.
- **1974 (June 17):** Died of rectal cancer. Her final act was giving an impromptu lecture to hospital staff and patients just days before her death.

**Academic philosophy:** Her famous motto was "做学问，功夫要死，心眼要活" (In scholarship, one must work with stubborn effort but keep an agile mind). She left behind millions of characters of reading notes, and her three papers on ancient performers (《古优解》 etc.) cited over 100 Chinese and foreign sources.

**Legacy and philanthropy:** Despite being a top-tier (一级) professor with high income, she lived extremely frugally. She donated 40 silver dollars to support a persecuted philosopher's family pre-1949, purchased 10,000 yuan of government bonds in the early PRC period, and planned to leave her savings as an academic scholarship for the nation. Her husband's will donated their entire book collection and savings to Shandong University. Her motto was "生前为民族，身后为国家" (serve the nation in life, give to the nation in death).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"在新旧交替的时期与其作已经宣告破产的礼法的降服者，不如作方生的主义真理的牺牲者。" (From her novel — "In this transitional era, it is better to be a sacrifice for a newborn truth than to submit to an already bankrupt moral code."), "身命可以牺牲，意志自由不可以牺牲，不得自由我宁死。人们要不知道争恋爱自由，则所有的一切都不必提了。这是我的宣言……" (Her declaration — "Life can be sacrificed, but freedom of will cannot; I would rather die than live without freedom."), "做学问，功夫要死，心眼要活。" (Her scholarly motto — "In scholarship, one must work with stubborn effort but keep an agile mind."), "我一介寒儒，连个后嗣亦无，能为国家民族留点什么？我想个人艰窘一点，存几个钱，身后让国家做学术奖金，奖掖后人吧！" (Her stated wish to leave her savings as national academic scholarships.), "我大半辈子与'老虎'同寝共枕，竟无察觉，是得了神经麻痹症吧？" (Her famous defiant response when pressured to denounce her husband in 1957.)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 环球人物 ---
URL: http://paper.people.com.cn/hqrw/html/2012-08/26/content_1112242.htm?div=-1

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from 《环球人物》 (Global People) magazine, written by historian 张耀杰, profiles the life and marriage standards of Chinese female writer 冯沅君 (Feng Yuanjun, 1900-1974), who was a pioneering female college student, feminist love-story writer, and later university professor. She was the sister of philosopher 冯友兰 (Feng Youlan) and geologist 冯景兰, and wife of classical literature scholar 陆侃如 (Lu Kanru).

Key biographical details:
- Born September 4, 1900, in 祁仪镇, 唐河县, 河南南阳, into a wealthy scholarly family. Her father 冯台异 was a 1898 jinshi (imperial examination graduate) who served in Zhang Zhidong's staff and died in 1908 as a county magistrate.
- Her feet were bound by her mother as a child, and her father arranged her marriage before his death to a wealthy young man from 方庄.
- In 1917, she insisted on going to Beijing to study at the newly upgraded 国立北京女子高等师范 (National Beijing Women's Higher Normal School), becoming one of the first generation of female university students in China's public education history. Her mother defied convention and took responsibility for allowing her to leave.
- During the May Fourth Movement (1919), she participated in demonstrations and drafted the manifesto to expel school principal 方还.
- The death of her classmate 李超 (Li Chao) in 1919, a victim of patriarchal family oppression, sparked a wave of anti-arranged-marriage sentiment. Feng Yuanjun led the movement by breaking off her own arranged engagement.

--- SOURCE 2: 本色书生——傅刚教授访谈录 ---
URL: https://news.pku.edu.cn/mtbdnew/058728e267e74ab4835cc3156c59d48e.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is an in-depth interview (published in 《名作欣赏》2021年第7、8期) with Professor 傅刚 (Fu Gang), a renowned scholar of ancient Chinese literature at Peking University. The interview traces his life and academic journey through a series of questions posed by 杨阿敏.

**Early Life and Education (1956-1975):** Fu Gang was born in 1956 to an illiterate peasant family in Suining County, Jiangsu Province. His father was a provincial labor model who met Chairman Mao in the early 1950s but was unjustly accused during the 1964 "Four Cleanups Movement" and died in 1968. Fu Gang grew up during the Cultural Revolution, read widely from borrowed books (classical novels, Gorky's works, modern Chinese literature), and developed a passion for writing. He attended 睢宁县中学 (a prestigious school descended from the Qing-era 昭义书院) through recommendation.

**Work in Sugar Factory (1975-1977):** After high school graduation, he worked as a temporary laborer at a county sugar factory (which also produced liquor), earning 1 yuan/day. He endured extremely hard physical labor in the liquor workshops, working 8+ hour shifts with heavy wooden shovels. His greatest aspiration at that time was to have Sundays off.

**College Entrance Exam (1977):** When the gaokao was restored, he successfully passed and was admitted to 徐州师范学院 (Xuzhou Normal College) Chinese Department — the first cohort after the gaokao restoration. He was one of few from his area to attend university.

**Undergraduate Years (1978-1982):** At Xuzhou Normal College, he read voraciously in the library. Notable teachers included 廖旭东 (Modern Chinese), 王进珊, 吴奔星, 郭广伟, 邱鸣皋, 郑云波, and 吴汝煜. His undergraduate thesis 《文贵清省说的时代意义——论陆云〈与兄平原书〉》 was later published in 《文艺理论研究》(1984) through the recommendation of his future mentor 马茂元.

**Graduate Studies at Shanghai Normal University (1983-1986):** He chose Shanghai Normal University because it was the only institution nationally recruiting graduate students specializing in Wei-Jin-Northern-Southern Dynasties literature that year. He studied under 曹融南 (a graduate of Central University's 1933 cohort who studied under Huang Kan, Wang Dong, and Wu Mei). Despite being the least prestigious candidate, he was the only one of three finalists admitted. He also studied with 马茂元, a brilliant scholar of Tang poetry who could recite over 10,000 poems from memory and came from the famous Tongcheng Ma family (grandfather 马其昶).

**PhD at Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1993-1996):** He studied under 曹道衡, a renowned scholar of pre-Tang literature. Cao Daoleng was from a scholarly family (related to the Pan family and Gu Tinglong), educated at Wuxi Guoxue Institute and Peking University, and pioneered research on Northern Dynasties literature and regional literary geography. Fu Gang's doctoral dissertation 《昭明文选研究》 (on the Wen Xuan) was supervised by Cao, won the prestigious "Excellent Doctoral Dissertation" award (one of only two in ancient literature nationwide).

**Postdoctoral Research at Peking University (1996-1998):** Supervised by 袁行霈, he conducted research on Wen Xuan textual criticism (版本研究). His postdoctoral report 《文选版本研究》 (published by Peking University Press in 2000) overturned the conclusions of Qing scholars (including 《四库总目提要》 and 顾广圻) regarding Li Shan's commentary edition, established that written-copy and printed-copy textual features must be treated separately, and initiated Wen Xuan textual studies as a major field. He later spent 2.5 years in Japan collecting materials on Japanese-held manuscripts.

**Academic Career:** He is now a 博雅特聘教授 (Boyi Distinguished Professor) at Peking University, Director of the Ancient Chinese Poetry Research Center, President of the Chinese Wen Xuan Studies Association, and Vice President of the Pre-Qin Literature Research Association. He is leading a major National Social Science Fund project on 《春秋左传》校注及研究.

**Reflections on Education:** Fu Gang emphasizes the importance of reading widely, the value of mentorship, and the unique training he received from a sequence of increasingly younger teachers (郝立诚, 曹融南, 曹道衡, 袁行霈). He expresses concern about the current academic environment, citing widespread academic misconduct, and is reluctant to offer advice to young scholars beyond urging them to follow their conscience — quoting 《史记》's admonition "务正学以言，无曲学以阿世" (pursue correct learning in speech, don't distort learning to flatter the world).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"务正学以言，无曲学以阿世。" (from 《史记》— quoted by Fu Gang regarding academic integrity), "曹先生是厚积厚发，他很勤奋，不断地写文章...到了70岁以后，新的学术创见还是不断地产生。" (on Cao Daoleng's scholarly productivity), "我提出写抄本阶段的文字特征，刻本阶段的文字特征要分开看，不能混在一起，这个看法现在好像越来越多人接受了。" (on his Wen Xuan textual research), "《四库总目提要》和顾广圻的基本结论是不对的，因为他们没有看到真正的国子监本李善注《文选》..." (on overturning traditional views of Wen Xuan editions), "马先生的艺术感觉非常敏锐，艺术感把握得非常准确，表达得又好，国内同辈学者中没有人能超过他。" (on Ma Maoyuan)

--- SOURCE 8: 湖南大学廖可斌：文献学如何与文学研究相结合-中国语言文化学院 ---
URL: https://zwxy.gdufs.edu.cn/info/1123/9458.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
On December 11, 2024, Professor Liao Kebin (廖可斌) of Hunan University's School of Liberal Arts delivered an academic lecture titled "How Philology Combines with Literary Research" (文献学如何与文学研究相结合) at Room 408, Building 7, Baiyunshan Campus of Guangdong University of Foreign Studies. The lecture was hosted by Professor Chen Enwei (陈恩维), with approximately 50 teachers and students in attendance. Guest discussants included Professor Wang Jingzhou (王京州), Deputy Dean of Jinan University's School of Liberal Arts, and Professor Xiang Yurong (项裕荣), Dean of the School of Literature and Media at Guangdong Polytechnic Normal University.

Key points of the lecture: (1) Liao emphasized that undergraduate and graduate students should adopt different approaches to studying ancient literature—undergraduates should read broadly to build foundations, while graduate students should focus on philological and textual version issues. (2) Using works like Journey to the West as examples, he illustrated differences between textual versions and stressed the importance of using correct editions. (3) He proposed a "point–plane–line" or "point–line–plane" (点—面—线/点—线—面) methodology for philological research to deepen understanding of literary works and their historical contexts. (4) He advised students to read and punctuate classical texts to improve classical Chinese reading ability, and to choose research subjects connected to their hometowns or familiar regions. (5) He noted common errors in citation, literary analysis, and evaluation of literary value, and recommended improving aesthetic appreciation through broad reading, opera, concerts, art exhibitions, and field trips.

In the discussion session, Professor Chen Enwei responded to the "point-line-plane" method based on his own academic experience. Professor Xiang Yurong shared insights on achieving academic breakthroughs through extensive document reading. Professor Wang Jingzhou discussed the application of digital humanities technology in ancient text collation, emphasizing that AI has learning capabilities enabling high efficiency and accuracy, while urging scholars to embrace digital tools but maintain critical thinking and avoid over-reliance on technology. Students raised questions about handling vast amounts of documents, which the scholars addressed with professional advice. The event concluded with a group photo.

Professor Liao Kebin is a member of the New Century Hundred-Thousand-Ten-Thousand Talents Project and a Changjiang Scholar Distinguished Professor, specializing in Ming-Qing literature and ancient drama and fiction. His notable works include "Research on the Ming Dynasty Literary Archaism Movement," "History of Ming Dynasty Literary Thought," and "The Dimension of Literary History." He has published over 100 academic papers and won two Ministry of Education second-class awards for outstanding achievements in humanities and social sciences research, plus one national second-class teaching achievement award.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"文献研究应走'点—面—线'或'点—线—面'之路，说明如何通过文献研究深入理解文学作品及其历史背景。" (Philological research should follow the "point–plane–line" or "point–line–plane" path to deeply understand literary works and their historical backgrounds.), "本科生阶段应广泛阅读，扩展知识面，打好基础，而研究生阶段则应开始关注文献和版本问题，深入研究。" (Undergraduates should read broadly to expand knowledge and build foundations, while graduate students should begin to focus on philological and textual version issues for in-depth research.), "人工智能具有学习能力，能够在古籍整理工作中实现高效率和准确性。他鼓励学者们积极拥抱数字技术，同时也提醒不可过度依赖技术，应保持批判性思维。" (AI has learning capabilities and can achieve high efficiency and accuracy in ancient text collation. --- SOURCE 1: 袁行霈 ---
URL: https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%A2%81%E8%A1%8C%E9%9C%88/1878173

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Baidu Baike (Baidu Encyclopedia) entry for 袁行霈 (Yuan Xingpei), a prominent Chinese classical literature scholar. He was born on April 18, 1936, in Jinan, Shandong Province, with ancestral roots in Wujin, Jiangsu. His courtesy name is 春澍 (Chunshu).

**Identity & Positions:** Yuan Xingpei is a professor in the Chinese Department of Peking University, Director of the Peking University Academy of Chinese Studies (国学研究院), Director of the Peking University Center for Chinese Traditional Culture Research, Editor-in-chief of the annual journal "国学研究" (Chinese Studies), member of the Peking University Council, and Director of the Humanities Division at Peking University. He also serves as the Director (馆长) of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History (中央文史研究馆), Standing Committee member of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), Vice-Chairman of the China Democratic League Central Committee, and member of the State Council Academic Degrees Committee. He became a foreign member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in April 2018.

**Education & Career Timeline:** 
- 1953: Admitted to Peking University Chinese Department
- 1957: Graduated and stayed at PKU as a faculty member, becoming a teaching assistant under Lin Geng (林庚)
- 1958-1960: Participated in labor assignments including coal mining in Chengzi, Beijing and steel production work
- 1960s: Designated as a "白专" (white-and-expert) model during political campaigns; criticized during the Cultural Revolution and sent to labor reform camp at Liyuzhou, where he survived a serious vehicle accident
- 1979: Promoted to lecturer; published notable papers including "山海经初探" and began gaining academic attention
- 1980: Appointed associate professor
- 1982-1983: Taught at Tokyo University in Japan
- 1984: Became specially-appointed professor in Chinese Department
- 1986: Qualified as doctoral supervisor
- 1992: Became Director of PKU Chinese Traditional Culture Research Center and Editor of 《国学研究》
- 1992-1993, 1998: Visiting professor at National University of Singapore
- 1997: Visiting scholar at Harvard-Yenching Institute; lectured at Harvard, Yale, Columbia, Washington, and Hawaii universities
- 1999: Became Director of PKU Humanities Division
- 2000: Became Director of PKU Academy of Chinese Studies
- 2004: Visiting professor at City University of Hong Kong
- 2005: Confirmed as senior professor at PKU (enjoying treatment equivalent to CAS academicians); also appointed professor at Nanyang Technological University
- January 18, 2006: Appointed Director of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History (the seventh director, succeeding Fu Dingyi, Zhang Shizhao, Yang Dongchun, Ye Shengtao, Xiao Qian, and Qi Gong)

**Key Academic Contributions:**
- Advocated "纵通" (vertical integration) and "横通" (horizontal integration) methodology in literary studies, articulated in a 1978 Guangming Daily article
- Major works include 《中国诗歌艺术研究》(1987, with Japanese and Korean translations), 《陶渊明集笺注》, 《陶渊明研究》, 《中国文学概论》, and the four-volume 《中国文学史》(1999) which he edited with 29 scholars from 19 universities—a textbook that won multiple national awards including the Fifth National Book Award (2001)
- Spent 20 years on Tao Yuanming research across three books: 《陶渊明研究》, 《陶渊明集笺注》, and 《陶渊明影像》
- Served as chief editor of the four-volume 《中华文明史》, whose English translation was published by Cambridge University Press (2012)
- Other edited works include 《中国地域文化通览》 (expected 15 million characters, 2012) and 《缀英集——中央文史研究馆馆员诗选》
- Recent star-map works include 《诗经国风新注》(2018, with Xu Jianwei and Cheng Sudong), 《好诗不厌百回读》(2017, selected for national "大众喜爱的50种图书"), and 《中华传统文化经典百篇》(2016, co-edited with Wang Zhongwei and Chen Jinyu)

**Awards & Honors:** National Outstanding Teaching Achievement Award (Special Grade, 1989), National Education System Model Worker and People's Teacher Medal (1991), Beijing People's Teacher title (1993, top ten by public vote), Beijing Advanced Worker (1995), PKU "Cai Yuanpei Award" (2006, considered PKU's highest faculty honor), and multiple awards for 《中国诗歌艺术研究》 and 《中国文学史》.

**Teaching & Character:** Renowned as a model of "儒雅" (cultured elegance) at PKU, following his mentor Lin Geng. His lectures on Tao Yuanming and Tang poetry were among the most popular in the Chinese Department. He emphasized the unity of scholarship and moral character, requiring students to submit both an academic paper and a "moral character paper." His notable students include Meng Erdong (孟二冬). He believes scholarship should have "气象" (grandeur/atmosphere) requiring dedicated attitude, broad-mindedness, and high moral character.

**Views on National Studies (国学):** He holds that guoxue (national studies) cannot save China or lead to modernization, but must be seriously studied as part of China's cultural heritage, approached with analytical, open, and developmental attitudes—absorbing essence and discarding dross.

**Family Background:** Comes from a distinguished scholarly family. His great-grandfather Yuan Jimao was a second-place jinshi (榜眼) in the Daoguang period who died defending Shunchang County during the Taiping Rebellion. His great-grandmother Zuo Xixuan was a literary woman. His grandfather Yuan Xuechang was a juren (举人) in the fifth year of Guangxu; his grandmother Zeng Yi was a famous female traditional Chinese medicine practitioner and poet. His uncle (second uncle) Yuan Lizhun was a late-Qing Hanlin scholar, calligrapher, and collector who served as one of Puyi's teachers.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"所谓'纵通'是'就文学论文学，着重研究文学史上各种现象、体裁、流派的发生、发展和衰落……'所谓'横通'就是力求将文学和史学、哲学、宗教、艺术乃至自然科学结合起来进行研究，'并努力从它们的关联上，从它们之间的相互影响、渗透的关系上，寻求带有规律性的东西'。" — Yuan Xingpei's 1978 article "纵通与横通" on his academic methodology, published in Guangming Daily.
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 中國文化研究所通訊 ---
URL: https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/enewsasp/app/article-details.aspx/D971B65599F6873DA603203511419E4A

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a Chinese-language interview with Professor Yuan Xingpei (袁行霈), published in the 2016 second issue of the Chinese Culture Institute Newsletter (中國文化研究所通訊) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. The interview was conducted on March 31, 2016, at the Institute's "澄軒" (Cheng Xuan) venue. The interviewer was Professor Zhang Jian (張健) of the Chinese Language and Literature Department, with transcription by Xu Yanlian and content organization by Hu Qi.

**About Professor Yuan Xingpei:**
- Born 1936 in Jinan, Shandong; ancestral home in Wujin, Jiangsu.
- Current positions: Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Peking University, Dean of the National Studies Institute (國學研究院), Director of the International Sinologists Research Base, and Chief Editor of "國學研究" (Studies in Sinology).
- Also serves as Director of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History (中央文史研究館), and member of the National Education Advisory Committee.
- Former roles: Standing Committee member of the 8th and 9th CPPCC, Standing Committee member of the 10th NPC, and Vice-Chairman of the China Democratic League Central Committee.
- Major publications include works on Chinese poetry art, Chinese literature, Tao Yuanming studies (including annotated edition and imagery), History of Chinese Literature (chief editor), History of Chinese Civilization (chief editor), and Survey of Chinese Regional Culture (chief editor), among others.

**Part 1: Academic Origins – Solid Foundation in Language and Literature**
- Entered Peking University's Chinese Department in 1953, benefiting from the 1952 reorganization that merged Peking, Tsinghua, and Yenching universities' liberal arts faculties.
- Studied Chinese literary history for four years (six class hours per week) under notable scholars including You Guoen, Pu Jiangqing (formerly Wang Guowei's assistant), Lin Geng, and others.
- Studied five linguistics courses due to department head Yang Hui's emphasis on the organic connection between language and literature, with teachers including Gao Mingkai, Wei Jiangong, Zhou Zumo, Yuan Jiahua, and Wang Li (who authored "漢語史稿" after his course).
- Influenced by scholars Lin Geng (his advisor), Zhu Ziqing (Lin's teacher), and Wen Yiduo, as well as Yu Pingbo and Wu Zuxiang.

**Part 2: Vertical and Horizontal Connections – From Literary History, Civilization History to Regional Culture**
- In 1995, began editing "History of Chinese Literature" as a "21st-century" textbook involving 30 professors from 19 universities.
- Proposed a three-part framework for literary history: "文學本位" (literary-centered approach), "史學思維" (historical thinking), and "文化學視角" (cultural perspective).
- Introduced the "三古七段" (Three Ancient Eras, Seven Periods) theory for literary periodization, breaking from pure dynastic division. Later refined to "三古七段雙視角" (dual perspective).
- Personally wrote chapters and the general introduction; never served as a "nominal chief editor."
- In 1999, initiated and led the compilation of "History of Chinese Civilization" (中華文明史) as a Peking University National Studies Institute project, involving 36 professors over six years, resulting in four volumes.
- The work was translated into English (by Prof. David R. Knechtges, Cambridge University Press), Japanese (by Waseda University's Inahata Koichiro, expanding four volumes to eight), Russian, Korean, Serbian, Hungarian, and Hindi.
- Edited "Survey of Chinese Regional Culture" (中國地域文化通覽) in 34 volumes organized by province/municipality (including Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan), involving about 500 scholars from local culture and history institutions.
- In 2009, proposed a new "Newly Edited and Newly Annotated Thirteen Classics" project to expand beyond the Confucian classics—removing six traditional texts and adding six new ones (Laozi, Zhuangzi, Mozi, Sunzi, Hanfeizi, Xunzi). Yuan personally handles the new annotation of the Book of Songs (詩經).

**Part 3: Work at the National Studies Institute, Sinologist Research Base, and Central Research Institute**
- Peking University National Studies Institute dates to 1992, funded by Nan Huaijin's donation of $100,000 USD. Publications include the journal "國學研究" (36 volumes to date) and the "國學研究叢刊" series. PhD program began in 2001.
- Created the 150-episode TV program "中華文明之光" (Light of Chinese Civilization) with CCTV.
- In 2009, established the International Sinologists Research Base with Hanban, producing journals "國際漢學研究通訊" and "Chinese Literature and Culture" (English, published in the US). Hosted the International Sinologists Translators Conference in 2014.
- Supports Professor Rong Xinjiang's Marco Polo research project, including a new translation of the travel record.
- At the Central Research Institute of Culture and History, succeeded Qigong as Director in 2006. Currently compiling "中國傳統文化經典百篇" (100 Classic Works of Chinese Traditional Culture).

Professor Yuan closes with his motto: "常懷感激之心，長存謙遜之意" (Always harbor gratitude, always maintain humility), expressing thanks to his teachers, colleagues, students, and friends, including those at CUHK.

**Background and Early Life:** Born in 1949 in Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, Mo Lifeng was named by his father with the hope he would "not show his edge" (不露锋芒). **Rustication Period (插队):** During his years in the countryside, Mo Lifeng initially tried to study science textbooks but found them too difficult to self-study, so he turned to humanities. Reading under limited conditions (only one jin of kerosene per month, no electricity), he read extensively—Marxist texts, novels, historical records, and classical poetry. He could recite the entire Art of War (孙子兵法) and Li Sao (离骚) from memory, and memorized 800 of Du Fu's poems. In 1973, after his roof was blown off in a storm, he recalled Du Fu's famous line "安得广厦千万间" and felt deep resonance with the poet. **Academic Career:** In 1975, Mo transferred to Anhui Province for continued rustication. In 1977, when college entrance exams resumed, he entered Anhui University's English department. He became a master's student under renowned scholar Cheng Qianfan (程千帆, born 1913), a distinguished expert in ancient literature, textual criticism, and education. Cheng assigned three additional academic assistants—Zhou Xunchu, Guo Weisen, and Wu Xinlei—to guide Mo's studies ("four teachers for one student, like an apprenticeship").

**Teaching Career:** After graduation, Mo taught at Nanjing University, inheriting Cheng Qianfan's teaching methods and prioritizing teaching over publishing. He became head of the Chinese Department in 2004. He bought his first mobile phone only in 2018 (to use ride-hailing apps), and once publicly apologized to two students he had wrongly criticized for using phones during class (they were actually viewing course materials).

(Mo Lifeng's life philosophy), "Cheng Qianfan wrote in his will: 'In my later years, though I have written somewhat, it is insignificant. But I have carefully cultivated several outstanding students...'", "I encountered Cheng Xiansheng and only then resolved to become a teacher. Since I've chosen to do it, I must do it well!"

--- SOURCE 9: 莫砺锋 黄伟豪：立雪程门薪火传——莫砺锋教授访谈_爱思想 ---
URL: https://www.aisixiang.com/data/159660.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a comprehensive interview with Mo Lifeng (莫砺锋), the first Doctor of Literature produced by the People's Republic of China, conducted by Huang Weihao (黄伟豪), an associate professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. The interview was originally published in 《文治春秋》第一卷 (2024年春) and is hosted on the aisixiang.com (爱思想) academic website. The piece was updated on 2025-02-19.

**Key biographical details:** Mo Lifeng (born 1949) graduated from Nanjing University in 1984 with a doctoral degree in literature, becoming the first literature PhD trained by the PRC. He is now a senior professor at Nanjing University's School of Humanities and Social Sciences, director of Jiangsu Province's Literature and History Research Institute, and holds various academic positions including member of the National Ancient Books Collation and Publishing Planning Leadership Group and honorary president of the Chinese Song Dynasty Literature Society. He authored the ten-volume 《莫砺锋文集》.

**Major themes covered in the interview:**

1. **Becoming the first literature PhD**: Mo graduated high school in 1966 when the Cultural Revolution halted university admissions, spent ten years farming in rural Anhui, then entered Anhui University's English program after the 1977 gaokao restoration. He transferred to Nanjing University's Chinese department under Cheng Qianfan (程千帆) and became the first doctoral student in Nanda's Chinese department in 1982, defending his dissertation in October 1984. His training involved a four-teacher supervision group (Cheng Qianfan, Zhou Xunchu, Guo Weisen, Wu Xinlei) and a mentorship-style (apprentice-like) training model rather than formal coursework.

2. **Academic heritage and the "Southeast Academic" tradition**: Cheng Qianfan inherited the "Zhang-Huang School" (章黄学派) tradition from Huang Kan (黄侃), who studied under Zhang Taiyan (章太炎). The Southeast Academic tradition emphasizes rationality, steadiness, and humanistic care, balancing new culture promotion with preserving traditional Chinese cultural essence. Cheng's hallmark was "combining textual research with criticism" and "building criticism on the foundation of textual evidence."

3. **Cheng Qianfan's teaching methods**: He used heuristic teaching, held biweekly half-day seminars at his home, and treated students with extraordinary dedication. In his will, Cheng wrote that he considered training excellent students more important than his own scholarship. Cheng's dying concern was the publication of Huang Jigang's (黄侃) diaries, not his own collected works—demonstrating his profound reverence for his teachers.

4. **"Chengmen Disciples" (程门弟子)**: Mo notes that they never called themselves a "school" (Cheng forbade this), but the group shares common scholarly values: combining philology (文献学) with literary theory (文艺学), bridging literature and history, empirical research with problem consciousness, and openness to domestic and international academic exchange. The group has recently developed new fields including overseas Chinese classical texts and overseas Sinology research.

5. **Views on "academic" (学术)**: Mo discusses how the definition of scholarship has historically marginalized literary/writing studies (辞章之学), citing the Institute of History and Philology (史语所) founded by Hu Shi and Fu Sinian as perpetuating this bias. He advocates for pluralistic academic standards rather than uniform criteria, and believes academic communities should be limited to smaller, more coherent fields.

6. **The role of philology (文献学)**: Documentary research has greatly strengthened in recent decades, exemplified by comprehensive collections like 《全宋诗》and 《全宋文》. At Nanjing University, ancient literature and classical philology are treated as one unified "two ancient subjects" (两古学科). Cheng's methodology of "building criticism on the foundation of textual evidence" is exemplified by his study of Zhang Ruoxu's 《春江花月夜》, which traced the poem's reception history to show its literary reputation only rose during the Ming dynasty. Mo himself demonstrated that 《桃花溪》attributed to Tang poet Zhang Xu was actually by Song dynasty calligrapher Cai Xiang, a view now accepted by two new editions of 《全唐诗》.

7. **Individual vs. collective research**: Mo strongly favors individual scholarship for humanities research, arguing it requires personal insight and unique judgment. While collective projects are now common, he believes individual works like Tai Jingnong's 《中国文学史》 retain far greater scholarly value than collective textbooks. He agrees with Qiu Xieyou that individual authors should focus on specialized literary history (断代史 or 文体史) rather than comprehensive surveys, citing Chen Yinke's 《元白诗笺证稿》as a model.

8. **"Poetic life" (诗意人生)**: This concept comes not from Heidegger but from reading Chinese classical poetry. Mo argues that Chinese civilization uniquely avoided the dual obscurations of religious theology and metaphysical thinking, allowing Confucianism (positive engagement with life) and Daoism (transcendent freedom) to complement each other in achieving a poetic grasp of life's meaning. He cites Qu Yuan, Tao Yuanming, Li Bai, Du Fu, Su Shi, and Xin Qiji as exemplars of poetic lives.

9. **"Feeling" as the foundation of literary study**: Following Cheng Qianfan, Mo emphasizes that emotional response ("感") is the primary motivation for literary research. His ten years of rural reading during the Cultural Revolution, though without scholarly guidance or utilitarian purpose, provided profound emotional experiences—reading Du Fu's poetry under a roofless hut, reciting Li Yu's lyrics on rainy nights—that continue to shape his scholarship, reflected in works like 《莫砺锋诗话》and 《杜甫评传》.

10. **On Western scholars and methods**: Mo discusses his interactions with Harvard's Stephen Owen (宇文所安), whom he respects as the finest non-Chinese Western scholar of Chinese poetry, though he finds Chinese evaluations of Owen somewhat inflated. Mo wrote a critical review of Owen's 《初唐诗》and 《盛唐诗》, noting factual errors and disagreeing with Owen's judgments (e.g., Owen rates Wang Wei above Li Bai and Du Fu; Mo disagrees with Owen preferring "望" over "见" in Tao Yuanming's poem). Mo advocates pragmatic method use: "methods are valuable only if they solve problems" (寸铁可以杀人), warning against the "myth of methodology."

11. **Assessment of Republican-era scholarship**: Mo argues today's scholarship generally surpasses the Republican era, though that era produced unmatched individual masters (Wang Guowei, Zhang Taiyan, Liang Qichao). He discusses the "rewriting literary history" (重写文学史) movement, criticizing previous literary histories for overemphasizing socioeconomic background ("庸俗社会论") and using rote author-work listings ("作家作品论") instead of tracing literary development. He acknowledges the immense difficulty of truly rewriting literary history, including unresolved questions about periodization.

12. **Popularization work**: Mo entered popular education relatively late, through writing 《莫砺锋诗话》(2004), giving lectures on CCTV's "百家讲坛" (14 lectures on "诗歌唐朝," later compiled into 《莫砺锋说唐诗》, which sold 100,000 copies), and 《莫砺锋评说白居易》. His 《莫砺锋讲唐诗课》(2019) won the "China Good Book Award" (中国好书奖). He argues scholars have a duty to transmit culture to the public, following Confucius's example of "温故知新" and "述而不作." He believes academic research and popularization are mutually reinforcing.

The interview was edited by chendongdong and is filed under the Literature section (文学 > 语言学和文学学人与经典) of aisixiang.com.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"程先生去世前最放不下的是黄季刚先生日记的出版...程先生在人生的最后瞬间不问他本人全集的事，却念念不忘黄季刚先生的书。" — Cheng Qianfan's dying concern was Huang Kan's diary, not his own works, demonstrating his reverence for teachers. Also, in his will Cheng wrote: "所精心培养学生数人，极为优秀" (the students he carefully trained were extremely outstanding).
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://www.chinastory.cn/PCzwdbk/chinastory/wap/detail/20230630/1006000000039761688086003526176672_1.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article profiles Mo Lifeng (莫砺锋), a 74-year-old distinguished professor of ancient Chinese literature at Nanjing University, who recently retired from teaching after a storied career spanning 45 years. Born with a passion for science and engineering, Mo's dreams were shattered by the Cultural Revolution (the abolition of the college entrance exam), leading him to a decade of rural life as an educated youth (知青) during which he self-studied voraciously. After the 1977 restoration of the college entrance exam, he studied English at Anhui University, then entered Nanjing University's ancient literature program under the mentorship of renowned scholar Cheng Qianfan (程千帆), becoming the first PhD student in the Chinese department in 1982.

Key highlights of his career include: a 2002 lecture on Du Fu on CCTV's "Lecture Room" (百家讲坛) which launched his popularization of classical literature, authoring best-selling books (one printing 100,000 copies), and recent lectures in Sichuan (on Su Dongpo at Sansu Shrine and Du Fu at Du Fu Thatched Cottage) each drawing ~2 million online/offline viewers. He recently published two poetry books for elementary and middle school students.

The article also details Mo's personal philosophy and lifestyle: his study named "Ningdun Zhai" (宁钝斋, "Rather Be Dull Studio") reflecting his father's wish for him not to show off sharpness; his embrace of simplicity (he had no mobile phone until 2018, still takes the subway, and apologizes publicly when he wrongly scolds students); his view that reading classics offers "useless use" (无用之用) as spiritual nourishment in modern society; and his educational philosophy that "being a person is more important than scholarship" (比做学问更重要的是做人), warning against raising "refined egoists." He served briefly as department chair but resigned after ~16 months. He is currently dean of the Mei'an Academy (梅庵书院) at Nanjing University. On May 23, 2023, he delivered his "final class" and formally retired from teaching.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"比做学问更重要的是做人，如果没有学会做人，那学问做得再好也没有意义" (Being a person matters more than scholarship; if one hasn't learned to be a good person, no matter how good the scholarship, it is meaningless), "如果我们培养出来的学生都成为精致的利己主义者，我们的教育就失败了" (If our students become refined egoists, our education has failed), "无用之用，方为大用" (The use of the useless is the greatest use - quoting Zhuangzi), "莫砺锋每次谈及这个话题都会笑起来：'别忘了我姓莫，当年父亲起这个名字就是希望我不露锋芒。'" (Mo laughs whenever discussing his name: "Don't forget my surname is Mo [meaning 'do not']; my father named me hoping I would not show my edge"), "感谢南大的同学至今没有把我轰下讲坛，使我完整地走完了教学生涯" (Thank you to Nanjing University students for never driving me off the podium, allowing me to complete my teaching career)

His scholarly work spans pre-Qin philosophy, classical Chinese literature, literary theory and criticism, classical philology, and modern academic history. He served as head of the Jiangsu Provincial Research Institute of Literature and History, consultant to the Chinese Tang Dynasty Literature Society, and in 2016 became head of the Jiangsu Literary Heritage academic steering committee.

--- SOURCE 1: 在学术研究中感受生命的活力——访葛晓音--报刊--中国作家网 ---
URL: https://www.chinawriter.com.cn/n1/2016/0810/c405176-28624277.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from 中国作家网 (China Writers Association website), featuring an interview with 葛晓音 (Ge Xiaoyin), a prominent professor of classical Chinese literature at Peking University. The interview was conducted by 梁海燕 and published in 文艺报 (Literary Gazette) on August 10, 2016.

**About the Scholar:** Ge Xiaoyin was born in Shanghai in August 1946. She entered Peking University's Chinese Department in 1963 (five-year program), but only completed two years of basic coursework before the Cultural Revolution interrupted her studies. After graduation, she spent 7 years in Xinjiang (including work at a farm in Hutubi County and teaching at a school in Changji) and later worked at a cultural center in Xinglong County, Hebei. In 1978, she was admitted to a special "refresher class" at Peking University (selected 25 out of 200 graduates of the 1963-1965 cohorts), and in 1979 began graduate studies under Professor 陈贻焮. She stayed at PKU, became a full professor in 1989, and has also taught at Tokyo University and Hong Kong Baptist University. She served as a National People's Congress deputy and currently serves as a CPPCC member. Her major works include 《汉唐文学的嬗变》《诗国高潮与盛唐文化》《先秦汉魏六朝诗歌体式研究》《八代诗史》《唐宋散文》《山水田园诗派研究》《古诗艺术探微》《唐诗宋词十五讲》.

**Key Themes from the Interview:**

1. **Research Approach:** Ge describes her scholarship as driven by old questions continuously generating new ones, rather than pre-designed research agendas. Her dissertation topic "初盛唐诗歌的发展" was deliberately broad, and subsequent research (on the 中唐古文运动, 北宋诗文革新, the "文儒" stratum of the 开元 era, poetry form/genre studies) all emerged from unresolved issues in earlier work. She spent 10 years (from 2002) completing 《先秦汉魏六朝诗歌体式研究》. She also notes the role of serendipity—e.g., discovering in Tokyo that 李峤's 《百咏》 was highly influential in Japan, which led to two major papers on Tang poetry popularization and 干谒 (self-recommendation) practices.

2. **On Method:** During the 1980s "new methodology" debates (including "三论"), Ge adopted an observational stance, arguing that methods should be judged by whether they solve problems. She wrote "吸取新方法要以传统研究方式为本" in 1985. She cites linguist 朱德熙's metaphor: "A method is like an axe—if an old axe can make good furniture, it's still a good axe." She maintains that Chinese classical poetry is not suited to wholesale application of Western poetics, citing discussions with Japanese scholar 松浦友久.

3. **On "自主设计" (Autonomous Design) in Chinese Scholarship:** Ge agrees Chinese scholars should develop their own research approaches but cautions against rushing to predictions. She emphasizes that Chinese scholars have advantages in linguistic nuance and cultural context that Western (and even Japanese) scholars lack, and advocates deeper integration of literary theory with creative writing practice. Traditional Chinese literary criticism uniquely combines poetic theory with creative practice, which should be better leveraged.

4. **On the Modern Value of Classical Literature Research:** Ge argues scholarship is a component of national culture and carries implications for national prestige. She recounts how a Japanese professor in the early 1980s offered to "teach" Chinese scholars because the Cultural Revolution had destroyed their scholarship, deeply shocking her elders. She cites the "无用之用就是大用" (the use of the useless is great use) principle from Zhuangzi. She gives vivid examples: in 1990 in San Francisco, she gave 14 lectures on Tang poetry to overseas Chinese in one month (a Chinese engineer told her he "felt like a Chinese person again"); in Japan, ordinary citizens held spontaneous poetry recitation meetings; in Shanghai and Beijing, public lectures on classical poetry regularly sell out. She quotes 王安石's 《游褒禅山记》 as her personal motto on perseverance. She also argues that contemporary writers need classical literary grounding or their work becomes "rootless wood and sourceless water."

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article by Liu Mengxi (刘梦溪), published in China Reading Weekly (中华读书报) on May 27, 2015, compares and contrasts two of China's greatest modern scholars: Chen Yinke (陈寅恪, b. 1890) and Qian Zhongshu (钱锺书, b. 1910), who were both admired by the discerning scholar Wu Mi (吴宓).

**Shared Traits:** Both scholars were polymaths who mastered multiple languages. Chen knew roughly 16-17 languages including rare ones like Mongolian, Tibetan, Pali, Western Xia, and Turkic scripts (studied to read Buddhist scriptures), plus Sanskrit learned from Baron von Staël-Holstein in Beijing. Qian knew English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, and Sanskrit fluently. Both had extraordinary memories, vast reading, and came from prestigious scholarly families (Chen's grandfather Chen Baozhen and father Chen Sanli; Qian's father Qian Jibo).

**Differences:** Chen's scholarship directly continued the Qian-Jia textual tradition (乾嘉), with Western influence rarely visible in his works, though he had excellent Western training (studied longest in Germany, possibly influenced by Leopold von Ranke and European positivist historiography). Qian integrated Chinese and Western scholarship openly, freely citing Western texts, effectively practicing comparative literature/culture studies. Chen specialized in history (using poetry and prose to verify historical facts), while Qian specialized in literature and poetics.

**On Hua-Yi Distinction (华夷之辨):** Both scholars concluded that cultural identity, not ethnicity, determines whether someone is "Chinese" or "barbarian." Chen's core doctrine was that culture transcends race, citing Confucius's "有教无类" (education knows no class). Qian reached identical conclusions independently, citing numerous sources including the Book of Northern Qi, Quan Tang Wen, and Yuan Zhen's poetry. Qian even annotated in English: "华夷非族类(ethnos)之殊，而亦礼教(ethos)之辩" (Hua-Yi distinction is not one of ethnos but of ethos/civilization). The author argues Chen's insight renders Huntington's "Clash of Civilizations" theory one-sided.

**On Literary Style (文体论):** Both were advocates of literary style reform. Both praised Han Yu's "以文为诗" (using prose methods in poetry). Chen rated Han Yu even higher than Qian did. On using unofficial histories and novels for historical research, Chen used them directly to verify history, while Qian believed they might not verify facts but could reveal the sentiments of the times. On coincidental similarity of conclusions among different authors, both rejected plagiarism accusations, attributing them to shared source materials or common creative situations.

**On the Liu Rushi Biezhuan (柳如是别传):** The author highly esteems this work as Chen's academic pinnacle, particularly for his use of poetry to verify history. However, Qian reportedly disapproved of the work's style and structure, a view the author confirmed through correspondence with Qian (who notably failed to respond to the author's article on the Biezhuan) and through scholar Wang Rongzu (汪荣祖).
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: 曹道衡诞辰九十周年 |《曹道衡文集》十卷本出版 ---
URL: http://literature.cass.cn/xjdt/202304/t20230418_5622719.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) Institute of Literature announces the publication of the ten-volume "Cao Daoheng Collected Works" (《曹道衡文集》) on the occasion of the 90th anniversary of Cao Daoheng's birth (1928-2005). Cao Daoheng was a renowned scholar of classical Chinese literature, particularly in the field of medieval (Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties) literature. He graduated from Peking University's Chinese Department in 1952 and served as a researcher and doctoral supervisor at the CASS Institute of Literature for over 50 years. A symposium marking the publication was held at the institute, co-organized by Zhongzhou Ancient Books Publishing House, the CASS Institute of Literature, and the editorial board of Literary Heritage (《文学遗产》) journal, chaired by Institute Director Liu Yuejin, with over sixty attendees including scholars and publishing representatives.

Key points from the article:

1. **Three "perseverances" of Cao Daoheng** (as noted by Liu Yuejin): his adherence to traditional research methods (even during the 1980s-90s), his sustained focus on Han-Wei-Six Dynasties literature in the latter half of his career (eventually concentrating on the "Zhaoming Wenxuan"), and his steadfast commitment to academic principles. He served long-term as president and honorary president of the Chinese Wenxuan Studies Association.

2. **Scholarly breadth and depth**: Cheng Yizhong (editor at Zhonghua Book Company) noted that Cao was known among friends as "Master Cao" (曹夫子) for his exemplary moral character (温良恭俭让). Cao first studied under You Guoen at Peking University focusing on pre-Qin and Han literature, then took on diverse assignments including Qing dynasty literature at the research institute. He eventually became a pioneering figure in medieval Chinese literary studies, assisting Yu Guanying in compiling the medieval section of "History of Chinese Literature." He was one of the rare post-May Fourth scholars who could recite the Four Books and Five Classics from memory.

3. **Family and educational background**: Cao was the great-grandnephew of Qing dynasty ritual studies master Cao Yuanbi. Under his maternal uncle Pan Jingzheng, he studied traditional philology (《说文》《尔雅》) from childhood. He studied history at the Wuxi National College (under Tong Shuye), then entered Peking University in 1950 as a transfer student, studying under You Guoen. He came from the famous Suzhou Pan family (descendants of Pan Shien) on his mother's side; his uncles Pan Jingzheng and Gu Tinglong were renowned bibliophiles and philologists. His great-grandfather Cao Cangzhou was a famous imperial physician, and his great-uncles Cao Fuyuan and Cao Yuanbi were classical scholars and Hanlin Academy editors.

4. **Austere personal life**: Yuan Xingpei (Director of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History) recalled visiting Cao in Beijing Hospital and bringing him chocolate. Cao said, "I love chocolate the most, but I've never been able to bear spending money on it in my whole life." This anecdote illustrates Cao's devotion to scholarship at the expense of personal comfort.

5. **Publication significance** (as analyzed by Xu Zhengying of Renmin University, a student of Cao): Cao is recognized as the preeminent scholar of Northern Dynasties literature, and no researcher of Wei-Jin and Northern-Southern Dynasties literature can bypass his work. Previously his works were scattered across many publishers over decades, with many out of print. The ten-volume collected works fulfill a long-standing expectation of the academic community and Cao's own wish. Xu noted the edition is meticulously proofread and scholarly rigorous, though Cao sometimes cited from memory (he famously said "computers can't beat the human brain" and could recite long passages from texts like the "Zizhi Tongjian" from memory), leading to occasional minor discrepancies in citations which the new edition corrects.

The page also provides the full navigation structure of the CASS Institute of Literature website, including its departments (administrative offices, research sections covering literary theory, Marxist literary theory, ancient literature, classical philology, modern literature, contemporary literature, Taiwan-Hong Kong-Macau literature, folk literature, comparative literature, online literature, and digital humanities), editorial boards (Literary Review, Literary Heritage, and the Chinese Literature Yearbook), affiliated academic societies, and talent training programs.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"First is the perseverance of traditional research methods, especially in the 1980s and 1990s, he did not change. Second is his perseverance in his academic research field, concentrating his later years on the Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties period. Third is his perseverance in academic philosophy." — Liu Yuejin on Cao Daoheng's "three perseverances", "He should be said to be an innovative inheritor of classical studies, and also a new-style philologist who could synthesize argumentation, textual research, and rhetoric." — Cheng Yizhong, "Cao Daoheng is a recognized master of medieval literature research, especially unrivalled in the field of Northern Dynasties literature. Anyone who studies Wei-Jin and Northern and Southern Dynasties literature cannot bypass his research results, and cannot avoid reading his works." — Xu Zhengying, "I love chocolate the most, but in this life I could not bear to spend money on it." — Cao Daoheng, as recalled by Yuan Xingpei
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 曹道衡 ---
URL: http://literature.cass.cn/jgsz/yjs/gdwxyjs/lrzjxz_136009/ded/cdh/202304/t20230427_5625448.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a biographical profile of Cao Daoheng (曹道衡, 1928–2005), a distinguished scholar of Chinese classical literature, hosted on the website of the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS). 

**Biographical Overview:**
- Born in Shanghai in 1928, ancestral home in Suzhou, Jiangsu; original name Wenquan (文铨), courtesy name Daoheng (道衡).
- Graduated from the Chinese Department of Peking University in August 1952.
- Began work at the Central Literary Research Institute in September 1952; transferred to the Peking University Literary Research Institute (which became the CASS Institute of Literature) in June 1953.
- Began publishing works in 1954; appointed Research Fellow in 1985.
- Served as a member of the CASS Institute of Literature Academic Committee, doctoral supervisor at the CASS Graduate School, deputy editor-in-chief of *Literary Review* (《文学评论》), editorial board member of *Literary Heritage* (《文学遗产》), and president/honorary president of the Chinese *Wenxuan* Studies Association.
- Member of the Jiusan Society; received special government allowance from the State Council.
- Research focus: Han-Wei-Six Dynasties literary history, especially Southern and Northern Dynasties literature, with notable achievements including over 100,000 characters of research on the *Zhaoming Wenxuan* (《昭明文选》), systematic studies of Wei-Jin-Southern-Northern Dynasties fiction, literary chronology, and literary geography.
- Retired in December 1988; died in Beijing on May 9, 2005.
- The *Collected Works of Cao Daoheng* (《曹道衡文集》, ten volumes) was published by Zhongzhou Ancient Books Publishing House in 2018.

**Publication List (Partial Highlights):**
- Over 30 major books, including *Collected Essays on Medieval Literary History* (《中古文学史论文集》), *History of Southern and Northern Dynasties Literature* (《南北朝文学史》, co-authored with Shen Yucheng), *Research on Southern Dynasties and Northern Dynasties Literature* (《南朝文学与北朝文学研究》), *Chronology of Southern and Northern Dynasties Literature* (《南北朝文学编年史》, co-authored with Liu Yuejin), *Biography of Xiao Tong* (《萧统评传》, co-authored with Fu Gang), *Annotated Selections of Han-Wei-Six Dynasties Literature*, and *A Biographical Dictionary of Chinese Writers (Pre-Qin, Han, Wei, Jin, Southern-Northern Dynasties Volume)*.
- Over 237 academic papers published from 1954 through the 2000s, covering topics such as the *Wenxuan*, Yuefu poetry, Six Dynasties prose and rhapsody (fu), individual authors (Tao Yuanming, Bao Zhao, Jiang Yan, Yu Xin, Lu Ji, etc.), regional literary culture, and classical textual criticism. Some early essays were published under the pen names Pan Chen (潘辰), Guan Ting (管汀), and Zong Jian (宗健).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
曹道衡（1928—2005），原名文铨，字道衡，祖籍江苏苏州，生于上海。1952年8月毕业于北京大学中文系。研究范围主要集中在汉魏六朝文学史，特别是在南北朝文学研究成就卓著。1988年12月退休。2005年5月9日因病在北京逝世。2018年中州古籍出版社出版《曹道衡文集》（全十卷）。, 担任中国社会科学院文学研究所学术委员会委员，中国社会科学院研究生院博士生导师，《文学评论》副主编，《文学遗产》编委，兼任中国《文选》学研究会会长、名誉会长等职务。九三学社社员。享受国务院政府特殊津贴。, 累计发表十余万字关于《昭明文选》研究的论文，并对魏晋南北朝小说做了较为系统的研究；在作家、作品研究的基础上，对于南北朝文学渊源和文化背景，以及汉魏六朝的文学编年、文学地理分布等情况均做了深入探讨。
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 6: 褚斌杰：坚持中国文学本位立场
_光明日报
_光明网 ---
URL: https://news.gmw.cn/2017-11/20/content_26834627.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from Guangming Daily (光明日报, published November 20, 2017) is a memorial tribute to 褚斌杰 (Chu Binjie, 1933–2006), a distinguished professor of Peking University's Chinese Department and a pioneering scholar in ancient Chinese literature, written by 方铭 (Fang Ming), a professor at Beijing Language and Culture University and president of the Chinese Qu Yuan Society.

**Biographical Background:**
- Born in Beijing in 1933 into a traditional Chinese medicine family; studied at Qilu University, entered Yenching University's Chinese Department in 1950, then transferred to Peking University after the 1952 department merger.
- Before college, was already a recognized poet writing under the pen name 楚子 (Chu Zi).
- Wrote 《白居易评传》 (Biography of Bai Juyi) before age 20 while at Peking University; served as teaching assistant to 游国恩 (You Guo'en) after graduating in 1954.
- Worked at Zhonghua Book Company from 1958 (editing philosophy and literature), participated in punctuating the 24 Histories; returned to Peking University in 1978.
- Died November 1, 2006, at age 73; buried at Beijing Fenghuangshan Cemetery in April 2008.

**Major Academic Contributions:**

1. **Pre-Qin and Han Dynasty Literature History:** His 《中国文学史纲要（先秦、秦汉文学）》 (1983) became a standard teaching text; he also served as chief editor of 《先秦文学史》 (Pre-Qin Literary History, People's Literature Publishing House, 1998, ~400,000 characters), part of the ten-volume Chinese literary history compiled by the CASS Institute of Literature. This webpage is a biographical profile of Yu Guanying (余冠英, 1906–1995), a prominent Chinese classical literature scholar, hosted on the official website of the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS). The page is part of the institute's section on former group leaders and department directors of the Ancient Literature Research Office.

Key biographical details:
- Born in 1906 in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province. Entered Jiangsu Provincial No. 8 Middle School (now Yangzhou Middle School) in 1922.
- Enrolled at Tsinghua University's History Department in 1926, later transferring to the Chinese Literature Department. Graduated in 1931 and remained to teach at the university.
- During the War of Resistance Against Japan, served as Associate Professor and then Professor at Southwest Associated University, teaching Chinese literary history, essay writing, and selected works of various dynasties. Also served as chief editor of the National Chinese Monthly (《国文月刊》).
- Returned to Tsinghua in autumn 1946 as Professor of Chinese Literature, teaching Chinese literary history and Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties poetry.
- In 1953, transferred to the Peking University Institute of Literature (predecessor of today's CASS Institute of Literature), where he served as the main leader of the Ancient Literature Group (Department) from 1953 to 1979.
- Held additional positions including Deputy Director of the Institute, Advisor, Director of the Academic Committee, and chief editor of the journal Literary Heritage (《文学遗产》).
- Served as Deputy to the Third National People's Congress, member of the Fifth and Sixth National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), member of the All-China Federation of Literary and Art Circles, council member of the Chinese Writers Association, member of International PEN, and advisor to the National Ancient Book Collation and Publication Planning Group.

Major published works include: 《汉魏六朝诗论丛》(Collected Essays on Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poetry), 《古代文学杂论》(Miscellaneous Essays on Ancient Literature), 《诗经选》(Selected Poems of the Book of Songs), 《诗经选译》(Selected Translations of the Book of Songs), 《乐府诗选》(Selected Yuefu Poems), 《汉魏六朝诗选》(Selected Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poems), and 《三曹诗选》(Selected Poems of the Three Caos).

The page also lists links to his four representative works and is accompanied by navigation menus showing the institute's structure, including research departments, editorial boards, academic societies, and research centers. The page was published on 2023-04-26.

# 余冠英

播报[讨论](https://baike.baidu.com/planet/talk?lemmaId=2936292&fromModule=lemma_right-issue-btn)[上传视频](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BD%99%E5%86%A0%E8%8B%B1/2936292)

中国古典文学专家

[](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BD%99%E5%86%A0%E8%8B%B1/2936292)

余冠英（1906年5月16日—1995年9月2日），字绍生，笔名灌婴，江苏松江（今属上海）人。中国古典文学专家，[中国民主同盟](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%B0%91%E4%B8%BB%E5%90%8C%E7%9B%9F/457730?fromModule=lemma_inlink)盟员 [2]。

1926年考入[清华大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B8%85%E5%8D%8E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/111764?fromModule=lemma_inlink)历史系，后转中国文学系，1931年毕业 [3]。历任清华大学、[西南联合大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%A5%BF%E5%8D%97%E8%81%94%E5%90%88%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/5622202?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教授，1952年任中国科学院文学研究所二级研究员，后任副所长、《[文学遗产](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E9%81%97%E4%BA%A7/23261?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》主编 [1] [4]。曾任[中国作家协会](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E4%BD%9C%E5%AE%B6%E5%8D%8F%E4%BC%9A/2049478?fromModule=lemma_inlink)理事，第三届全国人大代表，第五、六届全国政协委员，并担任国家古籍整理出版规划小组顾问。参与编写《[中国文学史](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E5%8F%B2/1343102?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《[唐诗选](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%94%90%E8%AF%97%E9%80%89/9624232?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》，主编《[诗经选](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%AF%97%E7%BB%8F%E9%80%89/1380958?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《[汉魏六朝诗选](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B1%89%E9%AD%8F%E5%85%AD%E6%9C%9D%E8%AF%97%E9%80%89/1494057?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》等著作 [4-5]。早年就读江苏省立第八中学，任扬州学生联合会首任会长，参与[五卅运动](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BA%94%E5%8D%85%E8%BF%90%E5%8A%A8/291952?fromModule=lemma_inlink)。抗战期间编辑《[国文月刊](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E6%9C%88%E5%88%8A/10406396?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》，1948年联名签署《抗议美国扶日政策并拒绝领取美援面粉宣言》 [3] [5]。研究方向集中于先秦至汉魏六朝诗歌，校注整理《[乐府诗选](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B9%90%E5%BA%9C%E8%AF%97%E9%80%89/8654201?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《[三曹诗选](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%89%E6%9B%B9%E8%AF%97%E9%80%89/1375730?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》等文献 [3] [6]。

1995年9月2日在北京逝世 [1-2]。

## 人物经历

播报

编辑

### 人物家世

1906年5月16日出生于江苏松江， [2]父亲是清季武职人员，母亲虽没学过太多的文化，但[会读书](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BC%9A%E8%AF%BB%E4%B9%A6/45845?fromModule=lemma_inlink)绘画。冠英之上的两个姐姐都过早夭折，所以这个男儿的出生对家庭来说就尤为金贵。小名“松寿”是望他健康长寿，大名“冠英”就是切盼他日后成为“群英之冠”。父母把全部希望都寄托在小冠英身上，所以从3岁起，就用方块卡片教他识字。6岁时全家迁至[扬州](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%89%AC%E5%B7%9E/6255?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，并在此生活了20年，少小的事物件件都给他留下了难以磨灭的印象。

### 学生时代

扬州旖旎的风光和浓郁的崇尚文化的气息，陶冶了他的性情，滋养了他的[文学素养](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E7%B4%A0%E5%85%BB/8760696?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，弥留之际，他念念不忘的还是扬州那让人眷恋的绿杨情。冠英11岁那年，父亲辞世，家道中落，但母亲仍十分重视冠英的学习，凡是冠英想买的书，母亲尽量满足他。扬州有两家冠英常去的书店，母亲给了他一个折子，可先取书记账，年底一并付钱。冠英13岁考入高等小学，15岁考入江苏省立第八中学（后改为[扬州中学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%89%AC%E5%B7%9E%E4%B8%AD%E5%AD%A6/2657030?fromModule=lemma_inlink)）。

20世纪20年代是中国革命风起云涌的时代，冠英也开始阅读进步书刊，接触革命思想，交结进步的同学朋友。到“五卅”运动爆发时，扬州爱国学生也奋起支援，余冠英便成了新成立的扬州学生联合会的第一任会长。他组织学生游行，邀请进步人士到学校讲演，其中，最有名的就是共产党员恽代英。

### 文学创作

[![Image 3](https://bkimg.cdn.bcebos.com/smart/8367d1fcedb873c7b801a053-bkimg-process,v_1,rw_252,rh_252,maxl_504?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)](https://baike.baidu.com/pic/%E4%BD%99%E5%86%A0%E8%8B%B1/2936292/0/8367d1fcedb873c7b801a053?fr=lemma&fromModule=lemma_content-image "于冠英推荐古代民歌")于冠英推荐古代民歌

1926年，余冠英以优异的成绩考入[清华大学历史系](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B8%85%E5%8D%8E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6%E5%8E%86%E5%8F%B2%E7%B3%BB/5047017?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，后转入[中国文学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6/178050?fromModule=lemma_inlink)系。他主修中国[古典诗歌](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8F%A4%E5%85%B8%E8%AF%97%E6%AD%8C/7530156?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，同时喜欢创作新诗。四年级时，冠英在同学中组织了“唧唧诗社”，每作一诗，社友们都要评头品足，在相互切磋之中体味诗之欢乐。

除诗之外，冠英的小品、散文、小说也很出色。他用汉朝大将“[灌婴](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%81%8C%E5%A9%B4/974832?fromModule=lemma_inlink)”之谐音为笔名，大多发表在《[清华周刊](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B8%85%E5%8D%8E%E5%91%A8%E5%88%8A/0?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》及《中国文学会刊》上。这些文章有的被[人民文学出版社](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E5%87%BA%E7%89%88%E7%A4%BE/2856101?fromModule=lemma_inlink)编的《当代散文精华》收入，有的被[朱自清](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9C%B1%E8%87%AA%E6%B8%85/0?fromModule=lemma_inlink)编的《[中国新文学大系](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%B0%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E5%A4%A7%E7%B3%BB/2223510?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》收入。同时代的[吴组缃](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%B4%E7%BB%84%E7%BC%83/5760549?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教授在1931年写的《清华的文风》一文中，曾高度评价了余冠英当时的作品，称余冠英是清华的代表作家，代表了清华的文风。在抗战的艰苦岁月中，冠英编辑影响很大的《[国文月刊](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E6%9C%88%E5%88%8A/10406396?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》到40期。

1938年5月，由清华、北大、[南开](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8D%97%E5%BC%80/9502905?fromModule=lemma_inlink)组成的长沙临时大学改名[西南联合大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%A5%BF%E5%8D%97%E8%81%94%E5%90%88%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/5622202?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，暑假后，又从[蒙自](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%92%99%E8%87%AA/4537818?fromModule=lemma_inlink)迁往[昆明](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%98%86%E6%98%8E/161012?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，由[朱自清](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9C%B1%E8%87%AA%E6%B8%85/0?fromModule=lemma_inlink)主持中文系。冠英得知后，带家小由上海坐船到[越南](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%B6%8A%E5%8D%97/155278?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，再由[滇越铁路](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%BB%87%E8%B6%8A%E9%93%81%E8%B7%AF/11038435?fromModule=lemma_inlink)赶往昆明，出任联大师范学院讲师，后又擢升副教授、教授。

1945年后，震惊全国的“一二·一”惨案，[李公朴](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%AC%E6%9C%B4/1341724?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[闻一多](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%97%BB%E4%B8%80%E5%A4%9A/148101?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教授被害案相继发生，[法西斯](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B3%95%E8%A5%BF%E6%96%AF/100054?fromModule=lemma_inlink)的独裁行径使冠英思想受到很大震动。清华等校广大师生多次开展反内战、反独裁、反饥饿斗争，在激烈的历史命运的抉择中，余冠英坚决地站在了人民一边。1948年6月18日，他与朱自清、[金岳霖](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%87%91%E5%B2%B3%E9%9C%96/119632?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[吴晗](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%B4%E6%99%97/446341?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[陈梦家](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%99%88%E6%A2%A6%E5%AE%B6/119379?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、钱伟长、[朱德熙](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BE%B7%E7%86%99/1180652?fromModule=lemma_inlink)等毅然在著名的百十师长严正声明，即《抗议美国扶日政策并拒绝领取美援面粉宣言》上签了名。

### 建国后

[1952年院系调整](https://baike.baidu.com/item/1952%E5%B9%B4%E9%99%A2%E7%B3%BB%E8%B0%83%E6%95%B4/1224948?fromModule=lemma_inlink)后，余冠英为北京大学文学研究所的研究员兼[古代文学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8F%A4%E4%BB%A3%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6/3195418?fromModule=lemma_inlink)研究组的组长。1955年文研所划归中国科学院，余冠英成为人大代表、全国政协委员、中国作协理事、[中国文联](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E8%81%94/2051297?fromModule=lemma_inlink)委员、[国际笔会](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9B%BD%E9%99%85%E7%AC%94%E4%BC%9A/5873030?fromModule=lemma_inlink)会员。

### 晚年

’“文化大革命”结束后，成立中国社会科学院，余冠英改任社科院文学研究所的副所长兼《[文学遗产](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E9%81%97%E4%BA%A7/23261?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》杂志主编。1985年，79岁的余冠英[退居二线](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%80%80%E5%B1%85%E4%BA%8C%E7%BA%BF/9570419?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，但仍任文学所顾问和[学术委员会](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%AD%A6%E6%9C%AF%E5%A7%94%E5%91%98%E4%BC%9A/4040736?fromModule=lemma_inlink)名誉主任及[博士生导师](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8D%9A%E5%A3%AB%E7%94%9F%E5%AF%BC%E5%B8%88/11051132?fromModule=lemma_inlink)。1995年9月2日，余冠英先生因病去世。

## 主要成就

播报

编辑

余冠英是著名的文学史家，其学术工作涵盖文学史编纂、诗歌选注与普及、学术研究及编辑工作等多个方面 [10] [13-14]。

### 文学史编纂与学术组织

余冠英主持编写了《中国文学史》（三卷本），1962年由人民文学出版社印行，担任全书总负责人及上古至隋部分主编 [10] [13]。该著作是古典文学研究领域中的重要成果 [7] [14] [17]。

### 诗歌选注与经典普及

余冠英主持编选的《唐诗选》历时十八年，是唐诗选本之一 [7] [13] [17]。其个人选注的《诗经选》《乐府诗选》《三曹诗选》《汉魏六朝诗选》等，成为古典文学普及的经典读本 [14]。《乐府诗选》是解放后较早出版的古代文学作品选读本之一 [17]，这些读本在社会上产生了广泛影响 [21]。

### 学术研究与翻译

余冠英的学术研究强调[中国文学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6/178050?fromModule=lemma_inlink)的“现实主义精神”和“[人民性](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BA%BA%E6%B0%91%E6%80%A7/3885520?fromModule=lemma_inlink)” [10]，在汉魏六朝诗歌研究领域成就卓著，著有《[汉魏六朝诗论丛](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B1%89%E9%AD%8F%E5%85%AD%E6%9C%9D%E8%AF%97%E8%AE%BA%E4%B8%9B/10540672?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《[古代文学杂论](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8F%A4%E4%BB%A3%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E6%9D%82%E8%AE%BA/57342536?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》等 [13-14]。余冠英将《[诗经](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%AF%97%E7%BB%8F/168138?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》译为白话文，其翻译受到认可 [14-15]。

### 社会职务与荣誉

余冠英历任第三届全国人大代表，第五、六届全国政协委员，全国文联委员，[中国作家协会](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E4%BD%9C%E5%AE%B6%E5%8D%8F%E4%BC%9A/2049478?fromModule=lemma_inlink)理事，[国际笔会](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9B%BD%E9%99%85%E7%AC%94%E4%BC%9A/5873030?fromModule=lemma_inlink)会员等社会职务 [8]。

### 兴趣爱好

余冠英爱吃零食，有时会自己出门购买雪糕、饼干等零食 [13]。

### 文章

《清华不是个读书的好地方》

余冠英

我曾问人：清华大学和清华园这两个名字将来谁更出风头？有人说：照眼前的事实看来，风头是属于后者的较多。这话大概没有什么错罢？你说：可不是嘛！大门口的“清华园”三个字是皇皇石刻而且巍巍居中，“[国立清华大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9B%BD%E7%AB%8B%E6%B8%85%E5%8D%8E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/3075325?fromModule=lemma_inlink)”六个字便是写在木头牌上而且只好一旁侍立呢。我说：决不止此！

清华的来宾往往是踵趾相接的。假如我说这些人之中被清华园的草、木、泉、石所吸引的一定比为了看清华大学的图书、仪器、标本、机械而来的多五十倍，该没有人反对罢？那末，无怪其然你一写信约朋友来玩，多半说“请来园子里逛逛罢”，而很少用“请到敝校参观参观”。清华原是“园”的空气多于“大学”的空气啊。

这样便可以转到正题了，“清华不是读书的好地方”理由不和“春天不是读书天”一般简单吗？春天有比读书更有趣的事让你做，清华有比读书更有趣的事叫你不得不做。

最可怪的，没有一个外人不对清华人赞叹：“贵校的读书环境真好！”而每一个清华人，纵然是最谦虚的你，也决不曾摇头否认。这是什么意思？你当真相信清华最适于读书么？我不信你比我缺少那些经验，随便举一件便可以做这句话的反证。

远的不用说，就以最近这两个礼拜说罢，你如曾有一次整个钟头耐心耐意地坐在教室里笔记，那才是奇迹呢！你有眼看得见黑板上的[白字](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%99%BD%E5%AD%97/6261884?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，当然也有眼看得见窗外那些轻摇慢舞的[鹅黄](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%B9%85%E9%BB%84/3420356?fromModule=lemma_inlink)细柳，那些笑靥迎人的[碧桃](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%A2%A7%E6%A1%83/502277?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，那些像有[胭脂](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%83%AD%E8%84%82/22962?fromModule=lemma_inlink)要滴下枝来的朱梅，那些火似的、像有一种要扑到你身上来的热情的不知名的花，那些，那些……迷人的东西，真的没有把你的心从a、b、c、d中勾走么？就算你是[道学家](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%81%93%E5%AD%A6%E5%AE%B6/6965697?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，有“目不窥园”的修养，还有[玫瑰](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%8E%AB%E7%91%B0/63206?fromModule=lemma_inlink)呢，丁香呢，它们会放香！熏风从那里钻进窗户，又在你鼻端打了一个回旋，你心不动么？就算你受了[春寒](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%98%A5%E5%AF%92/8404123?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，鼻子不通，还有[云雀](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BA%91%E9%9B%80/67054?fromModule=lemma_inlink)呢，[杜鹃](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9D%9C%E9%B9%83/3142533?fromModule=lemma_inlink)呢，远远地唱起来了，蜜蜂又团在窗外哼，甚至一双燕子索性坐在窗槛上说起情话来了，你又待怎样防御呢？总之，一切都引得你的心往外飞，这时的心，固然教授们的什么论，什么史，什么法，什么问题，什么公式抓它不住，便是你书中的[颜如玉](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%A2%9C%E5%A6%82%E7%8E%89/3922?fromModule=lemma_inlink)也照样不行。

再切实一点举例罢，你在三院教室，即使正听着法国[革命史](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%9D%A9%E5%91%BD%E5%8F%B2/23118808?fromModule=lemma_inlink)这样热闹的演讲，你也会忽然想到钓鱼的事情。因为你看见窗外的[垂柳](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9E%82%E6%9F%B3/3935180?fromModule=lemma_inlink)了，你自然会联想到正被那柔丝拂着的一河春水，和那正在水面吹沫的游鱼，也许那树杈[上正](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%8A%E6%AD%A3/10946285?fromModule=lemma_inlink)搁着一根[钓竿](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%92%93%E7%AB%BF/7640921?fromModule=lemma_inlink)呢。

相类的事多着呢，譬如你在科学馆做化学实习，虽然一分钟的不当心也会发生烧炸瓶子的危险，你竟然在那里想到，今天该约你的玛丽，或是莎菲，或是兰妹，或是蕙妹散步去了，这一念怎会闯进来的？因为只要你眼睛向窗外瞥一下，你不会看不见古月堂前那可爱的树木和那曲折通幽的小径哟。

决不止此！你在图书馆为了听见[啄木鸟](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%95%84%E6%9C%A8%E9%B8%9F/38385?fromModule=lemma_inlink)朗朗的鼓声而悠然掩卷的次数一定不在少，至于在生物馆听到稻田里[水禽](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B0%B4%E7%A6%BD/2346956?fromModule=lemma_inlink)相唤而神游研究室之外的事，更不用数计了。

决不止此！你从新大楼挟着书走出来，有时自会觉得心里一动：怎么啦？原来那体育馆遮不住的一角青山蓦然跳到你的眼里来了。

平时犹可，倘在宿雨初晴，或是夕阳将下，你的心会因而怦怦地跳个不住。因为那平时只是轻描淡写的青山，这时会紫得叫你感到重量，浓得像要溢出它的轮廓；平时是远远的，缥缈的，平面的，这时却堆起来了，逼近了。于是你惊得喘了一口气，于是你忘了本来要去的地方，于是你拔步向西飞跑，越过草地，爬上[土山](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9C%9F%E5%B1%B1/84760?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，于是山呀，树呀，云呀，浮图呀，都一涌来到你的眼里。这时[燕京大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%87%95%E4%BA%AC%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/198383?fromModule=lemma_inlink)的塔，万寿山的琳宫宇，甚至[圆明园](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%9C%86%E6%98%8E%E5%9B%AD/9328?fromModule=lemma_inlink)的断垣残柱，一切都富于色彩，一切都放射光辉，一切都给你幻想，这幻想竟和这镶金镀紫的云块一般变幻奇丽。于是你呆了，直到树迷山暝，归巢的乱鸦将你唤醒，你才跄踉下山，恍恍惚惚地向灯火辉煌的食堂走去，也许直等一碗[烩三鲜](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%83%A9%E4%B8%89%E9%B2%9C/8116132?fromModule=lemma_inlink)下肚之后你才想起今天缺了一堂什么课或是缺席一次什么练习了。

你点头笑了，这就够了，我想我不用再举你为了西园捉蛙，荷塘摘[莲蓬](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%8E%B2%E8%93%AC/150245?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，西园塑雪狮或是大礼堂晒太阳一类傻事而费去你用功的大好光阴的例了。

但是你不要脸红，这并不怪你的心野，只怪自然中间有些东西太迷人了，而清华偏又具备了这样多。就如极平常的马路罢，在清华偏偏高高地罩着翠柳的凉阴，并且还满布槐花的香气，散步一类的事，你自然会觉得是难以遏制的欲望了。说到马路，不过是举其最平常、最微末的，你要我谈谈清华的景物吗？清华有的是回环层叠的土山，山里有的是苍松、老桧、藤、萝、竹、石，以及人工设置的小亭和长椅，爱远眺的可以高处攀登，爱幽僻的可以深处追寻，[各适其适](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%84%E9%80%82%E5%85%B6%E9%80%82/13023254?fromModule=lemma_inlink)。清华也有四通八达的水。说到水，最富丽的是三面河环一面巨厦的[河池](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B2%B3%E6%B1%A0/742924?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，富于野趣的就该数西园长着芦苇的水田了。

燕大的湖虽然有人艳羡不止，我终以为那样大泥塘似的，正落了北平的许多“海”的陈套，我宁可取清华园里横贯东西的校河。好处在河身修长而且微有曲折，两岸的树丰茂可喜，河上几座桥都很好。在桥上，近可以看鱼，远可以看迷离的树影。可惜就是来源不大，所以下游不得不用一个闸，因而水流很缓，虽然有平静之美，终嫌缺少活泼的气象。因此那被挤到墙外，环园而流的小溪就更可爱了。

说到那小溪，又是你最熟悉的去处了，那里的淙淙水声往往费你整个下午去坐听。你有时嫌乡村姑嫂[捣衣](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%8D%A3%E8%A1%A3/1622451?fromModule=lemma_inlink)的聒扰，便不在西园的门外石上坐，而走到极东的一端来，或者顺着溪流拐一个弯，找到只剩你一个人的幽静地方，随处有光洁可坐的石头，有满身凉翠的树荫，有和流泉相应的蝉吟，于是你用柳条戏弄戏弄聚水水曲的小鱼，或投一个石子在那一个个碗大的小漩涡里，或伸一只脚在石块激成半尺高的小瀑布之下，你那时或许有出世之想了。

打住罢，假如再谈到清华的“花事”，一定更引起你的烦恼，我知道你正为了园里的[丁香花](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%81%E9%A6%99%E8%8A%B1/1738?fromModule=lemma_inlink)盛开而满处乱钻，总找不到一个地方可以躲这香气，急得想[找医生](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%89%BE%E5%8C%BB%E7%94%9F/8230172?fromModule=lemma_inlink)给你的鼻子动手术呢。

言归正传，清华虽是一个大学，而同时又是一个园，所以环境并不利于读书，这是我的观察。不过我又疑惑了，据我所知，清华的毕业生读书的成绩正被人家评为“不错”呢，这又当作何解释？呵，我懂了！这叫做“地灵人杰”，据说山水明秀的地方，[灵气所钟](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%81%B5%E6%B0%94%E6%89%80%E9%92%9F/10701683?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，人物自然也会明秀，所以“水木清华”的清华园，人物也一样非常之“清华”了。然则我这个题目根本就是一句废话，该由我自动收回，那么“谢罪”！

1931年6月1日

This is a Baidu Baike (Chinese encyclopedia) biographical entry for 余冠英 (Yu Guanying, 1906-1995), a renowned Chinese classical literature scholar.

**Basic Information:**
- Born May 16, 1906 in Jiangsu Songjiang (now part of Shanghai); died September 2, 1995 in Beijing
- Also known by aliases 绍生 (Shaosheng) and pen name 灌婴 (Guanying, a homophone of a Han dynasty general)
- Member of the Chinese Democratic League
- Graduated from Tsinghua University (enrolled 1926 in History, transferred to Chinese Literature, graduated 1931)

**Career Timeline:**
- 1926: Admitted to Tsinghua University
- 1931: Graduated from Tsinghua University Chinese Literature Department
- Served as professor at Tsinghua University and Southwest Associated University (西南联合大学)
- 1938: Moved to Kunming to join Southwest Associated University, initially as lecturer at the Normal College, later promoted to associate professor and full professor
- 1952: Became a Level 2 Researcher at the Chinese Academy of Sciences Literature Research Institute, later deputy director
- Served as chief editor of the journal 《文学遗产》 (Literary Heritage)
- Held positions including: 3rd NPC deputy, 5th-6th CPPCC National Committee member, China Writers Association council member, China Federation of Literary and Art Circles committee member, PEN International member, and advisor to the National Ancient Books Collation and Publishing Planning Group
- 1985: Retired from frontline work at age 79 but continued as consultant and honorary director of the Academic Committee and doctoral supervisor
- 1995: Passed away on September 2 in Beijing

**Key Achievements:**
- Led the compilation of 《中国文学史》(History of Chinese Literature, 3 volumes), published 1962 by People's Literature Publishing House
- Chief editor of 《唐诗选》(Selected Tang Poems), a selection project spanning 18 years
- Personally selected and annotated classic works including 《诗经选》(Selected Book of Songs), 《乐府诗选》(Selected Yuefu Poems), 《三曹诗选》(Selected Poems of the Three Caos), and 《汉魏六朝诗选》(Selected Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poems)
- Translated the Book of Songs (《诗经》) into vernacular Chinese
- Published academic works including 《汉魏六朝诗论丛》 and 《古代文学杂论》
- Research focused on pre-Qin to Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties poetry, emphasizing "realism" and "people-oriented" qualities in Chinese literature

**Early Life and Activism:**
- Father was a Qing dynasty military official; mother could read and paint
- Family moved to Yangzhou when he was 6, living there for 20 years
- Father died when he was 11; mother supported his book-buying habit
- At 15, entered Jiangsu Provincial No. 8 Middle School (later Yangzhou Middle School)
- During the May 30th Movement (五卅运动), served as first president of the Yangzhou Student Union, organizing student parades and inviting progressive speakers including communist revolutionary Yun Daiying (恽代英)
- During the war, edited the influential journal 《国文月刊》(National Chinese Monthly) through its 40th issue
- On June 18, 1948, signed the famous declaration "Protesting US Policy of Supporting Japan and Refusing American Aid Flour" (《抗议美国扶日政策并拒绝领取美援面粉宣言》) alongside Zhu Ziqing, Jin Yuelin, Wu Han, and others

**Notable Works List (Selected):**
- 乐府诗选注 (1953), 祖国十二诗人 (1955), 三曹诗选 (1956), 汉魏六朝诗论丛 (1956), 诗经选 (1956), 汉魏六朝诗选 (1958), 中国文学史 3-vol (1962), 诗经选译 (1985), 古代文学杂论 (1987), 中国古代山水诗鉴赏辞典 (1989), 古诗精选 (1992), 乐府诗集点校 (1979), among others

**Additional Details:**
- In his student years, organized the "唧唧诗社" (Jiji Poetry Society) at Tsinghua
- His essays and prose were published in 《清华周刊》 and 《中国文学会刊》; some works were collected by People's Literature Publishing House's 《当代散文精华》 and Zhu Ziqing's 《中国新文学大系》
- Wu Zuxiang praised him in 1931 as a representative writer embodying Tsinghua's literary style
- Personal quirk: enjoyed eating snacks like ice cream and cookies
- The page also includes the full text of his essay "清华不是个读书的好地方" (Tsinghua Is Not a Good Place to Study), written June 1, 1931, humorously arguing that Tsinghua's beautiful campus environment distracts students from studying
args.key_excerpts: "余冠英（1906年5月16日—1995年9月2日），字绍生，笔名灌婴，江苏松江（今属上海）人。中国古典文学专家，中国民主同盟盟员。"
