--- SOURCE 10: 有博有淡，这样的钱钟书才立体-中央纪委网站 ---
URL: https://m.ccdi.gov.cn/content/c1/58/31350.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from 学习时报 (Study Times) presents a biographical tribute to Qian Zhongshu (钱钟书), a towering figure of modern Chinese culture and literature who combined the roles of scholar and writer. The piece is organized into two main sections: "博学鸿儒" (Erudite Scholar) and "淡泊人生" (Detached Life).

**Education and Early Life:** Born in Wuxi to a distinguished family tracing back to Wu-Yue King Qian Liu of the Five Dynasties period, Qian's father Qian Jibo was a famous modern historian and Tsinghua University professor. His name "Zhongshu" (lover of books) came from a Zhou-era custom ritual where he picked up a book. His knowledge foundation came from three sources: missionary school education (Western learning), family education (Chinese classics), and self-study. In 1929, he entered Tsinghua University's Foreign Languages Department and was hailed as the top of the "Three Talents of Tsinghua" (alongside archaeologist Xia Nai and historian Wu Han).

**Overseas Study:** In autumn 1935, Qian won a British Boxer Indemnity scholarship and went to Oxford University with his wife Yang Jiang (杨绛), studying there until 1937. They then studied French literature at the University of Paris research institute, deepening his understanding of European cultures and languages.

**Academic Career:** In summer 1938, Tsinghua appointed him professor of Western Languages and Literature. His early major works include the essay collection "Written on the Margin of Life" (写在人生边上, 1941), the short story collection "Human, Beast, Ghost" (人·兽·鬼, 1946), his famous novel "Fortress Besieged" (围城, 1947), and the theoretical work "On the Art of Poetry" (谈艺录, 1948). He later published "Selected Poems of the Song Dynasty" (宋诗选注, 1958). His magnum opus, "Guan Zhui Bian" (管锥篇, meaning "Glimpses through a Tube and Pointings at the Earth"), was published in four volumes in 1979 after long preparation. This massive work comprises 781 reading notes across 10 volumes, written in elegant classical Chinese, commenting on ten classical Chinese texts including the Zhou Yi, Book of Songs, Zuo Zhuan, and Records of the Grand Historian. It covers philosophy, religion, history, philology, rhetoric, cultural anthropology, psychoanalysis, comparative culture and poetics, citing nearly 10,000 works by over 4,000 authors (including over 1,000 Western scholars), in Chinese, English, French, German, Italian, and Latin.

**Personal Character:** Qian remained remarkably detached from fame despite his rising popularity, especially after the 1990 CCTV television adaptation of "Fortress Besieged" made him an icon. He famously told a British woman seeking an audience: "If you eat an egg and find it tasty, why need you meet the hen that laid it?" He opposed the growing "Qian Xue" (Qian studies) movement, telling writer Shu Zhan: "Mount Kunlun is crushing me to death." In a letter to Professor Zheng Chaozong of Xiamen University (who pioneered Qian studies), he wrote that true scholarship is "the business of a few plain-hearted people deliberating in a desolate cottage, and the popular learning of the marketplace inevitably becomes vulgar learning." He resisted all forms of fame-chasing, sycophancy, and accommodation to worldly trends, embodying the scholar's spirit of quiet dedication.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"大抵学问是荒江（野）老屋中二三素心人商量培养之事，朝市之显学必成俗学。" (True scholarship is the business of a few plain-hearted people deliberating in a desolate cottage; the popular learning of the marketplace inevitably becomes vulgar learning.) — Qian Zhongshu's letter to Professor Zheng Chaozong, "假如你吃了一个鸡蛋觉得不错，又何必要认识那下蛋的母鸡呢？" (If you eat an egg and find it tasty, why need you meet the hen that laid it?) — Qian Zhongshu's reply to a British woman requesting a visit, "昆仑山快把我压死了。" (Mount Kunlun is crushing me to death.) — Qian Zhongshu's protest to writer Shu Zhan about the "Qian Xue" movement, "福过灾生，誉过谤至。" (Blessings overflowing breed disaster; praise overflowing invites slander.), "大学问家的学问，跟他的整个性情陶熔为一片" (The scholarship of a great scholar is fused with his entire temperament.)

--- SOURCE 1: 北京大学校史馆 ---
URL: https://www.xsg.pku.edu.cn/details/1595.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the Peking University (北京大学) History Museum website is a biographical article titled "北大的才女——冯沅君（北大第一位女研究生）" (A Talented Woman of Peking University — Feng Yuanjun, the First Female Graduate Student of Peking University), published on 2020-03-30 and written by 谢宁.

**Overview:** Feng Yuanjun (冯沅君, 1900-1974), originally named Feng Shulan, was a renowned literary historian, drama historian, and writer from Tanghe, Henan Province. She was among the first influential female writers of post-May Fourth Movement new literature, ranked alongside celebrated writers Bing Xin (冰心) and Lu Yin (庐隐). She graduated from Beijing Women's Higher Normal School in 1922, became Peking University's first female graduate student at the Institute of National Studies in 1925, and earned a PhD in literature from the University of Paris in 1935. She taught at Jinling Women's University, Fudan University, Sun Yat-sen University, Wuhan University, and Shandong University, where she later became vice president.

**Key biographical events (chronological):**
- **1900 (Sept 4):** Born in Qiyi Town, Tanghe County, Henan, into a wealthy official family. Her grandfather Feng Yuwen was a poet; her father Feng Taiyi was a Qing Dynasty jinshi who served under Governor-General Zhang Zhidong and later became magistrate of Chongyang County, Hubei.
- **Early education:** Showed exceptional literary talent from age 5, memorizing Tang poems while listening to her brothers' lessons. Her mother Wu Qingzhi was supportive of her education.
- **1917:** Persuaded her mother to let her attend Beijing Women's Higher Normal School, famously declaring she would give up her dowry money for tuition. She passed the entrance exam (a single composition test) easily.
- **May Fourth Movement (1919):** Actively participated, famously leading students to smash a lock on the school gate to protest the principal's restrictions, and drafted a petition to President Xu Shichang on behalf of 15 women's schools. She also adapted "孔雀东南飞" (Peacock Flying Southeast) into a play and performed the role of the villainous mother-in-law.
- **1922:** Graduated and enrolled at Peking University's Institute of National Studies as its first female graduate student.
- **1923-1926:** Published short stories under the pen name "淦女士" including 《隔绝》、《隔绝之后》、《慈母》、《旅行》, later collected as 《卷葹》(Juanshi). These works dealt with women's pursuit of marriage freedom and individual liberty. Lu Xun praised her work and included 《卷葹》 in his "乌合丛书" (Motley Collection), noting that "卷葹" is a small grass that survives even when its heart is pulled out.
- **1924-1926:** Became a contributor to 《语丝》 magazine, later changing her pen name to "沅君" (derived from Qu Yuan's "Nine Songs"). Her stories included 《劫灰》、《贞妇》、《缘法》.
- **1926:** Met her future husband Lu Kanru (陆侃如), a fellow classical literature scholar from Peking University, three years her junior.
- **1931:** Published 《中国诗史》(History of Chinese Poetry) with her husband Lu Kanru, praised as "取材审慎，要言不烦" (carefully selected material, concise and to the point) — the only poetry history work of its time. Lu Xun recommended it alongside works by major scholars.
- **1932:** Traveled to France with her husband, both enrolling in the doctoral program at the University of Paris. They joined the anti-war, anti-fascist alliance organized by Henri Barbusse.
- **1935:** Earned her doctorate from the University of Paris and returned to China. Taught at Yenching University (husband) and Hebei Women's Normal School.
- **1937:** Composed poems protesting the Marco Polo Bridge Incident (July 7 Incident) and Japan's invasion.
- **1938-1945:** Wartime years of displacement across Yunnan, Guangdong, Sichuan. Published collections 《四余诗稿》、《四余词稿》、《四余续稿》. In 1942, organized the "中华文艺界抗敌协会" (China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Resistance Association) Sichuan Northern Branch in Santai with her husband at the request of Lao She. Wrote important academic works 《古剧说汇》、《古优解》 during this period.
- **Post-war:** Taught at Shandong University in Qingdao from 1947.
- **Post-1949:** Served as professor, then vice president of Shandong University (appointed 1963). Was elected to the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd National People's Congresses. Co-authored (with Lu Kanru) the revised 《中国文学简史》, translated into English and Czech, which Mao Zedong kept on his desk as a favorite book.
- **1957:** Her husband was labeled a "rightist" (右派). When pressured to denounce him, she famously replied: "我大半辈子与'老虎'同寝共枕，竟无察觉，是得了神经麻痹症吧？" ("I've slept with a 'tiger' for most of my life without noticing — am I suffering from nerve paralysis?")
- **1958:** Herself became a target of the "white flag" campaign, forced to crush ore on Qianfo Mountain.
- **Cultural Revolution:** Persecuted as a "reactionary academic authority," forced to clean corridors and toilets, fell from a platform during a struggle session.
- **1974 (June 17):** Died of rectal cancer. Her final act was giving an impromptu lecture to hospital staff and patients just days before her death.

**Academic philosophy:** Her famous motto was "做学问，功夫要死，心眼要活" (In scholarship, one must work with stubborn effort but keep an agile mind). She left behind millions of characters of reading notes, and her three papers on ancient performers (《古优解》 etc.) cited over 100 Chinese and foreign sources.

**Legacy and philanthropy:** Despite being a top-tier (一级) professor with high income, she lived extremely frugally. She donated 40 silver dollars to support a persecuted philosopher's family pre-1949, purchased 10,000 yuan of government bonds in the early PRC period, and planned to leave her savings as an academic scholarship for the nation. Her husband's will donated their entire book collection and savings to Shandong University. Her motto was "生前为民族，身后为国家" (serve the nation in life, give to the nation in death).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"在新旧交替的时期与其作已经宣告破产的礼法的降服者，不如作方生的主义真理的牺牲者。" (From her novel — "In this transitional era, it is better to be a sacrifice for a newborn truth than to submit to an already bankrupt moral code."), "身命可以牺牲，意志自由不可以牺牲，不得自由我宁死。人们要不知道争恋爱自由，则所有的一切都不必提了。这是我的宣言……" (Her declaration — "Life can be sacrificed, but freedom of will cannot; I would rather die than live without freedom."), "做学问，功夫要死，心眼要活。" (Her scholarly motto — "In scholarship, one must work with stubborn effort but keep an agile mind."), "我一介寒儒，连个后嗣亦无，能为国家民族留点什么？我想个人艰窘一点，存几个钱，身后让国家做学术奖金，奖掖后人吧！" (Her stated wish to leave her savings as national academic scholarships.), "我大半辈子与'老虎'同寝共枕，竟无察觉，是得了神经麻痹症吧？" (Her famous defiant response when pressured to denounce her husband in 1957.)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 环球人物 ---
URL: http://paper.people.com.cn/hqrw/html/2012-08/26/content_1112242.htm?div=-1

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from 《环球人物》 (Global People) magazine, written by historian 张耀杰, profiles the life and marriage standards of Chinese female writer 冯沅君 (Feng Yuanjun, 1900-1974), who was a pioneering female college student, feminist love-story writer, and later university professor. She was the sister of philosopher 冯友兰 (Feng Youlan) and geologist 冯景兰, and wife of classical literature scholar 陆侃如 (Lu Kanru).

Key biographical details:
- Born September 4, 1900, in 祁仪镇, 唐河县, 河南南阳, into a wealthy scholarly family. Her father 冯台异 was a 1898 jinshi (imperial examination graduate) who served in Zhang Zhidong's staff and died in 1908 as a county magistrate.
- Her feet were bound by her mother as a child, and her father arranged her marriage before his death to a wealthy young man from 方庄.
- In 1917, she insisted on going to Beijing to study at the newly upgraded 国立北京女子高等师范 (National Beijing Women's Higher Normal School), becoming one of the first generation of female university students in China's public education history. Her mother defied convention and took responsibility for allowing her to leave.
- During the May Fourth Movement (1919), she participated in demonstrations and drafted the manifesto to expel school principal 方还.
- The death of her classmate 李超 (Li Chao) in 1919, a victim of patriarchal family oppression, sparked a wave of anti-arranged-marriage sentiment. Feng Yuanjun led the movement by breaking off her own arranged engagement.
- In 1922, she graduated and became the only female graduate student at Peking University's 国学门 (National Studies research institute).
- From 1924, she published bold short stories in the Creation Society journals 《创造》 including 《隔绝》(Isolation), 《旅行》(Journey), 《慈母》(Mother), and 《隔绝之后》—these dealt with free love among college students and were largely autobiographical.
- Her first love was 王品青 (Wang Pinqing), a contributor to 《语丝》 magazine who helped compile her short story collection 《卷葹》 (published 1926, reviewed by Lu Xun who recommended 陶元庆 design its cover). However, Wang was already married and stopped pursuing further studies, which led to their breakup.
- She fell in love with 陆侃如, three years her junior, a graduate student at Tsinghua's 研究院. Wang Pinqing, upon seeing Lu's love letters to Feng, went mad from heartbreak and died. Feng addressed this triangular relationship in her 1928 story 《Epoch Making》.
- Lu Kanru compiled Feng's 50 love letters to him into the epistolary novel collection 《春痕》 published by 北新书局.
- In January 1929, Feng and Lu married in 江苏海门. Their academic collaborations included 《中国诗史》(History of Chinese Poetry, 1931) and 《中国文学史编》(1932), both three-volume works published by 上海大江书铺, establishing their reputations in classical Chinese literature studies.
- In 1932 they both studied at the University of Paris (Sorbonne), earning doctorates in 1935. Lu taught at 燕京大学, 中山大学, and 山东大学; Feng taught at 金陵女子大学, 复旦大学, 中山大学, 武汉大学, and 山东大学, becoming vice-president of 山东大学 in 1955.

The article's central thesis: Feng Yuanjun's criterion for choosing a spouse was "好好读书" (studying hard and continuing intellectual advancement). This was the primary reason she left Wang Pinqing (who stopped pursuing studies after graduation) for Lu Kanru (who shared her scholarly ambitions). The article concludes that the couple's grounding in diligent reading and scholarship was their means of overcoming difficulties through war and peace.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"好好读书，一直是冯沅君选择志同道合的婚恋对象的第一指标。她与王品青分手的主要原因，就在于王品青大学毕业之后不再读书进取。" ("Diligent study was always Feng Yuanjun's first criterion in choosing a kindred romantic partner. Her primary reason for parting with Wang Pinqing was that he ceased pursuing intellectual advancement after graduating from university.")

"'五四'运动爆发后，冯沅君跟随同学砸开学校后门，与北京其他学校的学生一起参加游行示威。在国文部主任陈中凡和图画科主任吕凤子的鼓动下，冯沅君还执笔起草了驱逐校长方还的宣言，列出方还十大罪状，最终导致方还辞职。"

"冯友兰虽是哲学系，却喜欢听语言文字学家黄侃教授的课...他后来曾说：'我的这种课外学习，倒是在我家里发生了作用，那就是把我的一知半解传授给我的妹妹沅君，引她走上了文学的道路。'"

"李超的死和追悼会，给我班的刺激很大，激起了反封建婚姻的怒潮。冯沅君同学带头和儿时在河南订婚的未婚夫退婚，其他同学纷纷响应。" (Classmate Cheng Junying's recollection)

"鲁迅...在致陶元庆的信中介绍说，王品青希望陶元庆为《卷葹》设计封面，'乃是淦女士的小说集，《乌合丛书》之一。内容是4篇讲爱的小说。卷葹是一种小草，拔了心也不死，然而什么形状，我却不知道。'"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: 中国戏剧研究的三种路向 - 石景山图书馆 ---
URL: http://106.37.81.211:8082/images/sjsimages/pdf/qk/zsdxxb-shkxb/zsdx2010/1003pdf/100301.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a scholarly article by Chen Pingyuan (陈平原), published in the Journal of Sun Yat-sen University (Social Science Edition), 2010, No. 3, Vol. 50, titled "Three Approaches to the Study of Chinese Drama" (中国戏剧研究的三种路向). The article examines the history of Chinese drama studies over the 20th century, arguing that three distinct approaches have characterized the field.

**Main Thesis:** Drama research can and must take multiple paths. The three representative approaches are: (1) Wang Guowei's (王国维) emphasis on literary beauty and textual/philological verification; (2) Wu Mei's (吴梅) focus on vocal beauty, musical prosody (声韵), and deep appreciation of the art; (3) Qi Rushan (齐如山), Zhou Yibai (周贻白), and Dong Meikan's (董每戡) emphasis on theatrical beauty and practical stage experience. The article explores the persistent tension between "literariness" (文学性) and "theatricality" (演剧性) in drama studies.

**Section 1 - Wang Guowei (1877-1927):** Wang's contribution was pioneering—his "宋元戏曲考" (Study of Song-Yuan Drama, 1913) established the basic framework for Chinese drama history research. Written in just three months but based on years of accumulated work (including 曲录, 戏曲考原, 唐宋大曲考, etc.), it applied classical philological methods (治经治子治史之法) to drama study. Wang emphasized the "意境界" (artistic conception) and "自然" (naturalness) of Yuan drama. However, Wang was not a theater-goer and had no stage experience; he abandoned drama research after 1913, turning decisively to archaeology, ancient history, and frontier studies—driven by the discovery of new materials (oracle bones, Dunhuang manuscripts, Han dynasty wooden slips, and the Grand Secretariat archives), all linked to Luo Zhenyu's (罗振玉) influence. The article interprets this as a scholar responding to the "new materials and new problems" of his era (citing Chen Yinke's concept of "预流" or "entering the current" of scholarship).

**Section 2 - Wu Mei (1884-1939):** Wu Mei, professor of Chinese literature at Peking University from 1917, was a master of qü (曲) studies—equally skilled in composition, singing, collecting, editing, and theoretical analysis. Unlike Wang's historical emphasis, Wu focused on "艺" (art), especially 声律 (musical prosody and tonal rules). His key works include 《顾曲麈谈》, 《曲学通论》, 《南北词简谱》, and 《中国戏曲概论》. Wu believed "创作" (creation) trumped research, and his own drama compositions were what he most valued. While Wang and Wu are jointly recognized as the two founders of modern Chinese drama studies, Wu's influence has been far less than Wang's. Critics like Ye Dejun (叶德均) attacked Wu's sloppy scholarship and casual attribution of borrowed ideas; others noted his traditional "qu" study approach lacked modern innovation. Wu's students (Ren Zhongmin, Lu Qian, etc.) largely ended up following Wang's more scholarly path.

**Section 3 - Qi Rushan, Zhou Yibai, and Dong Meikan:** These three scholars emphasized that drama must live on the stage, not just in the study. Qi Rushan (1875-1962) worked for decades with Mei Lanfang, co-founding the 北平国剧学会 (Beijing National Drama Society, 1931), and developed "国剧" (national drama) theory. His method was ethnographic—interviewing veteran performers over 20-30 years, recording stage practices (costumes, makeup, props, movement, music). His four principles of Chinese opera: 有声必歌 (all sounds are song), 无动不舞 (all movement is dance), 不许真物器上台 (no real objects on stage), 不许写实 (no realism). Zhou Yibai (1900-1977), of humble origins, wrote seven complete Chinese drama histories over four decades (from 1936's 《中国戏剧史略》 and 《中国剧场史》 to 1979's posthumous 《中国戏曲发展史纲要》), insisting that drama history must combine both 案头 (desk/text) and 场上 (stage) perspectives. Dong Meikan (1907-1980), a playwright and director who turned scholar in 1943, insisted that drama scholars must prioritize "演剧性" (theatricality) over "文学性" (literariness). His 《五大名剧论》 (On Five Great Plays) provides superb stage-oriented textual analysis. --- SOURCE 1: 余冠英 ---
URL: http://literature.cass.cn/jgsz/yjs/gdwxyjs/lrzz_szr/ygy_136358/202304/t20230426_5625127.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a biographical profile of Yu Guanying (余冠英, 1906–1995), a prominent Chinese classical literature scholar, hosted on the official website of the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS). The page is part of the institute's section on former group leaders and department directors of the Ancient Literature Research Office.

Key biographical details:
- Born in 1906 in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province. Entered Jiangsu Provincial No. 8 Middle School (now Yangzhou Middle School) in 1922.
- Enrolled at Tsinghua University's History Department in 1926, later transferring to the Chinese Literature Department. Graduated in 1931 and remained to teach at the university.
- During the War of Resistance Against Japan, served as Associate Professor and then Professor at Southwest Associated University, teaching Chinese literary history, essay writing, and selected works of various dynasties. Also served as chief editor of the National Chinese Monthly (《国文月刊》).
- Returned to Tsinghua in autumn 1946 as Professor of Chinese Literature, teaching Chinese literary history and Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties poetry.
- In 1953, transferred to the Peking University Institute of Literature (predecessor of today's CASS Institute of Literature), where he served as the main leader of the Ancient Literature Group (Department) from 1953 to 1979.
- Held additional positions including Deputy Director of the Institute, Advisor, Director of the Academic Committee, and chief editor of the journal Literary Heritage (《文学遗产》).
- Served as Deputy to the Third National People's Congress, member of the Fifth and Sixth National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), member of the All-China Federation of Literary and Art Circles, council member of the Chinese Writers Association, member of International PEN, and advisor to the National Ancient Book Collation and Publication Planning Group.

Major published works include: 《汉魏六朝诗论丛》(Collected Essays on Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poetry), 《古代文学杂论》(Miscellaneous Essays on Ancient Literature), 《诗经选》(Selected Poems of the Book of Songs), 《诗经选译》(Selected Translations of the Book of Songs), 《乐府诗选》(Selected Yuefu Poems), 《汉魏六朝诗选》(Selected Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poems), and 《三曹诗选》(Selected Poems of the Three Caos).

The page also lists links to his four representative works and is accompanied by navigation menus showing the institute's structure, including research departments, editorial boards, academic societies, and research centers. The page was published on 2023-04-26.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"1953—1979在任，古典文学组组长、古代室主任" (Served from 1953 to 1979 as head of the Classical Literature Group and Director of the Ancient Literature Department)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 余冠英 ---
URL: http://literature.cass.cn/jgsz/bjb/wxycbjb/lrld_135859/lrzb/202305/t20230505_5626768.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a biographical profile page from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS) Institute of Literature website, specifically a "Past Editors-in-Chief" page for the journal《文学遗产》(Literary Heritage). It documents the life and career of 余冠英 (Yu Guanying), a prominent Chinese literary scholar.

Key biographical details:
- Born in 1906 in Yangzhou, Jiangsu Province; died in September 1995.
- Graduated from Tsinghua University in 1931, then taught at Tsinghua University and Southwest Associated University (西南联合大学).
- In 1952, became a research fellow at the Institute of Literature, Chinese Academy of Sciences.
- Later served as Deputy Director of the Institute of Literature, Director of the Academic Committee, and Editor-in-Chief of the journal《文学遗产》(Literary Heritage).
- Major editorial works include《唐诗选》(Selected Tang Poems) as chief editor.
- Notable publications: 《汉魏六朝诗论丛》(Essays on Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poetry), 《乐府诗选》(Selected Yuefu Poems), 《祖国十二诗人》(Twelve Poets of the Motherland), 《诗经选》(Selected Book of Songs), 《三曹诗选》(Selected Poems of the Three Caos), 《诗经选译》(Selected Translations of the Book of Songs), 《古代文学研究集》(Collection of Ancient Literature Studies), and《古代文学杂论》(Miscellaneous Essays on Ancient Literature).

The page also includes navigation information showing the website belongs to the CASS Institute of Literature (中国社会科学院文学研究所), with its permanent domain at literature.cass.cn and ICP filing number 京ICP备05084176号.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
余冠英，1906年生，1995年9月辞世，生于江苏扬州。(Yu Guanying, born 1906, passed away September 1995, born in Yangzhou, Jiangsu.)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: 余冠英 ---
URL: https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%BD%99%E5%86%A0%E8%8B%B1/2936292

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Baidu Baike (Chinese encyclopedia) biographical entry for 余冠英 (Yu Guanying, 1906-1995), a renowned Chinese classical literature scholar.

**Basic Information:**
- Born May 16, 1906 in Jiangsu Songjiang (now part of Shanghai); died September 2, 1995 in Beijing
- Also known by aliases 绍生 (Shaosheng) and pen name 灌婴 (Guanying, a homophone of a Han dynasty general)
- Member of the Chinese Democratic League
- Graduated from Tsinghua University (enrolled 1926 in History, transferred to Chinese Literature, graduated 1931)

**Career Timeline:**
- 1926: Admitted to Tsinghua University
- 1931: Graduated from Tsinghua University Chinese Literature Department
- Served as professor at Tsinghua University and Southwest Associated University (西南联合大学)
- 1938: Moved to Kunming to join Southwest Associated University, initially as lecturer at the Normal College, later promoted to associate professor and full professor
- 1952: Became a Level 2 Researcher at the Chinese Academy of Sciences Literature Research Institute, later deputy director
- Served as chief editor of the journal 《文学遗产》 (Literary Heritage)
- Held positions including: 3rd NPC deputy, 5th-6th CPPCC National Committee member, China Writers Association council member, China Federation of Literary and Art Circles committee member, PEN International member, and advisor to the National Ancient Books Collation and Publishing Planning Group
- 1985: Retired from frontline work at age 79 but continued as consultant and honorary director of the Academic Committee and doctoral supervisor
- 1995: Passed away on September 2 in Beijing

**Key Achievements:**
- Led the compilation of 《中国文学史》(History of Chinese Literature, 3 volumes), published 1962 by People's Literature Publishing House
- Chief editor of 《唐诗选》(Selected Tang Poems), a selection project spanning 18 years
- Personally selected and annotated classic works including 《诗经选》(Selected Book of Songs), 《乐府诗选》(Selected Yuefu Poems), 《三曹诗选》(Selected Poems of the Three Caos), and 《汉魏六朝诗选》(Selected Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poems)
- Translated the Book of Songs (《诗经》) into vernacular Chinese
- Published academic works including 《汉魏六朝诗论丛》 and 《古代文学杂论》
- Research focused on pre-Qin to Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties poetry, emphasizing "realism" and "people-oriented" qualities in Chinese literature

**Early Life and Activism:**
- Father was a Qing dynasty military official; mother could read and paint
- Family moved to Yangzhou when he was 6, living there for 20 years
- Father died when he was 11; mother supported his book-buying habit
- At 15, entered Jiangsu Provincial No. 8 Middle School (later Yangzhou Middle School)
- During the May 30th Movement (五卅运动), served as first president of the Yangzhou Student Union, organizing student parades and inviting progressive speakers including communist revolutionary Yun Daiying (恽代英)
- During the war, edited the influential journal 《国文月刊》(National Chinese Monthly) through its 40th issue
- On June 18, 1948, signed the famous declaration "Protesting US Policy of Supporting Japan and Refusing American Aid Flour" (《抗议美国扶日政策并拒绝领取美援面粉宣言》) alongside Zhu Ziqing, Jin Yuelin, Wu Han, and others

**Notable Works List (Selected):**
- 乐府诗选注 (1953), 祖国十二诗人 (1955), 三曹诗选 (1956), 汉魏六朝诗论丛 (1956), 诗经选 (1956), 汉魏六朝诗选 (1958), 中国文学史 3-vol (1962), 诗经选译 (1985), 古代文学杂论 (1987), 中国古代山水诗鉴赏辞典 (1989), 古诗精选 (1992), 乐府诗集点校 (1979), among others

**Additional Details:**
- In his student years, organized the "唧唧诗社" (Jiji Poetry Society) at Tsinghua
- His essays and prose were published in 《清华周刊》 and 《中国文学会刊》; some works were collected by People's Literature Publishing House's 《当代散文精华》 and Zhu Ziqing's 《中国新文学大系》
- Wu Zuxiang praised him in 1931 as a representative writer embodying Tsinghua's literary style
- Personal quirk: enjoyed eating snacks like ice cream and cookies
- The page also includes the full text of his essay "清华不是个读书的好地方" (Tsinghua Is Not a Good Place to Study), written June 1, 1931, humorously arguing that Tsinghua's beautiful campus environment distracts students from studying
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"余冠英（1906年5月16日—1995年9月2日），字绍生，笔名灌婴，江苏松江（今属上海）人。中国古典文学专家，中国民主同盟盟员。"

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is the official page for the Ancient Literature Research Office (古代文学研究室) of the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (CASS, 中国社会科学院文学研究所). The page provides a comprehensive directory of scholars associated with the office, organized into several categories: former directors/leaders, past experts by generation (first through fifth generations), and current active researchers.

KEY STRUCTURE:
- The office is one of several research units within the Institute of Literature, which also includes departments for literary theory, Marxist literary theory, classical philology, modern/contemporary literature, Taiwanese/Hong Kong/Macau literature, folk literature, comparative literature, online literature, and digital humanities. The Institute also publishes academic journals including 《文学评论》(Literary Review), 《文学遗产》(Literary Heritage), and 《中国文学年鉴》(China Literary Yearbook).

邓绍基（1933—2013），江苏常熟人。中国社会科学院荣誉学部委员。1951年考入复旦大学中文系。1955年10月毕业后到中国科学院哲学社会科学部（即今中国社会科学院）文学研究所工作...主编或参与主编的大型著作有《中华文学通史》《中国文学通史系列》《中华文学通典》和《中国大百科全书·中国文学卷》，其中《元代文学史》1991年获中国社会科学院优秀科研成果奖。,钱锺书（1910—1998），字默存，号槐聚，江苏无锡人。著名文学史家、教育家钱基博之子。曾在苏州桃坞中学、无锡辅仁中学接受中学教育。1929-1933年就读于清华大学外文系...1937年在牛津大学埃克塞特学院获文学学士学位，学位论文为《十八世纪英国文学里的中国》...,王水照，1934年出生，浙江余姚人。1955年-1960年，于北京大学中文系学习，参与北大55级学生编撰的红皮文学史、黄皮文学史，为宋元段主要执笔人。1960年-1978年，分配到当时隶属于中国科学院哲学社会科学部的文学研究所工作，在钱锺书、何其芳、余冠英等先生指导下，参与了多项集体项目，包括《中国文学史》《唐诗选》等,栾贵明（1940—2022），北京市人，中国社会科学院文学研究所研究员。1964年毕业于北京大学中文系古典文献学专业...在钱锺书先生指导下，长年从事《永乐大典》研究。1980年代起，响应钱锺书先生的倡导，主持"中国古典数字工程"建设，开启研发中国古典文献数据库的探索工作,陈君，字温其，河南鹿邑人，中国社会科学院文学研究所研究员、中国社会科学院大学文学院教授。北京大学中文系文学学士（1999），新加坡国立大学中文系文学硕士（2002），北京大学中文系文学博士（2006）。主要从事汉魏六朝文学研究，出版专著《东汉社会变迁与文学演进》《润色鸿业：<汉书>文本的形成与早期传播》
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 5: 余冠英：为人民做学问的古典文史专家-中国社会科学网 ---
URL: https://www.cssn.cn/skgz/bwyc/202511/t20251117_5949548.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage, from the Chinese Social Sciences Network (中国社会科学网), is a tribute article about Yu Guanying (余冠英, 1906–1995), a renowned scholar of Chinese classical literature. Published on November 17, 2025, by authors Liu Ming and Li Xuyang from the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the article commemorates Yu's lifelong dedication to popularizing classical Chinese literary works for the public.

Yu Guanying taught at Southwest Associated University and Tsinghua University, where his scholarly approach was influenced by Zhu Ziqing. His work emphasized the "realist spirit" and "people's character" (人民性) of Chinese literature, following the principle that "the secret to all successful work is consulting with the masses" (一切工作成功的秘诀就是和大众商量).

Key achievements highlighted:
1. In 1950, Yu completed "Selection of Yuefu Poetry" (《乐府诗选》), published by People's Literature Publishing House in 1953—one of New China's earliest classical literature readers aimed at popularizing literary heritage. It received high praise from Zhu Guangqian, Sun Wang, and Wang Yunxi.
2. Between 1954–1959, he published "Selection of the Book of Songs" (《诗经选》), "Selection of the Three Cao's Poetry" (《三曹诗选》), and "Selection of Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poetry" (《汉魏六朝诗选》), plus contributing to "Selection of Tang Poetry" (《唐诗选》).
3. He served as researcher and head of the Chinese Classical Literature Research Group at the Institute of Literature (established 1953, transferred to the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1955).
4. He was responsible for compiling the pre-Tang section of the "History of Chinese Literature" (《中国文学史》), published in 1962.

His distinctive selection and annotation methodology combined textual research (考据), moral principles (义理), and rhetoric (辞章), with concise annotations and poetic commentary. His work established the "China Classical Literature Reading Series" as an academic milestone of the 1950s. The article emphasizes Yu's legacy as a pioneer in making classical Chinese literature accessible to ordinary readers while maintaining scholarly rigor—a model of "doing scholarship for the people" (为人民做学问).
</summary>

</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 6: 王季思 - 维基百科，自由的百科全书 ---
URL: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%8E%8B%E5%AD%A3%E6%80%9D

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Chinese Wikipedia biography page about Wang Jisi (王季思), a prominent Chinese opera (戏曲) scholar. Wang Jisi (1906–1996), whose given name was Wang Qi (王起) and courtesy name Jisi (季思), was a native of Yongjia County, Zhejiang Province (now Ouhai District, Wenzhou City). He served as a literature professor in the Chinese Department of Sun Yat-sen University (中山大學).

**Early Life:** Wang was a descendant of the prominent Wang Che family of Yongjia. He was well-read in classical texts from childhood and had a passion for opera and fiction. He entered Zhejiang Provincial No. 10 Middle School before finishing primary school. In 1925, he enrolled in the Literature Department of National Southeast University (國立東南大學), studying under the renowned opera master Wu Mei (吳梅). Wu Mei praised him highly, writing on one of his assignments: "Since Wanli, Yuting, and Weizhao left, I have gained this talent again; my heart is overjoyed!"

**Teaching Career:** After graduation, he taught at Zhejiang Provincial No. 10 Middle School and Jiangsu Provincial Songjiang Women's Middle School. After the August 13 Battle (八一三戰爭) broke out, he returned home to participate in anti-Japanese resistance work. He later taught at universities in Guizhou and at Zhejiang University in Hangzhou. He subsequently taught at Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou for a long period until his death.

**Political Persecution:** During the Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius Movement (批林批孔運動), Wang Jisi was labeled a "reactionary academic authority" (反动学术权威) and was persecuted as a result.

**Family:** His son, Wang Zeke (王則柯), also taught at Sun Yat-sen University.

- Yu and his wife shared a genuine love for Kunqu opera. From 1956 to 1964, Yu led the Beijing Kunqu Research Society (北京昆曲研习社), contributing to the preservation of Kunqu.
- The article concludes with Yu's "养生歌谣" (health preservation song): "Happy labor brings good spirit, adequate rest protects the brain. Long-term exercise strengthens the body, moderate entertainment brings no worries..." The author relates Yu's "innocence" to the Daoist philosophy of "naturalness" (自然), citing Laozi's teaching that water is the most yielding yet most powerful force—innocence, like water, is invincible in matters of longevity.

The author is an editor at the Chinese Social Sciences Press (中国社会科学出版社).

SUMMARY:

This article from Jiangsu Writers' Network (江苏作家网) commemorates the 121st anniversary of the birth of Yu Pingbo (俞平伯, 1900–1990), a renowned Chinese literary scholar, poet, and Redology (红楼梦研究) expert. Written from the perspective of the author's reading of the "Wang Boxiang Diary" (《王伯祥日记》), the piece chronicles the friendship between Yu Pingbo and Wang Boxiang (王伯祥), two scholars who worked together at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences Institute of Literature.

Key biographical facts: Yu Pingbo was born in Suzhou to a family from Deqing County, Zhejiang. His great-grandfather was the famous Qing dynasty scholar Yu Yue (俞樾). He entered Peking University in 1915, published his first new-style poem "Spring Water" (《春水》) in the New Youth magazine in 1918, joined the New Tide Society, and was a participant in the May Fourth Movement. He published his first poetry collection "Winter Night" (《冬夜》) in 1922 and joined the Literary Research Society in 1921.

The article details the founding of the Institute of Literature in 1952–1953, when Yu Pingbo and Wang Boxiang participated in its preparation under Zheng Zhenduo's leadership. Yu was assigned to annotate the Book of Songs (《诗经选》) while Wang worked on the Records of the Grand Historian (《史记选》).

A major focus is the 1954 campaign criticizing Yu Pingbo's "A Study of the Dream of the Red Chamber" (《红楼梦研究》), which began with critiques by Li Xifan and Lan Ling in October 1954. The article uses Wang Boxiang's diary entries from October–December 1954 to document the intense criticism sessions at the Institute, the pressure on Yu, and the mutual support between the two elderly friends—including a memorable outing to Beihai Park and a mutton barbecue meal in November 1954, after which Yu composed a poem expressing gratitude for Wang's friendship during his hardship.

The article also covers: the 1956 researcher ranking system, where He Qifang (何其芳) insisted Yu Pingbo be rated as a first-class researcher despite the criticism he faced (Yu reportedly responded "差不多,差不多" - "roughly right"); Yu's later years maintaining private interest in the Red Chamber Dream despite public silence on the topic; Wang Boxiang's death in December 1975; and Yu's tribute elegy. The piece concludes with reflections on the scholarly virtues of Yu Pingbo's generation—their rigorous academic spirit, sincere character, and warm approach to life.

--- SOURCE 1: 唐圭璋，活成了一代词宗，也活成了一代情圣-青岛唐氏宗亲网 ---
URL: https://www.qdtang.cn?hygl%2F504.html=

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the Qingdao Tang Clan Association website (青岛唐氏宗亲网, qdtang.cn) and contains a detailed biographical article about Tang Guizhang (唐圭璋, 1901-1990), a renowned Chinese ci (词) poetry scholar affectionately known as "一代词宗" (a generation's master of ci poetry) and "一代情圣" (a generation's romantic devoted one).

**Biographical Overview:**
- Born January 23, 1901, in Nanjing to a Manchu (满族) bannerman family. Lost his father at age 7 and mother at age 11, raised by others. Two key benefactors: Principal Chen Rongzhi of Qiwangjie Primary School (who waived all fees) and Principal Qiu Cai of the Provincial Fourth Normal School.
- Entered National Southeast University's Chinese Department in 1922, studied under renowned ci master Wu Mei (吴梅). Became one of "吴门三杰" (Three Outstanding Students of Wu Mei) alongside Ren Zhongmin and Lu Qian, excelling specifically in ci studies.
- Graduated 1928, taught at various institutions including Jiangsu First Girls' Middle School, Central Military Academy, Central University (Chongqing/Chengdu during wartime), Jinling University, Northeast Normal University, and finally Nanjing Normal University (1953-1990) as professor and doctoral supervisor.
- Died November 28, 1990, at age 89, in his tiny study "Mengtong Zhai" (梦桐斋) of less than 8 square meters.

**Major Academic Works (20+ volumes, over 10 million characters):**
- 《全宋词》(Complete Ci of the Song Dynasty)
- 《全金元词》(Complete Ci of Jin and Yuan Dynasties)
- 《词话丛编》(Compilation of Ci Commentaries — revised 1986 edition by Zhonghua Book Company, 5 volumes, 85 ci commentaries, nearly 4 million characters)
- 《宋词三百首笺注》、《南唐二主词汇笺》、《唐宋词简释》、《宋词四考》、《宋词纪事》、《梦桐词》、《词学论丛》 and others.

**Teaching Style:** Like his mentor Wu Mei, he brought a flute to class and would sing ci poems and opera excerpts in Kunqu style to deepen students' understanding.

**"重拙大" (Heavy, Plain, Grand) Theory:** Tang was influenced by Wang Pengyun and Kuang Zhouyi, using "重拙大" as the standard for selecting and annotating Tang-Song ci poems in his 《唐宋词简释》, which includes 67 poets and 232 poems (56 Tang, 176 Song). He also proposed the four principles of "雅婉厚亮" (elegant, gentle, substantial, bright) for ci composition.

**Personal Life and Tragedy:**
- Married Yin Xiaozeng (尹孝曾), a young lady from the Yin family garden in Lijixiang, Nanjing. Their marriage was happy; he played the flute under the wutong tree while she fanned him on summer nights.
- Yin died on Lunar New Year's Eve 1936. Tang never remarried and mourned her for the rest of his life, visiting her grave with flute, books, and simple food for entire days.
- Suffered all three of life's great misfortunes: orphaned young, widowed in middle age, and losing his daughters Tang Dihua (d. 1967) and Tang Diyi (d. 1956), leaving him to raise grandchildren as an elderly man.
- His 《梦桐词》 (133 poems, 61 written during the Anti-Japanese War) was named "Mengtong" (Dream Wutong) partly to memorialize his late wife (referencing the "half-dead wutong tree" from Mei Cheng's 《七发》) and partly for his homesickness during the war years.

**Quotes:** In a 1984 letter he wrote: "词作通俗，可谓白话词，实不足与前贤相比，由于我身世凄凉少无父母，中年丧偶，晚年丧女所写每聊记梦痕而已" (My ci poems are plain, mere vernacular verse, not comparable to the ancients; because my life has been desolate — no parents in youth, widowed in middle age, losing daughters in old age — I merely record traces of dreams).

The article also references content from 《"情圣"词宗唐圭璋》 by Zhao Puguang of Nanjing Normal University. The site includes navigation for news, genealogy, notable figures, cultural relics, and contact information (phone: 18661637226, WeChat: 103317480).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"唐圭璋：1901-1990，字季特。南京人。我国著名词学家、文学家，被誉为'一代词宗'。", "人们常说，人生三大不幸是幼年丧怙，中年丧偶，老年丧子。然而这三不幸竟然全降临在一人身上。", "先生《论词之作法》云：'雅清新纯正；婉温柔缠绵；厚沉郁顿挫；亮名隽高华'。'雅婉厚亮'四字，凝聚了先生多年的研究心得和创作体验。", "词作通俗，可谓白话词，实不足与前贤相比，由于我身世凄凉少无父母，中年丧偶，晚年丧女所写每聊记梦痕而已。", "1986年中华书局出版《词话丛编》(修订本)精装五大册，增补了25种，共计85种词话，近400万字，集历代词话之大成，为我国词学史上矗立了一座丰碑。"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 从双林巷走出的曲学宗师吴梅 - 苏州市地方志编纂委员会办公室 ---
URL: https://dfzb.suzhou.gov.cn/dfzb/fzxh/200909/952cf8b7d8d440a2a4b4df77d3b8235c.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the Suzhou Local Chronicles (苏州地方志) website presents a detailed biographical and scholarly article about Wu Mei (吴梅, 1884-1939), a renowned Chinese opera (qu) master from Shuanglin Lane (双林巷) in Suzhou. The article is divided into four main sections covering his life, his research in qu studies, his dramatic works, and his students.

**Wu Mei's Life:** Born in 1884 in Changzhou County (now Suzhou), Jiangsu Province, Wu Mei came from a distinguished family (his great-grandfather Wu Zhongjun was a top imperial exam candidate in 1832). He experienced early family tragedy—his father died when he was 3, his mother when he was 10. He was adopted by his great-uncle Wu Changxiang. At age 12, he began studying under Pan Xiake, and despite failing the imperial exams, he developed a passion for ci poetry and early opera works like Wang Shifu's "The Romance of the Western Chamber." He began writing opera at age 17 (1901) with his first work "Fengdongshan." He taught at numerous institutions including Peking University, Southeast University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Central University. During the Sino-Japanese War, he fled with his family through multiple cities, eventually dying in Yunnan in March 1939 at age 56.

**Wu Mei's Qu Studies:** Wu Mei is considered one of the two greatest Chinese drama scholars of the early 20th century, alongside Wang Guowei (王国维). While Wang Guowei focused on historical research, Wu Mei excelled in the practical and theoretical study of qu itself—composing, notating, performing, and analyzing the art form. His major works include "Gugu Chen Tan" (顾曲麈谈), "Chinese Opera Overview" (中国戏曲概论), and "Southern and Northern Ci Simplified Notation" (南北词简谱, a 20-year project covering 1,108 musical modes). He was also a performer who appeared on stage in roles from famous plays and mentored celebrated actors including Mei Lanfang.

**Dramatic Works:** Wu Mei wrote approximately 10 surviving plays including "Fengdongshan" (his early revolutionary masterpiece about the Southern Ming resistance hero Qu Shisi), "Xuehuafei" (about the Six Gentlemen of the 1898 Reform Movement, later destroyed by his grandfather), "Luoyinji" and "Shuangleibei" (addressing women's rights issues), and his "Shuangya Sanju" trilogy including "Xiangzhenge," "Wujiabao," and "Chouchangcuan" (his most mature work, a four-play set about Tang and Song dynasty poets).

**His Students:** Wu Mei trained a remarkable generation of scholars including Ren Zhongmin (founder of the discipline of sanqu studies), Lu Qian, Tang Guizhang (famous for compiling "Complete Song Ci" / 全宋词), Wang Jisi (noted for annotating "The Romance of the Western Chamber"), Qian Nanyang (a leading scholar of Southern opera), Cai Ying, and Wan Yunjun, among others. Many of his students became leading figures in Chinese classical literature and opera studies.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"近世对于戏曲一门学问，最有研究者推王静安先生与吴先生两人。静安先生在历史考证方面，开戏曲史研究之先路，但在戏曲本身之研究，还当推瞿安先生独步……" (Pu Jiangqing's assessment that Wang Guowei led historical research but Wu Mei was unrivaled in the study of opera itself), "凡学问有为潮流所趋者，有为时代所弃者，有赖书本文献足以传后者，有非接近其人、得其指点不能妙悟者……今从先生游者尚不能尽其所学，况后世但读其书者乎？" (from Pu Jiangqing's memorial to Wu Mei), "吴梅'藏曲之富，海内无与伯仲'，但他并不居为奇货，秘不示人" (Wu Mei's collection of opera works was unmatched in China, yet he freely shared it), "特是曲学之兴，国维治之三年，未若吴梅之劬以毕生；国维限于元曲，未若吴梅之集其大成；国维评其历史，未若吴梅之发其条例；国维赏其文学，未若吴梅之析其声律。而论曲学者，并世要推吴梅为大师云！" (Qian Jibo's comparison of Wu Mei and Wang Guowei, concluding Wu Mei was the greater master of qu studies), "一出戏救活了一个剧种" (Zhou Enlai's 1956 comment on Kunqu opera, connecting to Wu Mei's legacy)
</key_excerpts>

2. **Curriculum Contributions**: Zhu established a five-year curriculum plan with one major (Chinese Language and Literature) and two specializations (Chinese Literature and Chinese Language). 3. **Teaching Style**: Zhu taught "History of Chinese Literary Criticism" to fourth-year students, following his 1944 book "大纲" (Outline of the History of Chinese Literary Criticism) published by Kaiming Bookstore. Zhu Ziqing called his book "China's first concise complete history of Chinese literary criticism." Guo Shaoyu is considered the pioneer and Zhu Dongrun one of the founders of Chinese literary criticism studies.

The lecture discusses the life and career of Zhu Dongrun (朱东润, 1897-?), a renowned Chinese scholar, calligrapher, and pioneering figure in Chinese biographical literature. Key points covered include:

- Zhu Dongrun was born in 1897 in Taixing County, northern Jiangsu Province, into a poor family (his father was a shop clerk). He survived being abandoned as an infant due to family poverty.
- His educational journey: he attended Nanyang Public School (南洋公学, predecessor of Jiaotong University) in Shanghai as a companion/study partner for a wealthy relative; the school principal Tang Wenzhi (唐文治) paid his tuition after he excelled. - He worked as a language teacher at a normal school in Nantong (established by Zhang Jian/张謇), where he was discovered by Wen Yiduo (闻一多), dean of the Wuhan University College of Liberal Arts. Wen invited him to teach English and then Chinese, leading to his compilation of the influential textbook 《中国文学批评史大纲》(Outline of the History of Chinese Literary Criticism), which established his academic reputation.
- During the Japanese invasion (from 1937), he traveled alone from Shanghai through Hong Kong, Cambodia, and Vietnam to rejoin Wuhan University, which had relocated to Leshan, Sichuan.
- In 1952 he joined Fudan University (复旦大学) in Shanghai, where he served as head of the Chinese Department for many years (including after his rehabilitation from the Cultural Revolution at age 80).
- He lived to age 92, attributed partly to his daily calligraphy practice. A collection of his calligraphy, 《朱东润书法作品选》, was published by Shanghai Calligraphy and Painting Publishing House in 1996.

- His autobiography 《八十年》(Eighty Years), published by the Eastern Publishing Center in 1999.
- His incomplete manuscript on Yuan Haowen was written even while hospitalized.

His biographical theory emphasized: choosing subjects with responsibility, character, and moral force; that both great and ordinary people could be biographical subjects (though practically great figures are more accessible); drawing on Western biographical traditions (Boswell's 'Life of Johnson', Strachey's 'Queen Victoria', Plutarch's 'Lives'); and using dialogue based on historical evidence. ###### *郭绍虞：披沙拣金，为中国文学批评史学科奠基*

分享到：

来源：文汇报　|　李纯一　　*2021年08月15日08:13*

**关键词：**[郭绍虞](http://search.chinawriter.com.cn/chinawriter/search.do?pageNum=1&searchField=content&keyword=%E9%83%AD%E7%BB%8D%E8%99%9E)

**【参与发起成立“文学研究会”】**

◆郭绍虞回忆“文学研究会”的成立，说郑振铎“是我们一班年轻小伙子中最有生气最有魄力的人”。一到晚上，郑振铎就来找他聊天：“一谈就扯得很远，言必称希腊的时候比较多，言必称三代的毛病，在当时似乎要犯得少一些（后来则有时不免就要谈到古典文学了）。有时又拉得太近，尤其在一俯一仰，月光如水，人影在地，当前景色成为谈话资料的时候，有时恬适，有时感慨，甚至有时也吐些狂言……”

**【自学成才的一级教授】**

◆出身“寒儒”家庭的郭绍虞没有接受“科班训练”的幸运，但他刻苦自学，终于有所成就。1980年，郭绍虞撰文《我怎样研究中国文学批评史的》告诉青年朋友：“我记忆力不强，悟性又不高，所以成就很小。差幸我没有惰性，依靠笔记或纸片，用极笨拙的办法来弥补这方面的缺陷。又因生性木讷，不长交际，于是尽量减少社交活动的时间……即所谓‘将勤补拙’。”

**【推崇狂狷，同时认为狷比狂更重要】**

◆唐弢用郭绍虞提倡的“狂狷人生”作为纪念文章的标题，他看到介而有守的“狷性”是郭绍虞以及许多中国知识分子的精神底色：“从狷性，从有所不为出发，不断进取，不断有选择、有辨别地吸收狂性，在现实主义的基础上带一点浪漫气氛，这是中国知识分子走向革命的可贵的性格，在这点上，绍虞先生有许多值得我们纪念的地方，我因此作《狂狷人生》。”

**“善于将不同门类的知识镕入一炉”**

“郭绍虞先生身处新文化运动的潮流中，学术上深受本时期中外文化交涉的影响。他不惟国学功底扎实，亦敏于吸纳外来思潮，治学力求会通文学与语言文字作一体化的考察，善于将不同门类的知识镕入一炉精心锤炼。”复旦大学中文系教授陈允吉仿效杜甫《八哀》作诗传追怀中文系故老，写到郭绍虞先生时，有一句“博通疏堰塞，鳞萃汇炉锤”。

【学术档案】

郭绍虞（1893—1984），原名希汾，字绍虞，江苏苏州人。早年投身五四新文化运动，1921年参与发起成立“文学研究会”。先后在福建协和大学、燕京大学、大夏大学、同济大学等校任教，解放后任复旦大学中文系教授兼系主任、文学研究室主任、图书馆馆长等。主要致力于中国古典文学、中国文学批评史、语言学、书法理论等方面的研究。著有《中国文学批评史》《沧浪诗话校释》《宋诗话考》《汉语语法修辞新探》等二十余部作品，主编《中国历代文论选》《清诗话续编》等，为建立有体系的中国文学批评史作出杰出贡献。

人们印象中温和乐善、慢条斯理、浓浓苏州腔的老先生郭绍虞，年轻时是一个标准的五四青年——写新诗，研究民歌谚语，宣扬社会主义。他解放后任职的复旦大学中文系有“斗士”的传统。与一般文学系多名士不同，复旦中文的老师多关心社会现实，与时代脉搏保持互动。而最早明言“斗士”一词的，正是郭绍虞。

抗战初北平沦陷，站在燕京大学课堂上，郭绍虞讲到《黍离》诗时，泪随声下。之后，拒不附逆的他离开北平回到南方。他反对“伪”、反对“滑”，分析汉奸的思想性情，批判部分文人“乡愿”的特质。他特别喜欢引用“狂者进取，狷者有所不为”，并将“狷性”写进对朱自清的悼念文章：

各人性分所限，未可一致，只须淡泊而不躁进，有正义感而不抹煞良心，自然不会帮凶；处事认真，生活严肃，自然也不会帮闲。不帮凶，不帮闲，虽不曾做到十足的积极的斗士，至少也可以说是不会与斗士背道而驰的。

“狂性”的闻一多先生更英锐、激烈，是斗士，而“狷性”的朱先生则沉潜、雍容，是“不必定以斗士姿态出现而仍不失为斗士的人”。

1985年，作家、文学理论家唐弢撰文纪念郭绍虞，题目正是“狂狷人生”。

**“这好像是个幸运，但是不然”**

1893年，郭绍虞出生于苏州吴县一户清寒的读书人家，因家境窘困，念到中学二年级便辍了学，之后辗转苏州、无锡、上海等地小学任教。1914年，他来到上海商务印书馆下属的尚公小学。商务印书馆专事古籍善本收藏的涵芬楼，让戮力自学的郭绍虞大大受益。期间，他还结识了1916年进入商务编译所的沈雁冰。

在受聘于进步书局（亦称文明书局）后，郭绍虞编撰注释了多部著作，包括《清诗评注读本》《战国策详注》等。他亦在体校兼课，为准备讲义，编成我国第一部《中国体育史》，童年时代的好友叶圣陶为之作序，由商务印书馆出版，后收入“万有文库”。

此时，新文化运动正如火如荼地展开。顾颉刚在北大新潮社，邀请为《新潮》写稿的同乡叶圣陶和郭绍虞入社。郭绍虞与顾颉刚就此相识。1919年秋，他应顾颉刚推荐为北京《晨报副刊》每日供稿，于是来到北京“勤工俭学”——在北大旁听，同时做一些翻译、写作的工作，他说这样，方才受到了一些大学教育。

郭绍虞对蔡元培提倡的美育产生兴趣，1920年为《晨报副刊》连作98篇“艺术谈”，并先后发表《马克思年表》《记录杜威演讲稿》等作品。他赞赏苏俄社会主义，认同社会改造不仅在物质，更在精神，需从文艺改造起来，撰有《社会改造家列传》《从艺术上企图社会的改造》《俄国美论与其文艺》等文，译述日本高山林次郎的《近世美学》。后来，他曾对学生兼助手的蒋凡提起，当时自己是初生牛犊不怕虎，英文、德文、日文都敢翻译——只有五四青年才敢这么做。

于此期间，郭绍虞结识了在北京铁路管理学校读书的郑振铎。郑振铎经常来沙滩春台公寓看望他，两人都不喜欢在斗室中闷坐，于是常常徘徊月下，边走边谈。由于郑振铎的介绍，郭绍虞与瞿秋白、耿济之、许地山等人相识。1920年10月，瞿秋白作为《晨报》驻莫斯科记者离京赴苏，郭绍虞赋《流星》一诗赠别：

你们冲开这云气的沉郁，/和别的星儿们/起新样的化合。为和上海方面取得联系，郭绍虞又介绍叶圣陶、沈雁冰与郑振铎通信。1921年元旦，他们共同发起成立了中国现代文学史上最著名的文学社团——“文学研究会”。2月，郭绍虞南下任济南第一师范教员。同年结婚，郑振铎为伴郎。

这年秋天，福建协和大学想要创办中文系，胡适、顾颉刚都保荐郭绍虞去。对方为郑重计，特地到济南来见，看到他的《战国策详注》《中国体育史》二书后，定下心来。由此，郭绍虞开始了他的大学执教生涯。对这一经历，他总结说：“我在大学教书，还不到28岁，而且一直当教授。这好像是个幸运，但是不然。”“自学严格才能抓得住机会，由机会所以更推动自学，加速进度。”之后，他倍加努力，集中精力研究讲授中国古代文学、文字学和语言学。

**用科学方法把旧学讲得系统化**

北伐军攻克武昌后，沈雁冰在汉口任《民国日报》主编。1927年，他已转用“茅盾”一名。缘于茅盾的推荐，当年2月，郭绍虞离开河南中州大学，抵达武昌第四中山大学任教。8月起，应冯友兰之邀赴燕京大学任教。他在燕大长达十四年，开设批评史课程，由此开始致力于《中国文学批评史》的研究写作。至1934年上册问世，1947年下册出齐，前后历时二十余年。他几乎是全身心地投入——儿子郭泽弘说，期间父亲曾经痴迷象棋，连烧掉几副才完成此书。

“在旧时代，诗文评论常被人们视为谈艺小道，地位不高；在目录学领域，诗文评被置于集部之末，没有人对古代文学批评进行系统的历史的论述。”王运熙在为郭绍虞《中国文学批评史》1998年重印版所撰序言里这样写道。国内学者有关中国文学批评史学科的第一部著作是1927年陈中凡先生的同题著作，这也是五四以后受西潮新潮影响，文学批评地位提升的结果。不过这部著作内容简单，材料也属常见的诗文评提要、史书文苑传。郭绍虞则在陈中凡《中国文学批评史》的启发下，另辟天地。涵芬楼此时再次护航。郭绍虞早前买到过一部《涵芬楼古今文钞》，曾辑出里面的论文之语，再读编者吴曾祺所著《涵芬楼文谈》，更觉批评史领域大有可为。他尤重文献资料的发掘整理，在燕京大学图书馆、书肆、友人等处多方搜求，广征中国古代各种诗话、词话、乐论、论诗诗等等，认真检阅每一个批评家的全部著作，搜找出有关篇章。朱自清先生1934年评价说：“第一个人大规模搜集材料来写中国文学批评史的，得推郭绍虞先生。……在浩如烟海的书籍中披沙拣金……他的书虽不是同类中的第一部，可还得算是开创之作；因为他的材料与方法都是自己的。”这部书后来也被公推为“最有系统、最深入的一部”，是中国文学批评史学科“最重要的奠基石”。

郭绍虞谦称自己只是跟随者，而且是因为对编著中国文学史的宏愿“知难而退”，才“各照隅隙，鲜观衢路” （《文心雕龙·序志篇》）地进入中国文学批评史这一较小也未及照亮的园地。他希望，能“从文学批评史以印证文学史，以解决文学史上的许多问题”“在这些材料中间，使人窥出一些文学的流变”。这一注重文学批评，同时不全然因为替新文学理论开道而抛弃中国古代文论的态度，可以追溯到他20岁刚来上海时。郭绍虞说，那时，他幸运地在旧书铺里买到几乎全部的《国粹学报》，读到刘师培如何论文，王国维如何论词，引起他对古典文学的兴趣——用科学方法把旧学讲得系统化；同时，他亦受到胡适的影响，认同胡适“研究问题，输入学理，整理国故，再造文明”的主张。这一对待学问的态度，贯穿他终身。

郭绍虞在中国文学批评史园地所做的系统性工作，以宋诗话的整理和研究最具代表性。针对明人视“诗话兴而诗亡”导致宋诗话多有散失或不确的情况，他着手搜辑与清理：考辨诗话作者及生平，严勘诗话文字异同，辨析著录情况与版本源流，并对诗话内容及影响加以评述。他先后完成《宋诗话辑佚》（1937年哈佛燕京学社印行，70年代末补充修订后中华书局重版），以及《沧浪诗话校释》《诗品集解》《杜甫戏为六绝句集解》等多部专书研究，著成《宋诗话考》（中华书局1979年出版）。其中《宋诗话辑佚》成为此后唐宋诗歌与诗学研究者案头必备的文献。在批评史研究的同时，郭绍虞还兼治语法修辞，可谓“照隅”与“通识”兼备，两相促进。就语法修辞这一隅，他说“清儒之治古书，与诗人文人之论诗例文例，均可视为奠定语法修辞之基”，由此“法从例出”，并且：

语法、修辞、词汇三者相结合，而汉语之特征显。汉语之特征显，然后吸收外人之学，取其分类之长而活用之，则洋为中用，而不为西语陈规所束缚，同时复使昔人《古书疑义举例》、《经传释词》以及《文则》一类之书成为科学化、通俗化，则古为今用，亦不致抱残而守阙，斯则最根本、最基础之步骤。

三十年代起，郭绍虞开始研究古代文学的语言问题，背景正是新诗句法越来越欧化，遭人诟病，他希望能从旧文学里为白话文学找到药方——他也是一个写新诗的诗人呐！在《中国语词之弹性作用》和《中国语词的声音美》等文章中，他指出中国旧文学富含语词升缩、分合、变化、颠倒等修辞技巧，而新文学作家如能学习文言文的这一长处，便能让白话文作品更富音乐性，声情并美。他从语言形式出发，认为自由化、散文化和语体化是中国文学的演进趋势，由此试图建立新旧文学之间的传续关系，解决文白之争，调和而务实。

**“吾 行 吾 素 耳，谈不到高调低调”**

1941年太平洋战争爆发，燕京大学也被日军所占领。日伪曾将郭绍虞关押两日，强迫他到伪北大任教，而为他坚拒。同人中有改至伪北大任课者，讥他不去是“唱高调”，郭绍虞于是撰《高调歌》一首以作回应：

不愿出山也好，便甘下海也好。吾行吾素耳，汝安则为之，谈不到高调低调！

各见平生怀抱，各显本来面貌！“纡辔诚可学，违己讵非迷”，原不关高调低调！

此后，郭绍虞一度在私立中国大学任教。1943年，他匆促南下，将家人安置在苏州，许多衣服用具都弃之不顾，但对自己搜藏得到的清人诗话资料，却不忍割舍。单身一人来到“孤岛”上海后，他为叶圣陶的开明书店编书编杂志，同时在大夏大学等校兼课。曾在大夏念书的儿童文学作家、翻译家任溶溶回忆，郭绍虞这时候一个人住在开明书店编辑部三楼，睡在一张帆布行军床上。

抗战胜利后，他愤怒于蝇营狗苟、无奇不有的社会现实，接连发表《民主与狂狷精神》《论狂狷人生》《论勇与狂狷》等文，号召知识分子不要“中行”，而要“狂狷”，主张特立独行、不说谎话，以肃清汉奸心理：

乡愿之病在于伪，国愿之病在于滑。……呼之为牛可以应之为牛，呼之为马可以应之为马……道家所谓“自然”，佛家所谓“随缘”，都给他们应用到恰好处。……所以自己没有立场，也就变作没有骨气；所以平时无所谓操守，遇变时就无所谓气节。

1946年，同济大学创立文学院中国文学系，郭绍虞任教授兼系主任，同时在多校兼职。他加入了上海大学教授联谊会，即“大教联”，积极投身民主运动。1950年，同济文法学院并入复旦大学，郭绍虞出任复旦大学中文系教授兼系主任，后来还兼任图书馆馆长、古代文学研究室主任、中国语言文学研究所名誉所长等职，在复旦大学度过了后半生的34年。

出任复旦大学中文系主任以后，郭绍虞锐意改革。据唐弢回忆，他约请了不少当时在上海的文学家去讲课，其中有冯雪峰、胡风、李健吾、王元化等等。郭绍虞1956年加入中国共产党。入党不久，便将他早年用教书薪酬在苏州建的99间房屋全部捐献给国家。在学术研究上，一直立志用科学方法重述旧学的郭绍虞，也努力根据新的理论来修改《中国文学批评史》。最早，他是站在“纯文学观”的立场来看古代文学批评的，依据文学观念的演变将中国文学批评史分为三个时期：演进期、复古期、完成期。1934年，《中国文学批评史》上册完成时，郭绍虞向胡适求序，胡适虽不满意于这三个分期的命名，并提出若干可议之处，但还是写道：“读者的见解也许不一定和郭君完全一致，但无论何人都不能不宝贵这一巨册的文学批评史料……他确能抓住几个大潮流的意义……使人格外明了文学变迁的理论的背景。”序言写成后未用，郭绍虞将序末二段收入自序。书出版后，钱锺书在《大公报·文艺副刊》上作《论复古》一文提出质疑，认为文学领域不存在古今、新旧的冲突，后来者未必比先起者内容结构更高明、价值更好或引起更大美感，历史进化论并不适用于文学；且所谓进化必然包含目标，然而历史演变无穷尽，这一时的顺流逆流将来可能会翻转。郭绍虞再作《谈复古》一文辩驳，他说自己绝不是“为学时髦而敌视复古”，且已在书序中说明：“曰复古，曰完成，都是不甚恰当的名词，亦强为之名而已。……复古的结果，正可以创造一种新文学。”对此，20世纪过去后，叶辉、周兴陆在《复旦中国文学批评史研究》一书中评述说：“在今天看来，用演进/复古、文/质、形式/内容的对立与转化来概括原本丰富复杂的古代文学批评史，不免失之偏颇、机械，但这种‘二元对立’恰恰是20世纪前期大部分时间里人文学者的最基本的思维模式。这种思维模式是与革旧布新的时代大势相一致的，也体现出人文学者从旧的文化遗产中寻求新动向、新萌芽的努力。”

五十年代，郭绍虞为方便初学者删改出一卷本的《中国文学批评史》，后来亦曾尝试用“现实主义与反现实主义斗争”的理论、“儒法斗争”的理论来作改写。改得很吃力，自己也不满意，但他并非违心努力，而是真诚地相信：“我们研究中国文学批评史，不是为研究而研究，而应该是有利于推动社会主义新文艺的发展。”这与早年发起文学研究会，提倡“为人生而艺术”一贯。六十年代初向郭绍虞请教问学的王元化，后来记下：

在粉碎“四人帮”后，那时的气氛完全不同了。他略带微笑地向我说，他曾经也想用儒法斗争的观点去修改《中国文学批评史》，可是还没有来得及，“文革”结束了。这种毫无掩饰的坦诚，再一次使我惊讶。绍虞先生虽教书多年，但他不是口才辩给的人。他不大会说话，因而就需要从他那近于木讷的谈吐中去发掘寄托遥深的寓意。绍虞先生真诚地相信应改造自己跟上时代的步伐，像许多老一代知识分子一样。

1961年起，郭绍虞与罗根泽共同主编“中国古典文学理论批评专著选辑”，还与钱仲联等同行专家一起编《中国历代文论选》。唐弢说起这一年大家的填词唱和里，郭绍虞写“犹有壮志雄心，争鸣其放，待创新文物。人在东风忘是老，管他白丝青发。红欲加鞭，专图破的，试作高峰越……”是“一个老学者专心致志地要求进步的胸怀”，他“狂狷人生的天平砝码”有变动了，浪漫的气氛益发强烈；但郭绍虞身上仍有狷性，所以旁人不必为他修改旧著而感到难过，因为“这种狷性必将引导他走上科学道路”。进入耄耋之年后，郭绍虞仍然紧跟时代的跃动，提出要建立具有中国民族特点的马克思主义文艺理论，用学术来参与新思想、新文化的建设。

**“烈 士 暮 年，壮心未已”**

![](/NMediaFile/2018/0510/MAIN201805101635526610551558369.jpg)

![](/img/MAIN/2018/04/118229/img/top.jpg)

args.summary:
This webpage is an article from China Writer's Network (中国作家网), published by Wenhui Daily (文汇报) on August 15, 2021, by author Li Chunyi (李纯一). The article is a biographical tribute to Guo Shaoyu (郭绍虞, 1893–1984), a foundational figure in the establishment of the academic discipline of Chinese literary criticism history (中国文学批评史).

Key biographical details:
- Born in 1893 in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, to an impoverished scholarly family; dropped out of school in his second year of middle school due to financial hardship.
- Self-taught and worked as an elementary school teacher in Suzhou, Wuxi, and Shanghai. At the Commercial Press's Shanggong Elementary School (1914), he benefited from the Hanfenlou (涵芬楼) rare books collection.
- Compiled China's first Physical Education History (《中国体育史》), published by Commercial Press with a preface by childhood friend Ye Shengtao.
- Joined the New Culture Movement; became a contributor to "晨报副刊" in Beijing in 1919, auditing courses at Peking University.
- In 1921, co-founded the "Literary Research Association" (文学研究会) with Zheng Zhenduo, Mao Dun, Ye Shengtao, and others on New Year's Day—one of the most famous literary societies in modern Chinese literary history.
- Began university teaching in 1921 at Fujian Xiehe University, recommended by Hu Shi and Gu Jiegang.
- Taught at Yenching University from 1927 to 1941 (14 years), where he began researching and writing "The History of Chinese Literary Criticism" (《中国文学批评史》)—upper volume published 1934, lower volume 1947.
- Refused to collaborate with Japanese occupation forces during WWII; wrote "高调歌" (Song of High Tune) in response to critics who mocked his refusal to teach at the puppet Peking University.
- After the war, taught at Tongji University (1946) and then Fudan University (1950 onward) as professor and department chair of Chinese; also served as library director and head of ancient literature research.
- Joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1956; donated a 99-room house he built in Suzhou to the state.
- Died in 1984.

Major academic contributions:
- His "History of Chinese Literary Criticism" is widely recognized as the most systematic and profound work in the field; Zhu Ziqing (1934) called him the first to systematically gather materials for this discipline and praised his work as a pioneering creation.
- Compiled "宋诗话辑佚" (1937, reprinted 1970s) and "宋诗话考" (1979), making foundational contributions to the study of Song dynasty poetry criticism.
- Authored over 20 works including "沧浪诗话校释", "汉语语法修辞新探", and edited "中国历代文论选" and "清诗话续编".
- Also researched grammar and rhetoric, arguing for integrating grammar, rhetoric, and vocabulary to reveal the distinctive features of Chinese.
- Advocated studying classical literature with scientific methods, influenced by Hu Shi's approach of "researching problems, importing theory, reorganizing national heritage."
- Divided the history of Chinese literary criticism into three periods (evolution, restoration, completion) in his early framework; later revised using socialist realist frameworks, though he found these revisions difficult.
- Advocated the "狂狷" (wild and stubborn) personality ideal—embracing both the aggressive "狂" and the principled restraint of "狷"—as a stance against sycophancy and opportunism among intellectuals.

Notable figures mentioned: Zheng Zhenduo, Mao Dun, Ye Shengtao, Gu Jiegang, Qu Qiubai, Hu Shi, Feng Youlan, Zhu Ziqing, Wen Yiduo, Qian Zhongshu, Wang Yuanhua, Chen Yunjie, Tang Tao, and others.
args.key_excerpts: "各人性分所限，未可一致，只须淡泊而不躁进，有正义感而不抹煞良心，自然不会帮凶；处事认真，生活严肃，自然也不会帮闲。不帮凶，不帮闲，虽不曾做到十足的积极的斗士，至少也可以说是不会与斗士背道而驰的。" (Guo Shaoyu on the "狷性" personality, in his memorial essay for Zhu Ziqing)

# 郭绍虞

最后更新：2023-11-23作者：访问量：385

郭绍虞（1893—1984），江苏苏州人，原名希汾，字绍虞。“五四”时期加入新潮社，20年代初，与茅盾、叶圣陶等创立文学研究会。建国后任复旦大学中文系主任、上海文联副主席、上海作协副主席、上海语文学会副会长、《辞海》副主编。同济大学文学院前院长，复旦大学首批博士生导师之一。郭绍虞为中国文学批评史学科的创建和发展做出了贡献，同时旁及古今语法修辞。书法也有精深造诣，为海内外学者所尊崇。

This is a page from the Fudan University Library website providing biographical and bibliographic information about Guo Shaoyu (郭绍虞, 1893–1984), a renowned Chinese literary scholar from Suzhou, Jiangsu. The page includes his biography and a comprehensive bibliography of 25+ works by or related to him, spanning from the 1920s through the 1980s.

Key biographical facts: Guo Shaoyu (original name Xifen, courtesy name Shaoyu) was born in 1893 in Suzhou, Jiangsu. He joined the Xinchao Society (新潮社) during the May Fourth Movement era, and in the early 1920s co-founded the Literary Research Association (文学研究会) with Mao Dun and Ye Shengtao. After 1949, he served as head of the Chinese Department at Fudan University, Vice Chairman of the Shanghai Federation of Literary and Art Circles, Vice Chairman of the Shanghai Writers' Association, Vice President of the Shanghai Linguistics Society, and Deputy Editor-in-Chief of the Cihai dictionary. He also served as former Dean of the College of Liberal Arts at Tongji University and was among the first group of doctoral supervisors at Fudan University. He is credited with founding and developing the discipline of Chinese literary criticism history in China, and also made contributions to grammar and rhetoric studies. He was also a highly regarded calligrapher.

The bibliography includes notable works such as:
- 中国文学批评史 (History of Chinese Literary Criticism), first published by Commercial Press in 1934, with revised editions in 1947 and 1979 (Shanghai Classics Publishing House)
- 宋诗话辑佚 (Collection of Lost Song Dynasty Poetry Notes), published by Harvard-Yenching Institute in 1937 and Zhonghua Book Company in 1980
- 中国历代文论选 (Selected Literary Theories Across Chinese Dynasties), edited by Guo, published in 1962 and 1979
- 宋诗话考 (Studies on Song Dynasty Poetry Notes), Zhonghua Book Company, 1979
- 汉语语法修辞新探 (New Explorations in Chinese Grammar and Rhetoric), Commercial Press, 1979 (two volumes)
- 沧浪诗话校释 (Annotated Canglang Poetry Notes), by Yan Yu, annotated by Guo, People's Literature Publishing House, 2nd edition 1983
- 清诗话续编 (Continuation of Qing Dynasty Poetry Notes), 1983
- 照隅室古典文学论集 (Collected Essays on Classical Literature from Zhaoyu Studio), 1983
- 中国近代文论选 (Selected Modern Chinese Literary Theories), co-edited with Luo Genze, 1959
- Other works include translations, textbooks (学文示例), and works on language studies (语文通论, 语文通论续编)

The page also contains the library's full navigation menu covering resources (catalog, databases, e-journals, e-books), services (borrowing, interlibrary loan, reference, thesis submission), guides, interactive features, professional master's programs, and branch libraries (Medical Library, Li Zhaoyi Library, Zhangjiang Library).

郭绍虞（1893年—1984年），名希汾，字绍虞，生于江苏[苏州](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%8B%8F%E5%B7%9E/122945?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，中国著名的教育家、古典文学家、语言学家、书法家，[复旦大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%A4%8D%E6%97%A6%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/111790?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教授， [1][中国科学院](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E9%99%A2/271375?fromModule=lemma_inlink)学部委员。 [2][中共党员](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%85%B1%E5%85%9A%E5%91%98/61543433?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，[民盟](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B0%91%E7%9B%9F/1971441?fromModule=lemma_inlink)成员。 [3]和[陈望道](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%99%88%E6%9C%9B%E9%81%93/990283?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[朱东润](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%9C%B1%E4%B8%9C%E6%B6%A6/7613154?fromModule=lemma_inlink)等并称为“复旦大学中文系十老” [5]。

1915年后历任上海进步书局编辑，上海[尚公小学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%B0%9A%E5%85%AC%E5%B0%8F%E5%AD%A6/22551051?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、启秀女中（今[启秀实验中学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%AF%E7%A7%80%E5%AE%9E%E9%AA%8C%E4%B8%AD%E5%AD%A6/121118?fromModule=lemma_inlink)）、[东亚体育专科学校](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%9C%E4%BA%9A%E4%BD%93%E8%82%B2%E4%B8%93%E7%A7%91%E5%AD%A6%E6%A0%A1/10228036?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教师，福州协和大学（今[福建师范大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%A6%8F%E5%BB%BA%E5%B8%88%E8%8C%83%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/662760?fromModule=lemma_inlink)）教授、系主任，开封[中州大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%B7%9E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/69700?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教授，[北平燕京大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8C%97%E5%B9%B3%E7%87%95%E4%BA%AC%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/12578620?fromModule=lemma_inlink)教授、主任。 [3]他因不愿加入日伪接管的北大，曾一度在私立[中国大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/5004972?fromModule=lemma_inlink)任教。1942年返上海，在[开明书店](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%BC%80%E6%98%8E%E4%B9%A6%E5%BA%97/1710278?fromModule=lemma_inlink)任编辑。此后在上海[大夏大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%A4%A7%E5%A4%8F%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/6255461?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[之江大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B9%8B%E6%B1%9F%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/6255538?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[光华大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%85%89%E5%8D%8E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/6255498?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[同济大学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%8C%E6%B5%8E%E5%A4%A7%E5%AD%A6/133590?fromModule=lemma_inlink)任中文系教授兼主任。 [2]

1950年，全国[高等学校院系调整](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%AB%98%E7%AD%89%E5%AD%A6%E6%A0%A1%E9%99%A2%E7%B3%BB%E8%B0%83%E6%95%B4/22559198?fromModule=lemma_inlink)，同济大学文学院并入复旦大学后，到复旦大学任教，先后任中文系教授兼主任、图书馆馆长、文学研究室主任等职。1956年加入中国共产党。先后兼任[华东军政委员会](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8D%8E%E4%B8%9C%E5%86%9B%E6%94%BF%E5%A7%94%E5%91%98%E4%BC%9A/3570437?fromModule=lemma_inlink)监察委员，上海文联副主席，中国作家协会上海分会副主席兼书记处书记、上海文学所所长和《辞海》副主编、《上海文学》编委等职。 [2]复旦大学首批博士生导师之一。 [4]

郭绍虞主要致力于[中国古典文学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E5%8F%A4%E5%85%B8%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6/3088630?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、中国文学批评史、中国语言学、[音韵学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%9F%B3%E9%9F%B5%E5%AD%A6/2342182?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、[训诂学](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%AE%AD%E8%AF%82%E5%AD%A6/3815210?fromModule=lemma_inlink)、书法 、理论等方面的研究。著有《[中国文学批评史](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E6%89%B9%E8%AF%84%E5%8F%B2/1875466?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《[沧浪诗话校释](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E6%B2%A7%E6%B5%AA%E8%AF%97%E8%AF%9D%E6%A0%A1%E9%87%8A/1799595?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《宋诗话考》《宋诗话辑佚》。郭绍虞先生以照隅室作为斋名。晚年印有《[照隅室古典文学论集](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%85%A7%E9%9A%85%E5%AE%A4%E5%8F%A4%E5%85%B8%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E8%AE%BA%E9%9B%86/8931975?fromModule=lemma_inlink)》《照隅室语言文字论集》《照隅室杂著》三种。 [4]

《中国文学批评史》由郭绍虞撰写，初版上卷于1934年由商务印书馆出版，经胡适审核列为民国教育部大学用书，下卷分两册于1947年完成。郭绍虞是中国文学批评史学科奠基人之一，与罗根泽、朱东润并称“华岳三峰”。2010年商务印书馆将上下卷合并重版，收录于《中华现代学术名著丛书》，系统梳理先秦至清中叶中国文学理论发展脉络。全书分上下两卷：上卷聚焦周秦至北宋文学观念的演变，分析儒家、道家思想对《文赋》《文心雕龙》等经典文论的影响，呈现文学性质从混沌到解析的过程；下卷探讨南宋至清中叶诗话、古文运动的体系化发展，解析格调说、性灵说等理论形态。著作以思想源流考辨结合文本细读，揭示文学批评与哲学思潮、文体演变的互动关系。郭绍虞运用“旧学系统法”，以“以问题为纲”的方式展开研究。其分期依据是文学观念的演变，将中国文学批评史分为文学观念演进期、文学观念复古期与文学批评完成期三个阶段。](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E6%96%87%E5%AD%A6%E6%89%B9%E8%AF%84%E5%8F%B2/1875466?lemmaFrom=lemma_starMap&fromModule=lemma_starMap&starNodeId=5c3a2427cfa7902dcb712533&lemmaIdFrom=1075971)

徐森玉（1881年8月17日—1971年5月19日），名鸿宝，字森玉，以字行，浙江吴兴（今浙江省湖州市南浔区）人。中国文物鉴定家、金石学家、版本学家、目录学家、文献学家。徐森玉毕业于山西大学堂（今山西大学），历任奉天、江苏工业学校监督，教育部俞事，北京大学图书馆馆长，故宫博物院古物馆馆长。生平致力于目录，版本、校勘学研究和古文物鉴定。抗日战争时期，为国家迁运故宫文物至西南，迁运居延汉简往香港，抢救《赵城藏》唐人写经等，并协助张咏霓、郑振铎等在上海抢救和保护善本图书，将抢救之珍本护送往重庆、香港等地，多有劳绩。建国后，曾任上海市文物保管委员会主任，上海博物馆馆长，第二、三届全国人大代表。周恩来总理称他为“国宝”。1971年5月19日不幸含冤辞世。徐森玉一生为查访、发掘中国的文物奔走天南地北，发现大同的辽代古寺、赵城的元代戏台、房山石经山唐代地契、北京的元代阿拉伯式浴池、蓟县唐代寺庙、三门峡摩崖石刻等，尤其是赵城古寺藏的多达44卷的石刻大藏经，更是稀世之珍宝。为国家征集鉴定大量具有重要价值的文物，其中有晋代王献之，宋代司马光、苏轼的真迹，春秋、战国和商代的青铜器，殷墟出土的一批甲骨片，秦汉以来的不少帝皇印玺等。居沪30余年，积集书籍15000余册。在他主持下，出版《上海博物馆藏书》《中国丛书综录》等。](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%BE%90%E6%A3%AE%E7%8E%89/2820589?lemmaFrom=lemma_starMap&fromModule=lemma_starMap&starNodeId=08b8cb851d69d863d33764d8&lemmaIdFrom=1075971)[![Image 吕思勉（1884年2月27日—1957年10月9日），字诚之，笔名驽牛、程芸、芸等，江苏省常州市人。中国近代历史学家、国学大师。代表作品有《白话本国史》《吕著中国通史》《秦汉史》《先秦史》等。1884年2月27日，吕思勉出生于常州的书香门第，16岁起，自学古史典籍。1914年7月，进中华书局当编辑。1918年，经介绍去沈阳高等师范学校任教。1923年，吕思勉出版《白话本国史》四册，是较早的一部有系统的中国通史，对当时史学界很有影响，后又著成《吕著中国通史》两册。1923年，应校长王饮鹤聘，赴江苏第一师范学校执教。1926年，前往光华大学任教。晚年从事断代史研究，先后出版有《先秦史》、《秦汉史》、《魏晋南北朝史》、《隋唐五代史》等著作。1951年起，任华东师范大学教授。1957年10月9日，吕思勉逝世。吕思勉是中国现代史学界一位重要人物。他用新思想、新观点、新方法研究历史，开创通史写作新纪元，在中国通史、断代史、各类专史等领域都有重大建树。一生的著述达1000万字以上，其中《先秦史》《秦汉史》《两晋南北朝史》《隋唐五代史》这4部断代史达300多万字，是他以一人之力完成的中国断代史著述，被史学界称为“通贯各时代，周瞻各领域”之巨著。](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%95%E6%80%9D%E5%8B%89/119263?lemmaFrom=lemma_starMap&fromModule=lemma_starMap&starNodeId=08b8cb851d69d863d33764d8&lemmaIdFrom=1075971)[![Image 陈望道（1891年1月18日—1977年10月29日），男，汉族，中共党员，民盟盟员，浙江金华义乌人。原名参一，单名融，字任重，笔名佛突、雪帆、晓风、张华等，是中国现代著名的思想家、社会活动家、教育家和语言学家，旷世巨著《辞海》总主编。他是《共产党宣言》第一个完整中译本的译者，中国共产党早期组织的发起人之一（中共重要创始人之一），五四新文化运动的积极推动者，亦是中国现代修辞学的奠基者和泰斗（修辞学之父）、中国语文现代化的先驱、现代新闻教育的开拓者之一，被誉为“千秋巨笔，一代宗师”。曾留学日本早稻田大学，学成回国后在浙江第一师范学校任教，后又返回故乡翻译《共产党宣言》。1920年5月，他前往上海，任《新青年》编辑，又与陈独秀、李汉俊、李达等酝酿组建上海马克思主义研究会，参与发起组建中国共产党。中国共产党成立后，他出任中共上海地方委员会第一任书记，后因与陈独秀发生矛盾而退党。此后，他以党外身份为党工作，并在上海大学、复旦大学、中华艺术大学等校任教，于1952年10月被毛泽东任命为复旦大学校长。1949年10月1日，作为特别邀请代表，与开国领袖一起登上天安门城楼参与并见证了新中国的诞生。1949年后，陈望道历任全国人大常委、全国政协常委、民盟中央副主席、民盟上海市委主委、中国科学院哲学社会科学部委员（院士）等职。1957年6月，陈望道直接由中央批准回到党内。](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E9%99%88%E6%9C%9B%E9%81%93/990283?lemmaFrom=lemma_starMap&fromModule=lemma_starMap&starNodeId=08b8cb851d69d863d33764d8&lemmaIdFrom=1075971)[![Image 吴蕴瑞（1892～1976），字麟若，江苏江阴人，著名体育家。先后毕业于南京高等师范学校体育专修科、国立东南大学体育系、哥伦比亚大学。吴蕴瑞是中国运动生物力学研究的先驱，在教学过程中开僻了运动生物力学的研究领域。吴蕴瑞是中国现代体育教育事业的开拓者，数十年中培养了众多体育界的栋梁之才。吴蕴瑞长期担任中国现代体育教育的发祥地南京大学（中央大学）体育系主任，也是中华人民共和国建立的第一所体育高等学校上海体育学院（华东体育学院）的创始人。](https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%90%B4%E8%95%B4%E7%91%9E/2767400?lemmaFrom=lemma_starMap&fromModule=lemma_starMap&starNodeId=08b8cb851d69d863d33764d8&lemmaIdFrom=1075971)
