--- SOURCE 5: 余冠英：为人民做学问的古典文史专家-中国社会科学网 ---
URL: https://www.cssn.cn/skgz/bwyc/202511/t20251117_5949548.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage, from the Chinese Social Sciences Network (中国社会科学网), is a tribute article about Yu Guanying (余冠英, 1906–1995), a renowned scholar of Chinese classical literature. Published on November 17, 2025, by authors Liu Ming and Li Xuyang from the Institute of Literature at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the article commemorates Yu's lifelong dedication to popularizing classical Chinese literary works for the public.

Yu Guanying taught at Southwest Associated University and Tsinghua University, where his scholarly approach was influenced by Zhu Ziqing. His work emphasized the "realist spirit" and "people's character" (人民性) of Chinese literature, following the principle that "the secret to all successful work is consulting with the masses" (一切工作成功的秘诀就是和大众商量).

Key achievements highlighted:
1. In 1950, Yu completed "Selection of Yuefu Poetry" (《乐府诗选》), published by People's Literature Publishing House in 1953—one of New China's earliest classical literature readers aimed at popularizing literary heritage. It received high praise from Zhu Guangqian, Sun Wang, and Wang Yunxi.
2. Between 1954–1959, he published "Selection of the Book of Songs" (《诗经选》), "Selection of the Three Cao's Poetry" (《三曹诗选》), and "Selection of Han, Wei, and Six Dynasties Poetry" (《汉魏六朝诗选》), plus contributing to "Selection of Tang Poetry" (《唐诗选》).
3. He served as researcher and head of the Chinese Classical Literature Research Group at the Institute of Literature (established 1953, transferred to the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 1955).
4. He was responsible for compiling the pre-Tang section of the "History of Chinese Literature" (《中国文学史》), published in 1962.

His distinctive selection and annotation methodology combined textual research (考据), moral principles (义理), and rhetoric (辞章), with concise annotations and poetic commentary. His work established the "China Classical Literature Reading Series" as an academic milestone of the 1950s. The article emphasizes Yu's legacy as a pioneer in making classical Chinese literature accessible to ordinary readers while maintaining scholarly rigor—a model of "doing scholarship for the people" (为人民做学问).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"一切工作成功的秘诀就是和大众商量" (The secret to all successful work is consulting with the masses) — from the afterword of Yu Guanying's "Selected Translation of the Book of Songs", cited in the article as reflecting his scholarly philosophy.
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 6: 王季思 - 维基百科，自由的百科全书 ---
URL: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E7%8E%8B%E5%AD%A3%E6%80%9D

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Chinese Wikipedia biography page about Wang Jisi (王季思), a prominent Chinese opera (戏曲) scholar. Wang Jisi (1906–1996), whose given name was Wang Qi (王起) and courtesy name Jisi (季思), was a native of Yongjia County, Zhejiang Province (now Ouhai District, Wenzhou City). He served as a literature professor in the Chinese Department of Sun Yat-sen University (中山大學).

**Early Life:** Wang was a descendant of the prominent Wang Che family of Yongjia. He was well-read in classical texts from childhood and had a passion for opera and fiction. He entered Zhejiang Provincial No. 10 Middle School before finishing primary school. In 1925, he enrolled in the Literature Department of National Southeast University (國立東南大學), studying under the renowned opera master Wu Mei (吳梅). Wu Mei praised him highly, writing on one of his assignments: "Since Wanli, Yuting, and Weizhao left, I have gained this talent again; my heart is overjoyed!"

**Teaching Career:** After graduation, he taught at Zhejiang Provincial No. 10 Middle School and Jiangsu Provincial Songjiang Women's Middle School. After the August 13 Battle (八一三戰爭) broke out, he returned home to participate in anti-Japanese resistance work. He later taught at universities in Guizhou and at Zhejiang University in Hangzhou. He subsequently taught at Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou for a long period until his death.

**Political Persecution:** During the Criticize Lin, Criticize Confucius Movement (批林批孔運動), Wang Jisi was labeled a "reactionary academic authority" (反动学术权威) and was persecuted as a result.

**Family:** His son, Wang Zeke (王則柯), also taught at Sun Yat-sen University.

- Yu and his wife shared a genuine love for Kunqu opera. From 1956 to 1964, Yu led the Beijing Kunqu Research Society (北京昆曲研习社), contributing to the preservation of Kunqu.
- The article concludes with Yu's "养生歌谣" (health preservation song): "Happy labor brings good spirit, adequate rest protects the brain. Long-term exercise strengthens the body, moderate entertainment brings no worries..." The author relates Yu's "innocence" to the Daoist philosophy of "naturalness" (自然), citing Laozi's teaching that water is the most yielding yet most powerful force—innocence, like water, is invincible in matters of longevity.

The author is an editor at the Chinese Social Sciences Press (中国社会科学出版社).

SUMMARY:

This article from Jiangsu Writers' Network (江苏作家网) commemorates the 121st anniversary of the birth of Yu Pingbo (俞平伯, 1900–1990), a renowned Chinese literary scholar, poet, and Redology (红楼梦研究) expert. Written from the perspective of the author's reading of the "Wang Boxiang Diary" (《王伯祥日记》), the piece chronicles the friendship between Yu Pingbo and Wang Boxiang (王伯祥), two scholars who worked together at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences Institute of Literature.

Key biographical facts: Yu Pingbo was born in Suzhou to a family from Deqing County, Zhejiang. His great-grandfather was the famous Qing dynasty scholar Yu Yue (俞樾). He entered Peking University in 1915, published his first new-style poem "Spring Water" (《春水》) in the New Youth magazine in 1918, joined the New Tide Society, and was a participant in the May Fourth Movement. He published his first poetry collection "Winter Night" (《冬夜》) in 1922 and joined the Literary Research Society in 1921.

The article details the founding of the Institute of Literature in 1952–1953, when Yu Pingbo and Wang Boxiang participated in its preparation under Zheng Zhenduo's leadership. Yu was assigned to annotate the Book of Songs (《诗经选》) while Wang worked on the Records of the Grand Historian (《史记选》).

A major focus is the 1954 campaign criticizing Yu Pingbo's "A Study of the Dream of the Red Chamber" (《红楼梦研究》), which began with critiques by Li Xifan and Lan Ling in October 1954. The article uses Wang Boxiang's diary entries from October–December 1954 to document the intense criticism sessions at the Institute, the pressure on Yu, and the mutual support between the two elderly friends—including a memorable outing to Beihai Park and a mutton barbecue meal in November 1954, after which Yu composed a poem expressing gratitude for Wang's friendship during his hardship.

The article also covers: the 1956 researcher ranking system, where He Qifang (何其芳) insisted Yu Pingbo be rated as a first-class researcher despite the criticism he faced (Yu reportedly responded "差不多,差不多" - "roughly right"); Yu's later years maintaining private interest in the Red Chamber Dream despite public silence on the topic; Wang Boxiang's death in December 1975; and Yu's tribute elegy. The piece concludes with reflections on the scholarly virtues of Yu Pingbo's generation—their rigorous academic spirit, sincere character, and warm approach to life.

--- SOURCE 1: 唐圭璋，活成了一代词宗，也活成了一代情圣-青岛唐氏宗亲网 ---
URL: https://www.qdtang.cn?hygl%2F504.html=

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the Qingdao Tang Clan Association website (青岛唐氏宗亲网, qdtang.cn) and contains a detailed biographical article about Tang Guizhang (唐圭璋, 1901-1990), a renowned Chinese ci (词) poetry scholar affectionately known as "一代词宗" (a generation's master of ci poetry) and "一代情圣" (a generation's romantic devoted one).

**Biographical Overview:**
- Born January 23, 1901, in Nanjing to a Manchu (满族) bannerman family. Lost his father at age 7 and mother at age 11, raised by others. Two key benefactors: Principal Chen Rongzhi of Qiwangjie Primary School (who waived all fees) and Principal Qiu Cai of the Provincial Fourth Normal School.
- Entered National Southeast University's Chinese Department in 1922, studied under renowned ci master Wu Mei (吴梅). Became one of "吴门三杰" (Three Outstanding Students of Wu Mei) alongside Ren Zhongmin and Lu Qian, excelling specifically in ci studies.
- Graduated 1928, taught at various institutions including Jiangsu First Girls' Middle School, Central Military Academy, Central University (Chongqing/Chengdu during wartime), Jinling University, Northeast Normal University, and finally Nanjing Normal University (1953-1990) as professor and doctoral supervisor.
- Died November 28, 1990, at age 89, in his tiny study "Mengtong Zhai" (梦桐斋) of less than 8 square meters.

**Major Academic Works (20+ volumes, over 10 million characters):**
- 《全宋词》(Complete Ci of the Song Dynasty)
- 《全金元词》(Complete Ci of Jin and Yuan Dynasties)
- 《词话丛编》(Compilation of Ci Commentaries — revised 1986 edition by Zhonghua Book Company, 5 volumes, 85 ci commentaries, nearly 4 million characters)
- 《宋词三百首笺注》、《南唐二主词汇笺》、《唐宋词简释》、《宋词四考》、《宋词纪事》、《梦桐词》、《词学论丛》 and others.

**Teaching Style:** Like his mentor Wu Mei, he brought a flute to class and would sing ci poems and opera excerpts in Kunqu style to deepen students' understanding.

**"重拙大" (Heavy, Plain, Grand) Theory:** Tang was influenced by Wang Pengyun and Kuang Zhouyi, using "重拙大" as the standard for selecting and annotating Tang-Song ci poems in his 《唐宋词简释》, which includes 67 poets and 232 poems (56 Tang, 176 Song). He also proposed the four principles of "雅婉厚亮" (elegant, gentle, substantial, bright) for ci composition.

**Personal Life and Tragedy:**
- Married Yin Xiaozeng (尹孝曾), a young lady from the Yin family garden in Lijixiang, Nanjing. Their marriage was happy; he played the flute under the wutong tree while she fanned him on summer nights.
- Yin died on Lunar New Year's Eve 1936. Tang never remarried and mourned her for the rest of his life, visiting her grave with flute, books, and simple food for entire days.
- Suffered all three of life's great misfortunes: orphaned young, widowed in middle age, and losing his daughters Tang Dihua (d. 1967) and Tang Diyi (d. 1956), leaving him to raise grandchildren as an elderly man.
- His 《梦桐词》 (133 poems, 61 written during the Anti-Japanese War) was named "Mengtong" (Dream Wutong) partly to memorialize his late wife (referencing the "half-dead wutong tree" from Mei Cheng's 《七发》) and partly for his homesickness during the war years.

**Quotes:** In a 1984 letter he wrote: "词作通俗，可谓白话词，实不足与前贤相比，由于我身世凄凉少无父母，中年丧偶，晚年丧女所写每聊记梦痕而已" (My ci poems are plain, mere vernacular verse, not comparable to the ancients; because my life has been desolate — no parents in youth, widowed in middle age, losing daughters in old age — I merely record traces of dreams).

The article also references content from 《"情圣"词宗唐圭璋》 by Zhao Puguang of Nanjing Normal University. The site includes navigation for news, genealogy, notable figures, cultural relics, and contact information (phone: 18661637226, WeChat: 103317480).
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"唐圭璋：1901-1990，字季特。南京人。我国著名词学家、文学家，被誉为'一代词宗'。", "人们常说，人生三大不幸是幼年丧怙，中年丧偶，老年丧子。然而这三不幸竟然全降临在一人身上。", "先生《论词之作法》云：'雅清新纯正；婉温柔缠绵；厚沉郁顿挫；亮名隽高华'。'雅婉厚亮'四字，凝聚了先生多年的研究心得和创作体验。", "词作通俗，可谓白话词，实不足与前贤相比，由于我身世凄凉少无父母，中年丧偶，晚年丧女所写每聊记梦痕而已。", "1986年中华书局出版《词话丛编》(修订本)精装五大册，增补了25种，共计85种词话，近400万字，集历代词话之大成，为我国词学史上矗立了一座丰碑。"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 从双林巷走出的曲学宗师吴梅 - 苏州市地方志编纂委员会办公室 ---
URL: https://dfzb.suzhou.gov.cn/dfzb/fzxh/200909/952cf8b7d8d440a2a4b4df77d3b8235c.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage from the Suzhou Local Chronicles (苏州地方志) website presents a detailed biographical and scholarly article about Wu Mei (吴梅, 1884-1939), a renowned Chinese opera (qu) master from Shuanglin Lane (双林巷) in Suzhou. The article is divided into four main sections covering his life, his research in qu studies, his dramatic works, and his students.

**Wu Mei's Life:** Born in 1884 in Changzhou County (now Suzhou), Jiangsu Province, Wu Mei came from a distinguished family (his great-grandfather Wu Zhongjun was a top imperial exam candidate in 1832). He experienced early family tragedy—his father died when he was 3, his mother when he was 10. He was adopted by his great-uncle Wu Changxiang. At age 12, he began studying under Pan Xiake, and despite failing the imperial exams, he developed a passion for ci poetry and early opera works like Wang Shifu's "The Romance of the Western Chamber." He began writing opera at age 17 (1901) with his first work "Fengdongshan." He taught at numerous institutions including Peking University, Southeast University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Central University. During the Sino-Japanese War, he fled with his family through multiple cities, eventually dying in Yunnan in March 1939 at age 56.

**Wu Mei's Qu Studies:** Wu Mei is considered one of the two greatest Chinese drama scholars of the early 20th century, alongside Wang Guowei (王国维). While Wang Guowei focused on historical research, Wu Mei excelled in the practical and theoretical study of qu itself—composing, notating, performing, and analyzing the art form. His major works include "Gugu Chen Tan" (顾曲麈谈), "Chinese Opera Overview" (中国戏曲概论), and "Southern and Northern Ci Simplified Notation" (南北词简谱, a 20-year project covering 1,108 musical modes). He was also a performer who appeared on stage in roles from famous plays and mentored celebrated actors including Mei Lanfang.

**Dramatic Works:** Wu Mei wrote approximately 10 surviving plays including "Fengdongshan" (his early revolutionary masterpiece about the Southern Ming resistance hero Qu Shisi), "Xuehuafei" (about the Six Gentlemen of the 1898 Reform Movement, later destroyed by his grandfather), "Luoyinji" and "Shuangleibei" (addressing women's rights issues), and his "Shuangya Sanju" trilogy including "Xiangzhenge," "Wujiabao," and "Chouchangcuan" (his most mature work, a four-play set about Tang and Song dynasty poets).

**His Students:** Wu Mei trained a remarkable generation of scholars including Ren Zhongmin (founder of the discipline of sanqu studies), Lu Qian, Tang Guizhang (famous for compiling "Complete Song Ci" / 全宋词), Wang Jisi (noted for annotating "The Romance of the Western Chamber"), Qian Nanyang (a leading scholar of Southern opera), Cai Ying, and Wan Yunjun, among others. Many of his students became leading figures in Chinese classical literature and opera studies.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"近世对于戏曲一门学问，最有研究者推王静安先生与吴先生两人。静安先生在历史考证方面，开戏曲史研究之先路，但在戏曲本身之研究，还当推瞿安先生独步……" (Pu Jiangqing's assessment that Wang Guowei led historical research but Wu Mei was unrivaled in the study of opera itself), "凡学问有为潮流所趋者，有为时代所弃者，有赖书本文献足以传后者，有非接近其人、得其指点不能妙悟者……今从先生游者尚不能尽其所学，况后世但读其书者乎？" (from Pu Jiangqing's memorial to Wu Mei), "吴梅'藏曲之富，海内无与伯仲'，但他并不居为奇货，秘不示人" (Wu Mei's collection of opera works was unmatched in China, yet he freely shared it), "特是曲学之兴，国维治之三年，未若吴梅之劬以毕生；国维限于元曲，未若吴梅之集其大成；国维评其历史，未若吴梅之发其条例；国维赏其文学，未若吴梅之析其声律。而论曲学者，并世要推吴梅为大师云！" (Qian Jibo's comparison of Wu Mei and Wang Guowei, concluding Wu Mei was the greater master of qu studies), "一出戏救活了一个剧种" (Zhou Enlai's 1956 comment on Kunqu opera, connecting to Wu Mei's legacy)
</key_excerpts>

2. **Curriculum Contributions**: Zhu established a five-year curriculum plan with one major (Chinese Language and Literature) and two specializations (Chinese Literature and Chinese Language). 3. **Teaching Style**: Zhu taught "History of Chinese Literary Criticism" to fourth-year students, following his 1944 book "大纲" (Outline of the History of Chinese Literary Criticism) published by Kaiming Bookstore. Zhu Ziqing called his book "China's first concise complete history of Chinese literary criticism." Guo Shaoyu is considered the pioneer and Zhu Dongrun one of the founders of Chinese literary criticism studies.

The lecture discusses the life and career of Zhu Dongrun (朱东润, 1897-?), a renowned Chinese scholar, calligrapher, and pioneering figure in Chinese biographical literature. Key points covered include:

- Zhu Dongrun was born in 1897 in Taixing County, northern Jiangsu Province, into a poor family (his father was a shop clerk). He survived being abandoned as an infant due to family poverty.
- His educational journey: he attended Nanyang Public School (南洋公学, predecessor of Jiaotong University) in Shanghai as a companion/study partner for a wealthy relative; the school principal Tang Wenzhi (唐文治) paid his tuition after he excelled. - He worked as a language teacher at a normal school in Nantong (established by Zhang Jian/张謇), where he was discovered by Wen Yiduo (闻一多), dean of the Wuhan University College of Liberal Arts. Wen invited him to teach English and then Chinese, leading to his compilation of the influential textbook 《中国文学批评史大纲》(Outline of the History of Chinese Literary Criticism), which established his academic reputation.
- During the Japanese invasion (from 1937), he traveled alone from Shanghai through Hong Kong, Cambodia, and Vietnam to rejoin Wuhan University, which had relocated to Leshan, Sichuan.
- In 1952 he joined Fudan University (复旦大学) in Shanghai, where he served as head of the Chinese Department for many years (including after his rehabilitation from the Cultural Revolution at age 80).
- He lived to age 92, attributed partly to his daily calligraphy practice. A collection of his calligraphy, 《朱东润书法作品选》, was published by Shanghai Calligraphy and Painting Publishing House in 1996.

- His autobiography 《八十年》(Eighty Years), published by the Eastern Publishing Center in 1999.
- His incomplete manuscript on Yuan Haowen was written even while hospitalized.

His biographical theory emphasized: choosing subjects with responsibility, character, and moral force; that both great and ordinary people could be biographical subjects (though practically great figures are more accessible); drawing on Western biographical traditions (Boswell's 'Life of Johnson', Strachey's 'Queen Victoria', Plutarch's 'Lives'); and using dialogue based on historical evidence. SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is an article from China Writer's Network (中国作家网), published by Wenhui Daily (文汇报) on August 15, 2021, by author Li Chunyi (李纯一). The article is a biographical tribute to Guo Shaoyu (郭绍虞, 1893–1984), a foundational figure in the establishment of the academic discipline of Chinese literary criticism history (中国文学批评史).

Key biographical details:
- Born in 1893 in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, to an impoverished scholarly family; dropped out of school in his second year of middle school due to financial hardship.
- Self-taught and worked as an elementary school teacher in Suzhou, Wuxi, and Shanghai. At the Commercial Press's Shanggong Elementary School (1914), he benefited from the Hanfenlou (涵芬楼) rare books collection.
- Compiled China's first Physical Education History (《中国体育史》), published by Commercial Press with a preface by childhood friend Ye Shengtao.
- Joined the New Culture Movement; became a contributor to "晨报副刊" in Beijing in 1919, auditing courses at Peking University.
- In 1921, co-founded the "Literary Research Association" (文学研究会) with Zheng Zhenduo, Mao Dun, Ye Shengtao, and others on New Year's Day—one of the most famous literary societies in modern Chinese literary history.
- Began university teaching in 1921 at Fujian Xiehe University, recommended by Hu Shi and Gu Jiegang.
- Taught at Yenching University from 1927 to 1941 (14 years), where he began researching and writing "The History of Chinese Literary Criticism" (《中国文学批评史》)—upper volume published 1934, lower volume 1947.
- Refused to collaborate with Japanese occupation forces during WWII; wrote "高调歌" (Song of High Tune) in response to critics who mocked his refusal to teach at the puppet Peking University.
- After the war, taught at Tongji University (1946) and then Fudan University (1950 onward) as professor and department chair of Chinese; also served as library director and head of ancient literature research.
- Joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1956; donated a 99-room house he built in Suzhou to the state.
- Died in 1984.

Major academic contributions:
- His "History of Chinese Literary Criticism" is widely recognized as the most systematic and profound work in the field; Zhu Ziqing (1934) called him the first to systematically gather materials for this discipline and praised his work as a pioneering creation.
- Compiled "宋诗话辑佚" (1937, reprinted 1970s) and "宋诗话考" (1979), making foundational contributions to the study of Song dynasty poetry criticism.
- Authored over 20 works including "沧浪诗话校释", "汉语语法修辞新探", and edited "中国历代文论选" and "清诗话续编".
- Also researched grammar and rhetoric, arguing for integrating grammar, rhetoric, and vocabulary to reveal the distinctive features of Chinese.
- Advocated studying classical literature with scientific methods, influenced by Hu Shi's approach of "researching problems, importing theory, reorganizing national heritage."
- Divided the history of Chinese literary criticism into three periods (evolution, restoration, completion) in his early framework; later revised using socialist realist frameworks, though he found these revisions difficult.
- Advocated the "狂狷" (wild and stubborn) personality ideal—embracing both the aggressive "狂" and the principled restraint of "狷"—as a stance against sycophancy and opportunism among intellectuals.

Notable figures mentioned: Zheng Zhenduo, Mao Dun, Ye Shengtao, Gu Jiegang, Qu Qiubai, Hu Shi, Feng Youlan, Zhu Ziqing, Wen Yiduo, Qian Zhongshu, Wang Yuanhua, Chen Yunjie, Tang Tao, and others.
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Baidu Baike (Chinese encyclopedia) entry for 郭绍虞 (Guo Shaoyu, 1893–1984), a renowned Chinese classical literature scholar, linguist, educator, calligrapher, and professor at Fudan University. He is considered a founding figure of the discipline of Chinese literary criticism history (中国文学批评史).

**Biography & Career:**
- Born November 21, 1893, in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province, to a poor scholarly family (grandfather was a Qing juren; father Guo Luqing was a clerk/tutor).
- Began teaching at Shanghai Shanggong Primary School (attached to Commercial Press) in 1913; influenced by the May Fourth Movement, joined the Xinchao Society, and became a special contributor to Beijing's "Morning Post" supplement (1919).
- Co-founded the Literary Research Association (文学研究会) in 1921 with Zheng Zhenduo, Wang Tongzhao, Shen Yanbing (Mao Dun), and Ye Shengtao.
- Held professorships at Fuzhou Xiehe University, Kaifeng Zhongzhou University, and Beijing Yenching University (1927–1941, a 14-year period of major academic work).
- During the Japanese occupation, he refused to cooperate with the puppet government, was imprisoned for two days for refusing to teach at the puppet Peking University, and delivered a famous "last lesson" reciting the "Shijing·Shu Li" before leaving.
- Served as editor at Kaiming Bookstore and taught at Daxia, Zhijiang, Guanghua, and Tongji Universities in Shanghai.
- Joined Fudan University in 1949/1950 after the department restructuring; served as Chinese department chair, library director, and literature research office director.
- Joined the Chinese Communist Party in 1956; held various posts including Vice Chairman of Shanghai Literature and Art Federation, Vice Chairman of the Shanghai branch of the Chinese Writers Association, Deputy Editor-in-Chief of "Cihai" dictionary, and first doctoral supervisor at Fudan.
- Elected first president of the Chinese Ancient Literature Theory Society in 1979.
- Died June 23, 1984, in Shanghai at age 91.
- Named one of the "Ten Elders" of Fudan University's Chinese Department alongside Chen Wangdao and Zhu Dongrun.

**Academic Contributions:**
1. **Chinese Literary Criticism History**: Published "中国文学批评史" (History of Chinese Literary Criticism) in 1934 (upper volume) and 1947 (lower volume); regarded as the discipline's foundational work — "the material and method are his own" (per Zhu Ziqing). Also wrote "宋诗话考" (Study of Song Dynasty Poetry Talks), "宋诗话辑佚" (Recovery of Lost Song Poetry Talks), "沧浪诗话校释" (Annotated Canglang Poetry Talks), and edited "中国历代文论选" (Selected Chinese Literary Criticism Through the Ages, 1962).
2. **Linguistics**: Works include "语文通论" (General Discourse on Language), "汉语语法修辞新探" (New Explorations in Chinese Grammar and Rhetoric), and research on proverbs, Chinese phonetics, character evolution, and function words.
3. **Calligraphy**: A skilled calligrapher with deep family tradition; wrote the preface to the famous "Peking Letter Paper" (北平笺谱) compiled by Lu Xun and Zheng Zhenduo; wrote over ten essays on calligraphy theory.

**Notable Students**: Yang Mingzhao, Jiang Fan, Ren Rongrong, Huang Baozhen.

**Major Works**: 中国文学批评史, 沧浪诗话校释, 宋诗话考, 宋诗话辑佚, 语文通论, 汉语语法修辞新探, 照隅室古典文学论集, 中国体育史 (1920), 近代文编 (1939), 学文示例 (1947), 开明新编国文读本, among others. His study was named 照隅室 (Zhaoyu Studio).

**Philosophy of Learning**: Believed scholarship requires both memory (记性) and insight/comprehension (悟性); advocated "将勤补拙" (making up for lack of talent with diligence).
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a biographical article from the China Association for Promoting Democracy (中国民主促进会, Mj.org.cn) website, published on February 2, 2026, from Wenhui Daily (文汇报), celebrating Liu Dajie (刘大杰, 1904–1977), a classical Chinese literature scholar renowned as "the most talented Chinese literary historian of the 20th century."

**Early Life and Education:** Liu Dajie was born in 1904 in a rural village in Yueyang, Hunan. His early life was marked by hardship—his father died early, the family was poor, and he worked as a child laborer. Despite this, he educated himself and gained admission to the free Hubei Traveling Middle School. His mother taught him The Three Hundred Tang Poems and The Tale of Heroes and Heroines before her death when he was 12, nurturing his literary interest. In 1922, he entered the Chinese Department at Wuchang Higher Normal School, where he studied under scholars including Huang Kan, Hu Xiaoshi, and Yu Dafu. Under Yu Dafu's encouragement, he began writing fiction—his first published work was "Temple of Peach Grove" (《桃林寺》), a story about escaping an arranged marriage, published in the Morning Post Supplement (《晨报副刊》).

**Literary and Translation Career:** Liu produced novels, plays, and short stories (including 《昨日之花》《三儿苦学记》《她病了》《十年后》《渺茫的西南风》《盲诗人》), praised by Yu Dafu for their "problem consciousness" addressing social issues. In 1926, he went to Japan for six years of study in European literature, translating works by Tolstoy, Jack London, Sienkiewicz, Dostoevsky, Turgenev, and Shelley, and writing monographs on Tolstoy, Ibsen, and German literature.

**Major Scholarly Work:** After returning to China, Liu taught at Fudan, Sichuan, Anhui, Daxia, and Jinan universities. During the Anti-Japanese War, he refused positions teaching Japanese and focused on writing. <summary>
## 金岳霖（Jin Yuelin）— 维基百科条目摘要

**基本信息：** 金岳霖（1895年7月14日—1984年10月19日），字龙荪，祖籍浙江诸暨草塔，生于湖南长沙。中国哲学家、逻辑学家。享年89岁。

**教育背景：**
- 1901年进入长沙私立明德学堂读四书五经
- 1907年进入美国教会创办的雅礼大学预科
- 后考入清华学堂（1912年改名清华学校）
- 1914年毕业于清华学校高等科，同年官费留美
- 1917年毕业于宾夕法尼亚大学
- 1920年获哥伦比亚大学政治学博士学位
- 1922年在伦敦大学经济学院听课

**学术生涯与任职：**
- 1925年11月回国，最初在北京中国大学任教
- 1926年受聘于清华大学，讲授西方政治思想和逻辑学
- 1926年秋与张东荪、张君劢共同创办清华大学哲学系，任教授、系主任
- 1938年任西南联大文学院心理学系教授兼清华大学哲学系主任
- 1948年当选中央研究院第一届院士（人文组）
- 1949年后任清华大学文学院院长
- 1952年全国高校院系调整后，历任北京大学哲学系教授、系主任（1952-1956年）
- 1955年被聘为中国科学院哲学社会科学部学部委员，任哲学研究所副所长兼逻辑研究组组长
- 1977年文革结束后任中国社会科学院副所长兼研究室主任
- 1979年中国逻辑学会成立，任首任会长和常务理事
- 1956年加入中国共产党；为中国民主同盟中央委员/常务委员；曾任国务院学位委员会第一届学科评议组成员

**代表作：**
- 1936年《逻辑》
- 1940年《论道》
- 1965年《罗素哲学批判》
- 1983年《知识论》
- 另出版《金岳霖学术论文选》《金岳霖文集》等

**学术贡献：** 金岳霖是最早把现代逻辑系统介绍到中国的主要人物，将西方哲学与中国哲学相结合，建立了独特哲学体系，培养了牟宗三、王浩、冯契、沈有鼎、殷海光等一批高素养人才。其受业弟子包括殷海光。

**文革遭遇：** 1966年文革开始后，金岳霖作为"资产阶级学术权威"被批斗，革命派不准其搭公车去医院看病，只能踩三轮木板车前往。

**家庭与轶事：**
- 父亲金珍原（浙江诸暨人，太平天国时期避乱至湖南长沙），母亲唐淑贤（湖南衡阳人）
- 因爱上林徽因而终生未娶；与梁思成、林徽因一家是邻居和挚友，晚年与梁从诫一家同住，梁从诫称其"金爸"，情同父子
- 曾与美籍女子Lilian (Lilyan) Taylor（中文名秦丽琳/秦丽莲）同居约五年（1925-1931年），1932年分手，丽琳后于1982年在洛杉矶去世

**政党/政治身份：** 中国民主同盟盟员，1956年加入中国共产党。

**荣誉与职位：** 中央研究院第一届院士（1948年）、中国科学院哲学社会科学部学部委员（1955年）、中国逻辑学会首任会长（1979年）、第二/三/五/六届全国政协委员、第三届全国人大代表。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
金岳霖（1895年7月14日—1984年10月19日），字龙荪，男，祖籍浙江诸暨草塔，生于湖南长沙，中国哲学家、逻辑学家。是最早把现代逻辑系统地介绍到中国来的主要人物。他把西方哲学与中国哲学相结合，建立了独特的哲学体系，培养了一大批高素养的哲学和逻辑学专门人才。著有：《逻辑》、《论道》和《知识论》。
</key_excerpts>

# 中国古典文学研究第一代学者知识背景调研——资料整理报告

## 一、查询与工具调用记录

本次调研通过tavily_search工具进行了多轮检索，查询内容包括：
1. 游国恩生平、北京大学毕业、留学、楚辞学术经历；钱锺书学历、清华大学、留学牛津
2. 冯沅君、陆侃如生平（北京大学、清华大学、师承吴梅）；林庚生平（清华、北大、楚辞、唐诗）；萧涤非生平（清华、汉魏六朝乐府、山东大学）
3. 余冠英生平（清华、汉魏六朝、社科院）；王季思生平（中山大学、戏曲、吴梅弟子）；俞平伯生平（北大、红楼梦）
4. 唐圭璋生平（中央大学、词学、吴梅弟子）；程千帆生平（金陵大学、武汉大学、南京大学、黄侃师承）；朱东润生平（毕业、留学英国、传记文学、复旦）
5. 郭绍虞生平（北大肄业、文学批评史、复旦、留学日本）；刘大杰生平（复旦、中国文学发展史、留学）；詹锳生平（西南联大、清华、河北大学、唐诗）

**重要说明：** 目前已完成游国恩、钱锺书、冯沅君、陆侃如、林庚、萧涤非、余冠英、王季思、俞平伯、唐圭璋、程千帆、朱东润、郭绍虞、刘大杰、詹锳等15位学者的信息收集。**隋树森、吴组缃、季镇淮、马茂元、刘永济、夏承焘、钱仲联、陈贻焮、王运熙、蒋天枢、苏雪林、施蛰存等学者仍需后续检索补充。**

---

## 二、全量发现

### （一）总体背景特征（跨学者综合信息）

#### 1. 1952年院系调整与学者流动
1952年全国高校院系调整中，清华大学文、理、法学院以及燕京大学各系并入北京大学。清华中文系教师调入北大的包括浦江清、吴组缃、余冠英、王瑶、季镇淮、郭良夫、冯钟芸、叶兢耕，以及来自燕京大学的林庚（本人是清华毕业生）；1954年王力从中山大学语言学系调入。[14] 王瑶1988年在清华大学"纪念朱自清诞生九十周年座谈会"上发言指出："现全国新成立了许多大学，为什么清华大学中文系就该取消呢？应该看到，清华中文系不仅是大学的一个系，而且是一个有鲜明特色的学派。"[14] 这批清华学人保留了清华人文学术传统，影响了其他院校的学术发展。[14]

#### 2. 清华学人与山东大学古典文学学科
高亨（1900-1986）、陆侃如（1903-1978）、萧涤非（1906-1991）三位清华毕业生在山东大学执教，塑造了20世纪山大古典文学学科。1950-60年代山东大学中文系以"冯陆高萧"四大名教授著称。三位清华学人将"朴学"传统和"清华学派"的"释古"理念带入山东大学。[23]

#### 3. 北京大学中文系"四老"与"清华四剑客"
林庚晚年与吴组缃、王瑶、季镇淮并称"北大中文四老"。[16][20] 林庚在清华期间与吴组缃、李长之、季羡林并称"清华四剑客"。[16][18][20]

#### 4. 社科院文学研究所的学术谱系
社科院文学研究所古代文学研究室将学者分为五代。第一代（1890年代-1910年代生）包括：王伯祥（1890-1975）、孙楷第（1898-1989，古典小说戏曲专家）、郑振铎（1898-1958）、俞平伯（1900-1990，红学家、俞樾曾孙）、陈友琴（1902-1996）、余冠英（1906-1995）、力扬（1908-1964）、吴世昌（1908-1986，曾任牛津讲师）、钱锺书（1910-1998）、何其芳（1912-1977）、汪蔚林（1912-1983）、吴晓铃（1914-1995）、范宁（1916-1997，闻一多学生）。[29] 邓绍基（1933-2013）1951年考入复旦大学中文系，1955年10月毕业后到文学研究所工作。[29] 王水照（b.1934）1955-1960年就读北大中文系，1960-1978年在文学研究所，在钱锺书、何其芳、余冠英等先生指导下参与《中国文学史》《唐诗选》等项目。[29]

#### 5. 西南联大的师承与学风
陈平原指出西南联大"最令人难忘的是学风，最值得珍惜的是师缘"。[68] 季镇淮（1913-1997）、王瑶（1914-1989）、吴宏聪（b.1918）分别师从闻一多（1899-1946）、朱自清（1898-1948）、杨振声（1891-1966）。季镇淮编《闻朱年谱》；闻一多曾为季镇淮、王瑶写四封推荐信给梅贻琦校长申请助教职位。闻一多的《"七十二"》一文属于"集体考据"，季镇淮提供了主要材料和意见，闻一多明确注明"主要的材料和主要的意见，还是镇淮的"。[68] 杨振声（哥伦比亚大学教育心理学毕业）是推动新文学进入大学课堂的关键人物。[68] 冯友兰评价西南联大时期："中国的大学教育，有了最高底表现。那个文学院的学术空气，我敢说比三校的任何时期都浓厚。教授学生，真是打成一片。"[68]

#### 6. 吴梅的学术传承网络
吴梅（1884-1939）是近代曲学宗师，第一个在高等学府专授戏曲课的教师，历任北京大学、中山大学、中央大学、金陵大学等校教授。[34][35] 钱基博评价："特是曲学之兴，国维治之三年，未若吴梅之劬以毕生；国维限于元曲，未若吴梅之集其大成；国维评其历史，未若吴梅之发其条例；国维赏其文学，未若吴梅之析其声律。而论曲学者，并世要推吴梅为大师云！"[42] 吴梅培养的弟子包括：任中敏（散曲学科创始人）、卢前（卢冀野，"江南才子"）、唐圭璋（编《全宋词》）、王季思（校注《西厢记》）、钱南扬（南戏专家）、蔡莹、万云骏等。[42] 本报告涉及的学者中，王季思、唐圭璋、俞平伯、程千帆均曾受业于吴梅。

#### 7. 黄侃的学术传承网络
黄侃（1886-1935），字季刚，湖北蕲春人，章太炎最著名的弟子，兼师刘师培，历任北京大学、武昌高等师范学校、金陵大学、中央大学等校教授。音韵学、文字学、训诂学大家，建立了古声十九类、古韵二十八部。著名学生包括范文澜、金毓黻、杨伯峻、龙榆生、陆宗达、殷孟伦、程千帆、潘重规、徐复等。[49] 黄侃治学名言："治学第一当恪守师承；第二当博学多闻；第三当谨于言语"；"读书贵专不贵博"；"治中国学问，当接收新材料，不接收新理论"。他坚持"五十之前不著书"，生前未出版专著，1935年因饮酒引发胃出血去世，去世前一天还在校勘《唐文粹补编》。[49] 本报告涉及的程千帆、刘大杰（武昌高师时期受黄侃影响）均与黄侃有师承关联。

#### 8. 中国戏剧研究的三种路向（陈平原学术史框架）
陈平原（2010）将20世纪中国戏剧研究归纳为三种路向：（1）王国维——文学之美与文字考据；（2）吴梅——声韵之美与曲学声律；（3）齐如山、周贻白、董每戡——演剧之美与舞台实践。大学中文系文学史课程的主导地位使王国维的考据路向成为主流。吴梅的学生（如中山大学王季思以治经方法校注《西厢记》）大体仍走王国维的路子。[13]

#### 9. 中央大学（东南大学）的学术环境
国立东南大学（1921年创办）是长江以南唯一国立大学，1927年与江苏境内9所公立学校合并组建国立第四中山大学，1928年定名国立中央大学，成为全国院系最全、规模最大的大学，赢得"民国最高学府"之誉。[45] 中央大学时期著名人文教授包括黄侃、胡小石、吴梅、汪辟疆、汤用彤、宗白华、徐悲鸿、闻一多等。[45] 东南大学/中央大学是《学衡》派的阵地，主张"白话应提倡，但文言不可废"，与北大新文化运动形成对峙。[44]

#### 10. 1954年批判俞平伯运动
1954年，李希凡、蓝翎在《文史哲》发表批判俞平伯《红楼梦研究》唯心论的文章，毛泽东就此写信，引发全国性批判运动。[39][40] 运动使俞平伯免受1957年"右派"之灾，也使他以红学家身份为公众所知，"因祸得福"。[39]

---

### （二）学者个人信息（按名单顺序）

#### 1. 游国恩（1899-1978）

**基本身份：** 字泽承（一作泽丞），斋名槁庵，江西临川湖南乡洪塘游家村人。著名楚辞研究专家、文学史家、北京大学一级教授。[1][2]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 6岁起在祖父（秀才）指导下读四书五经（旧学训练）[2]
- 1919年毕业于临川中学（今抚州一中）[2]
- 1920年考入北京大学预科班，1922年升入本科中文系学习古典文学，1926年毕业[1][2]
- 最高学历：北京大学中文系本科毕业（无海外留学）[1][2][4]

**师承关系：**
- 祖父（秀才）为其启蒙塾师[2]
- 1929年由闻一多邀请至武汉大学任教，闻一多称游国恩"最先启发我读《楚辞》"（闻一多1942年《楚辞校补·引言》："泽承最先启发我读《楚辞》，骏斋最热心鼓励我校勘它。没有他们，这本书是不会产生的。"）[3]
- 好友包括萧涤非、老舍、陆侃如、罗常培[2]
- 学生包括徐中玉、吴小如、臧克家、何炳棣[2]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1926年毕业后在江西省立第四中学、临川中学、第一女中、第一中学任教[1]
- 1929年起任教于国立武汉大学（讲师，讲中国文学史）、山东大学（1931-1936，讲师而教授）、华中大学（任系主任）、西南联大（1942-1946）、北京大学（1946年起直至去世）[1][2][5]
- 1931年7月应闻一多推荐到国立青岛大学（后国立山东大学）中文系任讲师，与闻一多同住一栋楼（闻上、游下），朝夕讨论楚辞与诗经；讲授中国文学史、楚辞、唐宋以后文学、中国文学故事等课程；1936年辞职赴武昌华中大学，学生赠"教导有方"银盾送行[3][5]
- 1942-1945年在西南联大期间居于昆明龙头村贫苦乡间，作旧体诗百余首[2]
- 1944年应邀赴云南大理帮助修县志[2]
- 1950年在华北革命大学政治研究所学习；1951年加入九三学社[1]
- 历任北京大学中文系副主任、中国科学院文学研究所学术委员、全国政协委员（第三、四、五届）、九三学社中央委员[1]
- 1956年评为一级教授[1]
- 1957-1959年编成《先秦文学史参考资料》《汉文学史参考资料》[2]
- 1961-1963年主持编写全国高校统编教材《中国文学史》（4卷），与王起（中山大学）、萧涤非（山东大学）、季镇淮和费振刚（北京大学）合作；累计发行逾200万册，使用20余年；1987年获国家教委优秀教材特等奖[2][5]
- 1963年赴日本讲屈原，1966年赴越南讲学[2]
- 1978年去世前一天仍在修订《中国文学史》、校勘《离骚》[2]

**主要著作：** 《楚辞概论》（1926，约15万字成名作）、《先秦文学》（1934）、《读骚论微初集》（1937）、《屈原》（1946）、《楚辞论文集》（1957）、《陆游诗选》（合编，1957）、《中国文学史大纲》（1962）、《中国文学史》（1963，4卷主编）、《离骚纂义》（1980，遗著）、《天问纂义》（1982，遗著，金开诚续成）、《游国恩学术论文集》（1989）、《楚辞注疏长编》（历时50年、三代学者的终身项目）。[2] 另有《游國恩文史叢談》（2016年商务印书馆出版，女儿童游宝谅编）。[1]

**知识构成特点：** 旧式私塾教育出身（祖父授四书五经）；无海外留学经历；通晓旧体诗创作；治学方法集训诂、考据、义理于一体，被称为"现代楚辞学的集大成者"。[1][2] 1933年罗常培在青岛记录其临川方言发音，成为《临川音系》主要语音来源。[1]

#### 2. 冯沅君（1900-1974）

**基本身份：** 原名冯淑兰，河南唐河县祁仪镇人，著名文学史家、戏曲史家、作家，五四后第一代有影响的女作家之一（与冰心、庐隐并列）。北京大学第一位女研究生。哲学家冯友兰之妹、地质学家冯景兰之妹、陆侃如之妻。[11][12]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1917年考入国立北京女子高等师范（国文），1922年毕业[11][12]
- 1922年考入北京大学国学门研究生，为该门第一位（唯一）女研究生[11][12]
- 1932年与丈夫陆侃如同赴法国巴黎大学攻读博士学位，1935年获巴黎大学文学博士学位[11][12]
- 最高学历：法国巴黎大学文学博士（1935年）[11]

**师承关系：**
- 哥哥冯友兰引她走上文学道路："我的这种课外学习，倒是在我家里发生了作用，那就是把我的一知半解传授给我的妹妹沅君，引她走上了文学的道路。"（冯友兰语）[12]
- 鲁迅将其小说集《卷葹》编入"乌合丛书"并亲自推荐[11][12]
- 丈夫陆侃如（清华国学研究院毕业，小她3岁）为学术合作者[11][12]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1923-1926年以笔名"淦女士"发表《隔绝》《隔绝之后》《慈母》《旅行》等短篇小说，后集为《卷葹》，写女性追求婚姻自由与个性解放[11]
- 1924-1926年为《语丝》杂志撰稿人，后改笔名"沅君"（取自《九歌》）[11]
- 1931年与陆侃如合著《中国诗史》，被赞"取材审慎，要言不烦"，鲁迅将其与大家著作并荐[11]
- 1935年获得博士学位后回国，先后任教于金陵女子大学、复旦大学、中山大学、武汉大学、山东大学[11][12]
- 1942年应老舍之请在四川三台与丈夫组织"中华文艺界抗敌协会"川北分会[11]
- 抗战期间完成《古剧说汇》《古优解》等重要学术著作[11]
- 1947年起任教于山东大学，1955年（一说1963年）任山东大学副校长[11][12]
- 当选第一、二、三届全国人大代表[11]
- 与陆侃如合著修订《中国文学简史》，被译成英文、捷克文，毛泽东案头常放之书[11]
- 1957年丈夫被划"右派"，被施压揭发时答："我大半辈子与'老虎'同寝共枕，竟无察觉，是得了神经麻痹症吧？"；1958年自身成为"拔白旗"对象[11]
- 1974年6月17日因直肠癌去世，去世前几日还给医院人员即兴讲课[11]

**治学格言：** "做学问，功夫要死，心眼要活"。其《古优解》等三篇论文引用中外文献100余种。遗嘱将全部藏书和积蓄捐给山东大学作学术奖学金。[11]

#### 3. 陆侃如（1903-1978）

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 江苏海门人。1926年入清华国学研究院，1927年毕业，毕业论文《古代诗史》获奖[23]
- 最高学历：清华国学研究院毕业（研究生）[23]

**师承关系：**
- 在清华国学研究院受业于梁启超等，梁启超赠对联："读书最要识家法，行事不须同俗人"（此为高亨所记梁启超赠语，陆侃如同为梁门弟子）[23]
- 与冯沅君为夫妻兼学术合作者[11][12]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1931年与冯沅君合著《中国诗史》，1932年合著《中国文学史编》，均由上海大江书铺出版[12]
- 1932年与冯沅君同赴法国巴黎大学留学[11][12]
- 1935年回国后任教于燕京大学、中山大学、山东大学[12]
- 1937-1947年花十年写成80万字的《中古文学系年》，考订汉至晋150余位作家[23]
- 1951年任山东大学副校长、《文史哲》编委[23]
- 1957年被划为"右派"[11]
- 培养学生包括：牟世金（《文心雕龙》研究）、龚克昌（汉赋研究，在山大建立全国第一个赋学博士点）、张可礼（《三曹年谱》）[23]

#### 4. 林庚（1910-2006）

**基本身份：** 字静希，原籍福建闽侯，生于北京。现代诗人、古代文学学者、文学史家，北京大学教授。享年97岁（一说96岁）。[16][17][18]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1928年毕业于北京师范大学附属中学，考入清华大学物理系[16][18][20]
- 1930年受丰子恺漫画和郑振铎文章影响，转入清华大学中文系[16][18][20]
- 1933年毕业，留校任朱自清助教[16][18]
- 最高学历：清华大学中文系本科毕业[17][18]

**师承关系：**
- 父亲林志钧（林宰平）为清华大学哲学教授，沈从文称赞其文学、法学、哲学、佛学、诗、书法成就[16][18]
- 朱自清（毕业后任其助教）；闻一多（诗集《夜》封面设计）；俞平伯（诗集《夜》序）[16][18]
- 与吴组缃、李长之、季羡林并称"清华四剑客"[16][18][20]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1934年辞职赴上海专事写作，秋返北平任教[16][18]
- 1935年开始写格律诗，出版《北平情歌》《冬眠曲及其他》[16][18]
- 抗战期间任厦门大学（迁长汀）教授，开始楚辞研究（1939年作《湘君及湘夫人》）[16][19]
- 1947年任燕京大学教授[16][18]
- 1952年院系调整后任北京大学中文系教授，1956年任古代文学教研室主任[16][18]
- 1954-1963年任《光明日报·文学遗产》编委[16]
- 文革中被诬为"反动学术权威"遭批斗劳改[18]
- 1986年退休但仍任博士生导师；2004年任北大诗歌中心主任[16]
- 晚年与吴组缃、王瑶、季镇淮并称"北大中文四老"[16][20]

**主要学术贡献：**
- 提出唐诗"盛唐气象"与"少年精神"概念，被学界广泛接受[16][18]
- 发现并推广贺知章《咏柳》，使其进入小学课本[16]
- 楚辞研究：论证《天问》为"古代传说中的一部兴亡史诗"；提出"兮"字为半逗律节奏标记；主张《湘君》《湘夫人》原为一篇；《招魂》为招阵亡将士的仪式诗[19]
- 著作：《中国文学简史》（大学教材）、《诗人屈原及其作品研究》、《诗人李白》、《天问论笺》、《唐诗综论》、《西游记漫话》（80岁出版，程千帆赞"盖自有《西游记》以来之第一篇文章也"）、《新诗格律与语言的诗化》[16][18]
- 新诗理论提出"五字组""半逗律"；创九言诗"林庚体"[16][18]
- 朱自清称赞其《中国文学史》将文学发展视为有机再生[20]

**知识构成特点：** 清华物理系转中文（理工跨学科背景）；诗人兼学者（废名："在新诗当中，林庚的分量或者比任何人都要重些"）；旧学与新学兼备。[16][20]

#### 5. 萧涤非（1906/1907-1991）

**基本身份：** 也写作肖涤非，原名萧忠临，江西临川茶溪村人。著名学者，山东大学中文系教授，乐府与唐诗研究权威。[21][22]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1907年1月11日生（一说1906年11月27日）[22][25]
- 1920年考入开封留美预备学校，后转入南昌心远中学；1926年由南京江苏省立第一中学同时考取清华和东南大学，入清华大学中文系[22]
- 1930年毕业后免试入清华大学研究院，1933年毕业[22][25]
- 最高学历：清华大学研究院毕业[22][25]

**师承关系：**
- 研究生导师为黄节（黄晦闻），萧涤非尊其为"恩师"[25]
- 经黄节推荐到青岛山东大学任中文系讲师[22][23][25]
- 后经余冠英、黄玉佳相助赴昆明西南联大[22]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1933年到山东大学任教；1936年秋被解聘（离校时与李烈钧外甥女黄兼芬结婚）[22]
- 1936年转任四川大学讲师，1941年因拒绝参加国民党被解聘[22]
- 1941年赴昆明西南联合大学任副教授、教授，生活极其艰难；抗战八年与杜甫诗歌产生深度共鸣，开始讲授杜诗并积累数十万字讲义[22][25]
- 1947年重返山东大学任教授，执教47年[21][22]
- 1951年到华北人民革命大学学习；1952年加入中国民主同盟[22]
- 历任山东大学中文系主任、教授、硕士博士生导师、教务部副部长、古典文学教研室主任、古籍整理研究所副所长、《文史哲》编委会副主任[21]
- 1961-1963年与游国恩、王起（王季思）、季镇淮、费振刚共同主编《中国文学史》[22]
- 1964年当选第三届全国人大代表；1978年、1983年当选第五、六届全国政协委员[22]
- 国务院学位委员会第一届学科评议组文学组成员；中国唐代文学学会首任会长；山东省第四届文联副主席[21][23]
- 文革中被诬为"反动学术权威"[22]
- 1991年4月15日去世[22]

**主要著作：** 《汉魏六朝乐府文学史》（1944年，1984年修订再版，被誉"乐府诗史最佳之作"）、《读诗三札记》（1956）、《解放集》（1959）、《杜甫研究》（1959，1949年后第一部全面研究杜甫的著作，奠定杜诗研究权威地位）、《杜甫诗选注》（1979）、《乐府诗词论薮》（1985）、《皮子文薮》（1959，校点）、《杜甫全集校注》。[21][22][23][24]

**培养学生：** 李从军、林继中为全国首批古典文学博士（1985、1986年）；训练了全国首批5名硕士生和2名博士生；按国家教委安排指导美国高级进修生。美、日等国学者赞之为"汉学伟人"。[23][24]

**其他：** 青年时代为华北著名足球健将，清华100米纪录11.1秒保持到解放后。[25]

#### 6. 余冠英（1906-1995）

**基本身份：** 字绍生，笔名灌婴，江苏松江（今属上海）人，中国古典文学专家，中国民主同盟盟员。[26][28]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1906年5月16日生，6岁随家迁扬州，在扬州生活20年[28]
- 1922年入江苏省立第八中学（今扬州中学）[26][28]
- 1926年考入清华大学历史系，后转入中文系，1931年毕业[26][28]
- 最高学历：清华大学中文系本科毕业[26][28]

**师承关系：**
- 在西南联大、清华时期治学受朱自清影响[30]
- 吴组缃1931年称赞其为代表清华文学风格的作家[28]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 毕业后留清华任教；抗战期间（1938年）赴昆明西南联大，先后任师范学院讲师、副教授、教授，讲授中国文学史、各体文写作、历代文选；任《国文月刊》主编至第40期[26][28]
- 1946年秋返清华任中文系教授，讲授中国文学史和汉魏六朝诗[26]
- 1952年任中国科学院（后社科院）文学研究所二级研究员，后任副所长；1953-1979年任古代文学组组长、古代室主任[26][27][28]
- 任《文学遗产》主编、所学术委员会主任、顾问[26][27][28]
- 第三届全国人大代表、第五六届全国政协委员、中国文联委员、中国作协理事、国际笔会会员、全国古籍整理出版规划小组顾问[26][28]
- 1985年79岁时退休，仍任顾问、学术委员会名誉主任、博士生导师[28]

**主要著作与学术贡献：**
- 主持编纂《中国文学史》（3卷，1962年人民文学出版社）[28]
- 主编《唐诗选》（历时18年）[27][28]
- 个人选注《诗经选》《诗经选译》《乐府诗选》（1953年）、《三曹诗选》（1956）、《汉魏六朝诗选》（1958）；著《汉魏六朝诗论丛》（1956）、《古代文学杂论》（1987）[26][27][28]
- 学术方法：考据、义理、辞章结合，注释简明，点评诗意[30]
- 五四时期参与五卅运动，任扬州学生联合会首届会长；1948年6月18日与朱自清、金岳霖、吴汉等共同签署《抗议美国扶日政策并拒绝领取美援面粉宣言》[28]
- 在清华组织"唧唧诗社"[28]

#### 7. 王季思/王起（1906-1996）

**基本身份：** 名王起，字季思，以字行。浙江永嘉（今温州市瓯海区）梧埏上田村人。中国戏曲学者，中山大学中文系文学教授。[31]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 幼年即遍读经史，酷爱戏曲小说；未读完小学即考入浙江省立第十中学[31]
- 1925年（一说1924年）考入国立东南大学文学系（中文系），师从曲学大师吴梅[31][33]
- 最高学历：国立东南大学中文系本科毕业[31][33]

**师承关系：**
- 师从吴梅，学习古代词曲和戏曲，参加吴梅组织的"潜社"从事诗词和散曲创作；吴梅在其作业上批语："自万历以来，遇庭、韦昭去后，我又得此才，中心大快！"[31][33]
- 在闻一多指导下从事话剧与新诗创作[33]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1927年曾在瓯海中学任教，因宣传第一次全国代表大会宣言在"四一二"事变中被捕，后获释返南京复学[33]
- 毕业后任教于浙江、安徽、江苏多所中学；在江苏松江女中期间收集大量元曲资料[31][33]
- 1940年代初至1948年任教于浙江大学龙泉分校、杭州浙江大学、杭州之江文理学院，从事元杂剧和中国文学史研究[33]
- 1944年出版《西厢五剧注》；1948年出版《集评校注西厢记》[33]
- 1948年夏到中山大学，工作48年至1996年去世[33]
- 1950年代以马克思主义文学理论分析古代作品，发表《从〈莺莺传〉到〈西厢记〉》等；1957年4月出版《桃花扇校注》[33]
- 1962年受教育部委托赴北京大学与游国恩等合编《中国文学史》，历时三年[33]
- 文革中被批斗、关"牛棚"、打断肋骨，学术研究被迫中断[33]
- 1981年经国务院学位委员会批准为全国首批博士生导师之一[33]
- 1982年主编《中国十大古典悲剧集》《中国十大古典喜剧集》（上海文艺出版社），成为全国畅销书[32][33]
- 1985年80岁时主持编纂《全元戏曲》，获全国古籍整理一等奖等多项奖[33]
- 1949年后历任中山大学中文系主任、古文研究所所长、民盟广东省委副主任委员、第三四届全国政协委员等[33]
- 1990年84岁高龄退休[32]

**主要著作：** 《西厢五剧注》《集评校注西厢记》《桃花扇注》《中国十大古典悲剧集》《中国十大古典喜剧集》《元杂剧选》《元散曲选》《中国戏曲选》《全元曲选》《王轮轩戏曲新论》《王季思学术论著自选集》。[31]

**其他：** 国务院学位委员会第一届学科评议组（文学组）成员，中华诗词学会顾问。[31] 其分类悲剧/喜剧的尝试源于1979年与易新农教授的合作，为全国高校戏剧师资培训班授课。[32] 诗句"薪尽火传光不绝"体现其学术传承精神。[32]

#### 8. 钱锺书（1910-1998）

**基本身份：** 字哲良，又字默存，号槐聚。江苏无锡人。著名学者、作家，被誉为"文化昆仑"。[7][9][10]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 早年就读苏州桃坞中学、无锡辅仁中学（教会学校）[29]
- 1929年考入清华大学外文系：数学仅15分，因国文、英文成绩优异（英文满分）被校长罗家伦亲阅试卷后破格录取（"此为奇才，破格录取"）[9]
- 1933年从清华大学外文系毕业（因日军入侵热河，学校提前放假，未举行毕业考试和典礼，未交毕业论文）[8]
- 1935年考取第三届中英庚款奖学金（262名考生中17人考英国文学，钱锺书得87.95分，为三年来所有考试最高分），入牛津大学埃克塞特学院[6][8]
- 1937年获牛津大学B.Litt.（副博士/文学学士，相当于M.Phil.）学位，论文题为《十七、十八世纪英国文学中的中国》（China in the English Literature of the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries）；1937年10月29日颁发毕业证书，但钱锺书未申请正式学位，"从理论上说，钱锺书在牛津并没有被授予任何学位"[6][7]
- 1936年经友人盛澄华在巴黎大学注册博士，但完成牛津学业后失去兴趣，因奖学金只能延长一年、经济压力和国内局势，1938年8月与杨绛回国[8]
- 最高学历：牛津大学B.Litt.（相当于硕士），无博士学位[6][8]

**师承关系：**
- 父亲钱基博（钱基博），古典散文大师、现代著名文史学家、清华大学教授[7][10][29]
- 清华时期受教于吴宓等，吴宓赞其为"人中之龙"，认为老一辈文史杰出人才推陈寅恪，年轻一辈推钱锺书[9]
- 与曹禺、颜毓蘅并称清华外文"龙虎狗三杰"，钱锺书居首[7]
- 冯友兰为其牛津申请史博定讲席（Spalding Lectureship）写推荐信（推荐钱锺书和王维诚，冯认为王维诚中国哲学宗教知识更强，钱锺书英文更好；1937年王维诚获任）[6]

**工作经历：**
- 1933年毕业后任教于上海光华大学（其父钱基博时任光华中文系主任）[7][8]
- 1938年夏清华聘其为外文系教授，赴西南联大任教；1939年返沪探亲后未归[7][8]
- 抗战期间写《写在人生边上》（1941）、《人·兽·鬼》（1946）、《围城》（1947）、《谈艺录》（1948）[10]
- 1953年任中国科学院文学研究所一级研究员；1982年任中国社会科学院副院长[7][9]
- 参与《毛泽东选集》（1950）英译委员会、《毛泽东诗词》（1960、1974）英译[9]
- 1979年出版巨著《管锥编》（4卷，781则读书笔记，评论《周易》《诗经》《左传》《史记》等十种典籍，引证近万种著作、4000余位作者，含1000余位西方学者，使用中、英、法、德、意、拉丁文）[10]

**知识构成特点：** 教会学校西学 + 家庭旧学 + 自学；多语言能力；"照相机式"记忆；在清华立志"横扫清华图书馆"；毕业后的五大麻袋读书笔记是《管锥编》主要资料来源[9][10]。其治学态度："大抵学问是荒江（野）老屋中二三素心人商量培养之事，朝市之显学必成俗学。"[10] 拒绝哈佛、普林斯顿、耶鲁、哥伦比亚、芝加哥等美国名校名誉博士学位，退还哈佛寄来的3000美元支票。[8]

#### 9. 俞平伯（1900-1990）

**基本身份：** 原名俞铭衡，乳名僧宝，字平伯，以字行。祖籍浙江德清，生于江苏苏州马医科巷曲园春在堂。现代诗人、作家、红学家。九三学社社员。[36][37][40]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1915年入北京大学预科（国文），1919年12月从北京大学毕业[36][37][39]
- 1920年尝试赴英留学、后尝试赴美留学，均很快返回（不能吃苦）[39]
- 最高学历：北京大学本科毕业[36][37]

**师承关系：**
- 曾祖父为清代朴学大师俞樾（曲园）；父亲俞陛云为1898年探花[36][37][39]
- 1915年在北大预科师从吴梅学昆曲[36][37][38]
- 北大时期老师包括黄侃、周作人、胡适、刘半农；同学包括傅斯年、许德珩[39]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1918年5月在《新青年》发表第一首白话诗《春水》（与鲁迅《狂人日记》同期），为最早的白话诗先驱之一；与傅斯年、罗家伦共同创立新潮社[36][37]
- 1923年出版《红楼梦辨》，确立《红楼梦》前80回为曹雪芹作、后40回为高鹗续作，与胡适同为"新红学"创始人[36][37]
- 1922年1月与朱自清、郑振铎、叶圣陶创办《诗》月刊（五四后最早的新诗刊物）[37]
- 1925年任教于燕京大学；1928年转清华大学；1935年创办"清华谷音社"推广昆曲[36][37][38]
- 1946年任北京大学教授；1947年加入九三学社[37]
- 1953年入中国科学院文学研究所（今社科院），此后终身在该所工作[36][37]
- 1954年毛泽东亲自发动全国性批判运动，批判其《红楼梦》研究及胡适"反动思想"[36][37]
- 1956年创办北京昆曲研习社并任社长，1958年10月2日纪念汤显祖逝世340周年之际恢复演出《牡丹亭》（周恩来总理出席首演）；1959年10月作为唯一业余团体参加国庆十周年演出[38]
- 文革中被批斗，1969年11月-1971年1月下放河南息县五七干校劳动（年迈妻子许宝驯坚持陪同）[36][37][39]
- 1979年北京昆曲研习社恢复活动；1986年文学所为其举办学术活动65周年纪念，赴香港讲红学[37]
- 1990年10月15日在北京去世[36][37]

**主要著作：** 红学方面：《红楼梦辨》（1923）、《红楼梦研究》（1952）、《红楼梦八十回校本》（1958）、《俞平伯论红楼梦》（1988）；诗词：《冬夜》（1922）、《雪潮》（1923）、《西还》（1924）；学术：《读诗札记》（1934）、《读词偶得》（1923/1947）、《清真词释》（1948）、《唐宋词选释》（1979）；《俞平伯全集》10卷（1997年花山文艺出版社）。[36][37]

**知识构成特点：** 朴学世家出身；昆曲终身爱好（与赵景深并称昆曲界"南赵北俞"）；1956年评为一级研究员（何其芳坚持，俞平伯回应"差不多，差不多"）。[36][39][40]

#### 10. 唐圭璋（1901-1990）

**基本身份：** 字季特，南京人（满族旗籍），著名词学家，被誉为"一代词宗"。[41]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1901年1月23日生于南京，7岁丧父、11岁丧母，由他人抚养[41]
- 1922年入国立东南大学中文系，师从词曲大师吴梅；1928年毕业[41]
- 最高学历：国立东南大学中文系本科毕业[41]

**师承关系：**
- 吴梅弟子，与任中敏、卢前并称"吴门三杰"，专攻词学[41]
- 受王鹏运、况周颐"重拙大"理论影响[41]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 毕业后任教于江苏省立第一女子中学、中央军校、中央大学（抗战时期重庆/成都）、金陵大学、东北师范大学，最后到南京师范大学（1953-1990）任教授、博士生导师[41]
- 治词学，著作20余种、逾千万字：编《全宋词》《全金元词》《词话丛编》（1986年中华书局修订本精装5册，增补25种，共85种词话，近400万字，集历代词话之大成）、《宋词三百首笺注》《南唐二主词汇笺》《唐宋词简释》《宋词四考》《宋词纪事》《梦桐词》《词学论丛》[41]
- 教学方式如老师吴梅，带笛子上课，以昆曲唱词和戏曲片段加深学生理解[41]
- 提出词作四原则"雅婉厚亮"（雅清新纯正；婉温柔缠绵；厚沉郁顿挫；亮名隽高华）[41]
- 1990年11月28日去世，享年89岁[41]

**其他：** 一生历经幼年丧怙、中年丧偶（1936年除夕妻子尹孝曾去世，终身未续弦）、晚年丧女三大不幸；《梦桐词》133首中61首写于抗战时期。[41]

#### 11. 程千帆（1913-2000）

**基本身份：** 原名逢会，改名会昌，字伯昊，四十岁以后别号闲堂，"千帆"为笔名之一。祖籍湖南宁乡，生于长沙。著名古代文史学家、教育家，公认的国学大师。九三学社社员。[46][47][50]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 出身文学世家，曾祖程霖寿、叔祖程颂万、父亲程康皆为诗人，自幼通晓声律[47][50]
- 约1923年随家迁武昌，在伯父程君硕指导下接受古典文学教育[47]
- 1928年考入金陵中学，1932年升入金陵大学（原想学化学，因学费贵改入中文系）[47][48][50]
- 1936年毕业于金陵大学中文系[46][47][50]
- 最高学历：金陵大学中文系本科毕业[46][50]

**师承关系：**
- 在金陵大学师从黄侃、吴梅、汪辟疆[46][47][50]
- 黄侃为其重要导师，临终遗言"我对不起老师，我对不起黄先生！"（遗憾《黄侃日记》未出版）[48]
- 第一任妻子沈祖棻（著名词人，原中央大学商科转中文）；第二任妻子陶芸[48][50]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 毕业后历任金陵中学、金陵大学、四川大学、武汉大学教职；28岁即被刘永济聘为武汉大学教授[47][48][50]
- 1957年被错划为"右派"，1958年起被迫中断学术研究近20年[47][50]
- 1977年被武汉大学强制退休；1978年由南京大学校长匡亚明邀请复出，经一次试讲即聘为教授[47][48][50]
- 1984年回武汉大学讲学，校长刘道玉正式道歉[48]
- 1988年自愿退休，继续研究至2000年6月3日在南京去世[48][50]
- 任南京大学教授、江苏省文史馆馆长、中国唐代文学学会会长[46][50]

**学术成就与方法：** 学术精髓为"将考证和批评密切地结合起来，将批评建立在考据基础上的方法"，是对古代文学研究在方法论上的最重要贡献。复出后十多年出版十多部重要学术著作：《校雠广义》（与徐有富合著）、《两宋文学史》、《程氏汉语文学通史》、《史通笺记》、《文论十笺》、《唐代进士行卷与文学》、《闲堂文薮》、《古诗考索》、《被开拓的诗世界》等。[47][50]

**培养学生：** 晚年精心培养研究生，使南大古代文学专业成为全国重点学科；弟子号称"八大金刚"（莫砺锋、张伯伟、张宏生、巩本栋、曹虹、程章灿、蒋寅等）；莫砺锋为中国内地第一位文学博士[47][50]。教学格言："敬业、乐群、勤奋、谦虚"；治学十二字格言："以学心听，以公心辨，以仁心说"。[47][50] 遗嘱称"所精心培养学生数人，极为优秀，为国家之宝贵财富"。[48]

#### 12. 朱东润（1896-1988）

**基本身份：** 江苏泰兴人。中国古代文学及各体文学著名专家、文艺批评家、文学史家、教育家、书法家。[52]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 出身贫苦家庭（父亲为店员），出生时因家贫险被遗弃[53]
- 入上海南洋公学（交通大学前身）作富家子弟伴读，因成绩优异得校长唐文治资助学费[53]
- 1913年（一说1916年）赴英国伦敦西南学院留学[52][54]
- 1916年伦敦西南学院肄业（因反帝制革命回国）[52][53]
- 最高学历：英国伦敦西南学院肄业（无学位）[52]

**师承关系：**
- 南洋公学校长唐文治资助其学费；吴稚晖安排其赴英留学[53]
- 1929年被闻一多（武汉大学文学院院长）发现并邀请至武汉大学教英文、后教中文[53]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 曾在南通张謇所办师范学校教语文[53]
- 1929-1957年（一说1929-1952）在武汉大学任教28年[51][52]
- 抗战期间（1937年起）只身经香港、柬埔寨、越南赴迁至四川乐山的武汉大学[53]
- 1952年院系调整后入复旦大学，1957-1967年任复旦大学中文系主任（陈望道校长任命）[51][52]
- 晚年任全国写作学会名誉会长[52]

**学术贡献：**
- 中国文学批评史学科创始人之一（郭绍虞为开创者，朱东润为主要奠基人之一）：1944年出版《中国文学批评史大纲》，朱自清称其为"我国第一部简要的中国文学批评全史"；钱锺书致王水照信："郭朱二老，当代耆硕，学问笃实，亦京华冠盖中所无也"（赞郭绍虞、朱东润）[51]
- 现代中国传记文学开拓者：读英国留学时读Boswell《约翰生传》后对传记产生兴趣；1943年（抗战时期）为激励国人而作《张居正大传》（基于46卷《张文忠公全集》写8个月），以张居正"以社会国家为己任"的精神鼓舞抗战；另有《陆游传》《梅尧臣传》《杜甫叙论》《陈子龙及其时代》《元好问传》《王守仁大传》《李方舟传》（悼念文革中自杀的妻子）、《朱东润自传》；本人愿被称为"传记文学家"[51][53]
- 争议性学术观点：1940年发表《国风出于民间论质疑》（主张160首国风多为统治阶级诗而非民歌）；1951年主张《离骚》非屈原所作[51]
- 1954年为中华书局编《左传选》，提出《左传》作者可能为战国初期吴起[51]

**治学特点：** 读《诗经》必先通读齐、鲁、韩、毛及郑玄笺注、陈启源、陈奂、马瑞辰、龚橙等各家再下判断；"言必有据，无征不信"。[51][53] 口头禅："年轻人是要苦干的"。[53]

#### 13. 郭绍虞（1893-1984）

**基本身份：** 原名希汾，字绍虞，江苏苏州人。著名教育家、古典文学家、语言学家、书法家，复旦大学教授，中国科学院学部委员。中共党员，民盟成员。与陈望道、朱东润等并称"复旦大学中文系十老"。[59]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1893年11月21日生于苏州贫寒书香之家（祖父为清举人，父亲郭鲁卿为文案/塾师）[59]
- 中学二年级即因家贫辍学，此后自学成才[56][59]
- 1914年起在上海商务印书馆尚公小学任教，得以利用涵芬楼藏书自学[56][59]
- 1919年到北京任《晨报副刊》特约撰稿人，在北大旁听课程[56][59]
- 最高学历：无正式学历（中学肄业，北大旁听）[56][59]

**师承关系：**
- 与叶圣陶为童年好友（叶圣陶为《中国体育史》作序）[56]
- 1921年由胡适、顾颉刚推荐到福建协和大学任教，开始大学教学生涯[56]
- 与郑振铎、茅盾、叶圣陶等于1921年元旦共同创立文学研究会[56][57][59]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 1921年起任教于福建协和大学、开封中州大学、北京燕京大学（1927-1941年14年，此间开始研究与撰写《中国文学批评史》）[56][59]
- 抗战时期拒绝与日伪合作，因拒任伪北大课被拘押两天，讲授"最后一课"朗诵《诗经·黍离》后离去[56][59]
- 1946年任同济大学文学院院长；1950年起任复旦大学中文系教授、系主任、图书馆馆长、文学研究室主任[56][57][59]
- 1956年加入中国共产党；1979年当选中国古代文学理论学会首任会长[57][59]
- 1984年6月23日在上海去世，享年91岁[59]

**学术贡献：**
- 中国文学批评史学科奠基人：《中国文学批评史》1934年（上卷）、1947年（下卷）由商务印书馆出版，被公认为该领域最系统深刻的著作；朱自清（1934）称其为第一个系统搜集材料者，认为"材料和眼光都是他自己的"；该书将批评史分为演进、复古、完成三期[56][57][59]
- 宋诗话研究：《宋诗话辑佚》（1937年哈佛燕京学社，1980年中华书局）、《宋诗话考》（1979）[56][57][59]
- 语法修辞研究：《汉语语法修辞新探》（1979，2卷）、《语文通论》，主张语法修辞词汇相结合[56][57]
- 书法家：为鲁迅、郑振铎编《北平笺谱》作序，有书法论文十余篇[59]

**治学特点：** 受胡适"研究问题、输入学理、整理国故"方法影响，主张以科学方法研究古典文学；强调"记性"与"悟性"并重，"将勤补拙"。晚年主张"狂狷"人格理想（既有进取的"狂"，又有原则的"狷"），反对帮闲帮凶。[56][59]

#### 14. 刘大杰（1904-1977）

**基本身份：** 笔名大杰、雪容女士、绿蕉、夏绿蕉、修士、湘君、刘山等，室名春波楼。湖南岳阳人。著名文史学家、作家、翻译家，被誉为"20世纪最有才气的中国文学史家"。[62][63][65]

**毕业院校与学历：**
- 1904年生于岳阳十步乡庙升塘，生后不满1岁父死，12岁母死，由外婆资助进私塾[63]
- 14岁入岳阳贫民工厂做童工（织毛巾、做伞），攒35块银元后于1919年入武昌旅鄂中学，课余在学校食堂养猪自给[63]
- 1922年入国立武昌高等师范学校中文系（原报考数学，被分入中文系），1926年毕业[62][63]
- 1926年赴日本，1927年入早稻田大学大学院（研究生院）文学部，专攻欧洲文学，靠为国内报刊撰稿自给，1930年毕业[63]
- 最高学历：日本早稻田大学大学院文学部毕业[63]

**师承关系：**
- 武昌高师时期受教于黄侃、胡小石，特别受郁达夫影响（郁达夫教文学课，鼓励其写小说）；1925年郁达夫因受保守派排挤辞职，刘大杰随其离校赴上海[63]
- 郁达夫资助其在早稻田大学的学业；1945年郁达夫被日军杀害后，刘大杰先后作四首悼诗[63]

**工作经历与研究方向：**
- 留日回国后任上海大东书局编辑，为《现代学生》杂志审外国文学稿件[63]
- 先后任教于复旦大学、安徽大学、暨南大学，与鲁迅、林语堂有交往[63]
- 1935年任四川大学中文系教授、系主任；1937年返沪省亲遇抗战爆发，滞留上海8年，完成《中国文学发展史》（80余万字，上卷1941年1月出版，下卷1943年完成）和《魏晋思想论》（20余万字，1949年出版）；期间在之江大学、圣约翰大学兼课[63]
- 1945年后任上海临时大学文法系主任、暨南大学文学院院长[63]
- 1949年后暨南大学系并入复旦大学，任复旦大学中文系教授、文学研究室主任、代理系主任，在复旦工作29年直至1977年11月26日病逝[61][62][63][65]
- 历任中国作协上海分会副主席、中国文联常委、农工民主党上海市委副主任、第四届全国政协委员、第四届全国人大代表、《收获》《文学评论》《上海文学》编委[63]
- 1965年5月20日在复旦受到毛泽东主席接见和鼓励，此后与毛泽东书信讨论李白、李商隐诗歌（现存韶山毛泽东故居的毛泽东生前最后一封信即与此相关）[62][63]

**学术贡献：**
- 《中国文学发展史》被视为"文学史研究领域内具有系统性、成就最为突出的一部文学史样本，确定了中国文学史著作的基本范式"（陈尚君）；"博大深沉的刘著，正好为民国时期的文学史撰写，画上了一个圆满的句号，也为发轫于世纪初的中国文学史史学走向成熟，建立了重要的里程碑"（陈尚君）[62][64]
- 该书成功三因素（骆玉明）：理论上的特色（首次将西方文学理论系统运用于中国文学史）、鲜明的时代立场（站在"五四"新文化立场，发掘古代文学与五四精神相通处）、个性化特征（一人独著，史家理性与诗人感性共存）[61][64]
- 受泰纳（Taine）、朗松（Lanson）、弗里契、勃兰兑斯（Brandes）等西方理论影响，但不机械搬用，组织成自己的体系，主张"求因明变"[62][64]
- 1963年1962年修订版经教育部1983年重印作为全国高校文科教材；"要论影响的广泛与持久，至今还没有一种文学史能够超过它"（陈尚君）[62]
- 《中国古典文学的现实主义问题》一文为全国最早质疑"现实主义与反现实主义"公式的文章之一[62]
- 讲课极受欢迎："听大杰先生讲课，同学们都形成了一个心理习惯，就是怕下课，希望他讲得越长越好"；能背诵《红楼梦》黑山村庄头乌进孝缴租单[62]
- 翻译托尔斯泰、杰克·伦敦、屠格涅夫、显克微支、陀思妥耶夫斯基、雪莱等作品；著《易卜生研究》《托尔斯泰研究》《德国文学大纲》《表现主义的文学》《东西文学评论》等[63][65]
- 首批"上海社科大师"名单成员（同列者有徐森玉、吕思勉、陈望道、吴蕴瑞等）[63]

#### 15. 詹锳（1916-1998）

**基本信息：** 字振文。1916年6月29日生，1998年12月6日去世。曾任河北大学古籍整理研究所所长、国务院古籍规划出版小组成员、中国唐代文学学会顾问、中国李白研究会会长、名誉会长、中国古代文学理论学会第二届、第三届理事。[66]

--- SOURCE 1: 袁行霈 ---
URL: https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E8%A2%81%E8%A1%8C%E9%9C%88/1878173

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Baidu Baike (Baidu Encyclopedia) entry for 袁行霈 (Yuan Xingpei), a prominent Chinese classical literature scholar. He was born on April 18, 1936, in Jinan, Shandong Province, with ancestral roots in Wujin, Jiangsu. His courtesy name is 春澍 (Chunshu).

**Identity & Positions:** Yuan Xingpei is a professor in the Chinese Department of Peking University, Director of the Peking University Academy of Chinese Studies (国学研究院), Director of the Peking University Center for Chinese Traditional Culture Research, Editor-in-chief of the annual journal "国学研究" (Chinese Studies), member of the Peking University Council, and Director of the Humanities Division at Peking University. He also serves as the Director (馆长) of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History (中央文史研究馆), Standing Committee member of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC), Vice-Chairman of the China Democratic League Central Committee, and member of the State Council Academic Degrees Committee. He became a foreign member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences in April 2018.

**Education & Career Timeline:** 
- 1953: Admitted to Peking University Chinese Department
- 1957: Graduated and stayed at PKU as a faculty member, becoming a teaching assistant under Lin Geng (林庚)
- 1958-1960: Participated in labor assignments including coal mining in Chengzi, Beijing and steel production work
- 1960s: Designated as a "白专" (white-and-expert) model during political campaigns; criticized during the Cultural Revolution and sent to labor reform camp at Liyuzhou, where he survived a serious vehicle accident
- 1979: Promoted to lecturer; published notable papers including "山海经初探" and began gaining academic attention
- 1980: Appointed associate professor
- 1982-1983: Taught at Tokyo University in Japan
- 1984: Became specially-appointed professor in Chinese Department
- 1986: Qualified as doctoral supervisor
- 1992: Became Director of PKU Chinese Traditional Culture Research Center and Editor of 《国学研究》
- 1992-1993, 1998: Visiting professor at National University of Singapore
- 1997: Visiting scholar at Harvard-Yenching Institute; lectured at Harvard, Yale, Columbia, Washington, and Hawaii universities
- 1999: Became Director of PKU Humanities Division
- 2000: Became Director of PKU Academy of Chinese Studies
- 2004: Visiting professor at City University of Hong Kong
- 2005: Confirmed as senior professor at PKU (enjoying treatment equivalent to CAS academicians); also appointed professor at Nanyang Technological University
- January 18, 2006: Appointed Director of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History (the seventh director, succeeding Fu Dingyi, Zhang Shizhao, Yang Dongchun, Ye Shengtao, Xiao Qian, and Qi Gong)

**Key Academic Contributions:**
- Advocated "纵通" (vertical integration) and "横通" (horizontal integration) methodology in literary studies, articulated in a 1978 Guangming Daily article
- Major works include 《中国诗歌艺术研究》(1987, with Japanese and Korean translations), 《陶渊明集笺注》, 《陶渊明研究》, 《中国文学概论》, and the four-volume 《中国文学史》(1999) which he edited with 29 scholars from 19 universities—a textbook that won multiple national awards including the Fifth National Book Award (2001)
- Spent 20 years on Tao Yuanming research across three books: 《陶渊明研究》, 《陶渊明集笺注》, and 《陶渊明影像》
- Served as chief editor of the four-volume 《中华文明史》, whose English translation was published by Cambridge University Press (2012)
- Other edited works include 《中国地域文化通览》 (expected 15 million characters, 2012) and 《缀英集——中央文史研究馆馆员诗选》
- Recent star-map works include 《诗经国风新注》(2018, with Xu Jianwei and Cheng Sudong), 《好诗不厌百回读》(2017, selected for national "大众喜爱的50种图书"), and 《中华传统文化经典百篇》(2016, co-edited with Wang Zhongwei and Chen Jinyu)

**Awards & Honors:** National Outstanding Teaching Achievement Award (Special Grade, 1989), National Education System Model Worker and People's Teacher Medal (1991), Beijing People's Teacher title (1993, top ten by public vote), Beijing Advanced Worker (1995), PKU "Cai Yuanpei Award" (2006, considered PKU's highest faculty honor), and multiple awards for 《中国诗歌艺术研究》 and 《中国文学史》.

**Teaching & Character:** Renowned as a model of "儒雅" (cultured elegance) at PKU, following his mentor Lin Geng. His lectures on Tao Yuanming and Tang poetry were among the most popular in the Chinese Department. He emphasized the unity of scholarship and moral character, requiring students to submit both an academic paper and a "moral character paper." His notable students include Meng Erdong (孟二冬). He believes scholarship should have "气象" (grandeur/atmosphere) requiring dedicated attitude, broad-mindedness, and high moral character.

**Views on National Studies (国学):** He holds that guoxue (national studies) cannot save China or lead to modernization, but must be seriously studied as part of China's cultural heritage, approached with analytical, open, and developmental attitudes—absorbing essence and discarding dross.

**Family Background:** Comes from a distinguished scholarly family. His great-grandfather Yuan Jimao was a second-place jinshi (榜眼) in the Daoguang period who died defending Shunchang County during the Taiping Rebellion. His great-grandmother Zuo Xixuan was a literary woman. His grandfather Yuan Xuechang was a juren (举人) in the fifth year of Guangxu; his grandmother Zeng Yi was a famous female traditional Chinese medicine practitioner and poet. His uncle (second uncle) Yuan Lizhun was a late-Qing Hanlin scholar, calligrapher, and collector who served as one of Puyi's teachers.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"所谓'纵通'是'就文学论文学，着重研究文学史上各种现象、体裁、流派的发生、发展和衰落……'所谓'横通'就是力求将文学和史学、哲学、宗教、艺术乃至自然科学结合起来进行研究，'并努力从它们的关联上，从它们之间的相互影响、渗透的关系上，寻求带有规律性的东西'。" — Yuan Xingpei's 1978 article "纵通与横通" on his academic methodology, published in Guangming Daily.
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 2: 中國文化研究所通訊 ---
URL: https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/enewsasp/app/article-details.aspx/D971B65599F6873DA603203511419E4A

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is a Chinese-language interview with Professor Yuan Xingpei (袁行霈), published in the 2016 second issue of the Chinese Culture Institute Newsletter (中國文化研究所通訊) at The Chinese University of Hong Kong. The interview was conducted on March 31, 2016, at the Institute's "澄軒" (Cheng Xuan) venue. The interviewer was Professor Zhang Jian (張健) of the Chinese Language and Literature Department, with transcription by Xu Yanlian and content organization by Hu Qi.

**About Professor Yuan Xingpei:**
- Born 1936 in Jinan, Shandong; ancestral home in Wujin, Jiangsu.
- Current positions: Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Peking University, Dean of the National Studies Institute (國學研究院), Director of the International Sinologists Research Base, and Chief Editor of "國學研究" (Studies in Sinology).
- Also serves as Director of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History (中央文史研究館), and member of the National Education Advisory Committee.
- Former roles: Standing Committee member of the 8th and 9th CPPCC, Standing Committee member of the 10th NPC, and Vice-Chairman of the China Democratic League Central Committee.
- Major publications include works on Chinese poetry art, Chinese literature, Tao Yuanming studies (including annotated edition and imagery), History of Chinese Literature (chief editor), History of Chinese Civilization (chief editor), and Survey of Chinese Regional Culture (chief editor), among others.

**Part 1: Academic Origins – Solid Foundation in Language and Literature**
- Entered Peking University's Chinese Department in 1953, benefiting from the 1952 reorganization that merged Peking, Tsinghua, and Yenching universities' liberal arts faculties.
- Studied Chinese literary history for four years (six class hours per week) under notable scholars including You Guoen, Pu Jiangqing (formerly Wang Guowei's assistant), Lin Geng, and others.
- Studied five linguistics courses due to department head Yang Hui's emphasis on the organic connection between language and literature, with teachers including Gao Mingkai, Wei Jiangong, Zhou Zumo, Yuan Jiahua, and Wang Li (who authored "漢語史稿" after his course).
- Influenced by scholars Lin Geng (his advisor), Zhu Ziqing (Lin's teacher), and Wen Yiduo, as well as Yu Pingbo and Wu Zuxiang.

**Part 2: Vertical and Horizontal Connections – From Literary History, Civilization History to Regional Culture**
- In 1995, began editing "History of Chinese Literature" as a "21st-century" textbook involving 30 professors from 19 universities.
- Proposed a three-part framework for literary history: "文學本位" (literary-centered approach), "史學思維" (historical thinking), and "文化學視角" (cultural perspective).
- Introduced the "三古七段" (Three Ancient Eras, Seven Periods) theory for literary periodization, breaking from pure dynastic division. Later refined to "三古七段雙視角" (dual perspective).
- Personally wrote chapters and the general introduction; never served as a "nominal chief editor."
- In 1999, initiated and led the compilation of "History of Chinese Civilization" (中華文明史) as a Peking University National Studies Institute project, involving 36 professors over six years, resulting in four volumes.
- The work was translated into English (by Prof. David R. Knechtges, Cambridge University Press), Japanese (by Waseda University's Inahata Koichiro, expanding four volumes to eight), Russian, Korean, Serbian, Hungarian, and Hindi.
- Edited "Survey of Chinese Regional Culture" (中國地域文化通覽) in 34 volumes organized by province/municipality (including Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan), involving about 500 scholars from local culture and history institutions.
- In 2009, proposed a new "Newly Edited and Newly Annotated Thirteen Classics" project to expand beyond the Confucian classics—removing six traditional texts and adding six new ones (Laozi, Zhuangzi, Mozi, Sunzi, Hanfeizi, Xunzi). Yuan personally handles the new annotation of the Book of Songs (詩經).

**Part 3: Work at the National Studies Institute, Sinologist Research Base, and Central Research Institute**
- Peking University National Studies Institute dates to 1992, funded by Nan Huaijin's donation of $100,000 USD. Publications include the journal "國學研究" (36 volumes to date) and the "國學研究叢刊" series. PhD program began in 2001.
- Created the 150-episode TV program "中華文明之光" (Light of Chinese Civilization) with CCTV.
- In 2009, established the International Sinologists Research Base with Hanban, producing journals "國際漢學研究通訊" and "Chinese Literature and Culture" (English, published in the US). Hosted the International Sinologists Translators Conference in 2014.
- Supports Professor Rong Xinjiang's Marco Polo research project, including a new translation of the travel record.
- At the Central Research Institute of Culture and History, succeeded Qigong as Director in 2006. Currently compiling "中國傳統文化經典百篇" (100 Classic Works of Chinese Traditional Culture).

Professor Yuan closes with his motto: "常懷感激之心，長存謙遜之意" (Always harbor gratitude, always maintain humility), expressing thanks to his teachers, colleagues, students, and friends, including those at CUHK.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"我提出三句話，第一句是「文學本位」，把文學當作文學來研究，不做社會學的圖解。第二句是「史學思維」，文學史是史學，要講出史的發展線索。第三句是「文化學視角」，在廣闊的文化學的背景上研究文學。" (Yuan's three-part framework for literary history), "在文學史的分期上，我打破朝代分期...所以我提出「三古七段」說，即上古、中古、近古，再細分成為七段。" (Yuan's "Three Ancient Eras, Seven Periods" theory), "回顧過去的學術及生活經歷，我有一句話：「常懷感激之心，長存謙遜之意。」" (Yuan's personal motto), "國學研究院沒有一位專職老師，都是兼職。我們的口號是「虛體辦實事」。" (Description of the National Studies Institute's operational model), "我不希望中國文化變得「千人一面」，中國文化是多元的，應當保持各地豐富多彩的特色，找出各地文化發展的優勢。" (Yuan on cultural diversity in China)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 3: 悼傅璇琮先生-清华校友总会 ---
URL: https://www.tsinghua.org.cn/info/1951/20781.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a memorial tribute page from the Tsinghua University Alumni Association website (清华校友总会) honoring the life and legacy of Fu Xuancong (傅璇琮, 1933–2016), a preeminent scholar of classical Chinese literature and one of the most influential figures in Tang Dynasty literary and historical studies over the past half century.

**Key biographical details:**
- Born November 1933 in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province
- Entered Tsinghua University's Chinese Department in 1951; transferred to Peking University's Chinese Department in October 1952 due to the national restructuring of universities; graduated in 1955 and stayed as a teaching assistant
- Suffered political persecution during the "Hu Feng counter-revolutionary clique" investigation and was labeled a "rightist" for involvement with a "anti-Party clique," being demoted to the Commercial Press (商务印书馆) and then to Zhonghua Book Company (中华书局)
- Rose through the ranks at Zhonghua Book Company from editor to chief editor
- Returned to Tsinghua University as a professor in 2008
- Served as Secretary-General of the State Council's Ancient Books Collation and Publishing Planning Group, President of the Chinese Tang Dynasty Literature Society, member of the 9th CPPCC National Committee, and member of the Central Research Institute of Culture and History
- Died January 23, 2016 (described as the coldest day in 30 years)

**Major academic contributions:**
- Published numerous foundational works including 《唐代诗人丛考》(Studies of Tang Dynasty Poets), 《唐代科举与文学》(Tang Dynasty Imperial Examinations and Literature), 《李德裕年谱》, 《唐代诗学丛稿》, 《唐翰林学士传论》, plus major editorial projects like 《全宋诗》, 《全宋笔记》, 《续修四库全书》, and 《中国古籍总目》
- His research emphasized the relationship between politics, social institutions, and literature — pioneering a new methodological approach
- 《唐代科举与文学》won the prestigious Third Siyuan Originality Award (思勉原创奖) in December 2015

**Notable themes and quotes:**
- His early political setbacks were described as "a lifetime's treasure," giving him time to pursue deep scholarship
- He was renowned for mentoring younger scholars, writing prefaces (序言) for 71 books collected in 《学林清谈》— younger scholars considered receiving a preface from him "ascending the dragon gate" (登龙门)
- He integrated Qianjia school textual criticism with Western literary theory (citing Taine's "Art Philosophy" and Lanson's "history of literary life")
- The page includes a personal memoir from a scholar who published his first paper in a journal Fu edited, describing Fu's encouragement
- Fu was still reviewing manuscripts on his deathbed the day before he died

**Related articles linked on the page:** Multiple memorial essays from the Tsinghua alumni website covering his relationship with Tsinghua, his mentoring of younger scholars, his book donations to the library, and the 2023 commemoration of his 90th birthday with the publication of 《傅璇琮文集》.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"傅璇琮先生（1933-2016）是近半个世纪以来文史研究中开风气的领袖人物之一。在唐代文史研究上，更是近五十年来的'第一人'。"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 4: 傅璇琮先生忆念-南方都市报·奥一网 ---
URL: https://epaper.oeeee.com/epaper/A/html/2023-05/21/content_9173.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a memorial article by Guo Jie (郭杰), a professor at Shenzhen University, commemorating the renowned Chinese scholar Fu Xuancong (傅璇琮, 1933–2016) on the occasion of his 90th birthday. The article was published in Southern Metropolis Daily (南方都市报) on May 21, 2023.

**Key context and events:**
- On the occasion of Fu Xuancong's 90th birthday, Zhonghua Book Company (中华书局) published the 24-volume "Collected Works of Fu Xuancong" (《傅璇琮文集》), which includes his major personal works: 《唐代诗人丛考》 (A Study of Tang Dynasty Poets), 《唐代科举与文学》 (Tang Imperial Examinations and Literature), 《唐翰林学士传论》, 《李德裕年谱》, plus co-authored works and a collection of over 360 articles written between 1956–2016 titled 《驼草集》.
- A commemorative symposium was jointly held by Zhonghua Book Company and Tsinghua University's School of Humanities.

**The author's personal connection:**

<summary>
This webpage is a comprehensive interview with Mo Lifeng (莫砺锋), the first Doctor of Literature produced by the People's Republic of China, conducted by Huang Weihao (黄伟豪), an associate professor at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. The interview was originally published in 《文治春秋》第一卷 (2024年春) and is hosted on the aisixiang.com (爱思想) academic website. The piece was updated on 2025-02-19.

**Key biographical details:** Mo Lifeng (born 1949) graduated from Nanjing University in 1984 with a doctoral degree in literature, becoming the first literature PhD trained by the PRC. He is now a senior professor at Nanjing University's School of Humanities and Social Sciences, director of Jiangsu Province's Literature and History Research Institute, and holds various academic positions including member of the National Ancient Books Collation and Publishing Planning Leadership Group and honorary president of the Chinese Song Dynasty Literature Society. He authored the ten-volume 《莫砺锋文集》.

**Major themes covered in the interview:**

1. **Becoming the first literature PhD**: Mo graduated high school in 1966 when the Cultural Revolution halted university admissions, spent ten years farming in rural Anhui, then entered Anhui University's English program after the 1977 gaokao restoration. He transferred to Nanjing University's Chinese department under Cheng Qianfan (程千帆) and became the first doctoral student in Nanda's Chinese department in 1982, defending his dissertation in October 1984. His training involved a four-teacher supervision group (Cheng Qianfan, Zhou Xunchu, Guo Weisen, Wu Xinlei) and a mentorship-style (apprentice-like) training model rather than formal coursework.

2. **Academic heritage and the "Southeast Academic" tradition**: Cheng Qianfan inherited the "Zhang-Huang School" (章黄学派) tradition from Huang Kan (黄侃), who studied under Zhang Taiyan (章太炎). The Southeast Academic tradition emphasizes rationality, steadiness, and humanistic care, balancing new culture promotion with preserving traditional Chinese cultural essence. Cheng's hallmark was "combining textual research with criticism" and "building criticism on the foundation of textual evidence."

3. **Cheng Qianfan's teaching methods**: He used heuristic teaching, held biweekly half-day seminars at his home, and treated students with extraordinary dedication. In his will, Cheng wrote that he considered training excellent students more important than his own scholarship. Cheng's dying concern was the publication of Huang Jigang's (黄侃) diaries, not his own collected works—demonstrating his profound reverence for his teachers.

4. **"Chengmen Disciples" (程门弟子)**: Mo notes that they never called themselves a "school" (Cheng forbade this), but the group shares common scholarly values: combining philology (文献学) with literary theory (文艺学), bridging literature and history, empirical research with problem consciousness, and openness to domestic and international academic exchange. The group has recently developed new fields including overseas Chinese classical texts and overseas Sinology research.

5. **Views on "academic" (学术)**: Mo discusses how the definition of scholarship has historically marginalized literary/writing studies (辞章之学), citing the Institute of History and Philology (史语所) founded by Hu Shi and Fu Sinian as perpetuating this bias. He advocates for pluralistic academic standards rather than uniform criteria, and believes academic communities should be limited to smaller, more coherent fields.

6. **The role of philology (文献学)**: Documentary research has greatly strengthened in recent decades, exemplified by comprehensive collections like 《全宋诗》and 《全宋文》. At Nanjing University, ancient literature and classical philology are treated as one unified "two ancient subjects" (两古学科). Cheng's methodology of "building criticism on the foundation of textual evidence" is exemplified by his study of Zhang Ruoxu's 《春江花月夜》, which traced the poem's reception history to show its literary reputation only rose during the Ming dynasty. Mo himself demonstrated that 《桃花溪》attributed to Tang poet Zhang Xu was actually by Song dynasty calligrapher Cai Xiang, a view now accepted by two new editions of 《全唐诗》.

7. **Individual vs. collective research**: Mo strongly favors individual scholarship for humanities research, arguing it requires personal insight and unique judgment. While collective projects are now common, he believes individual works like Tai Jingnong's 《中国文学史》 retain far greater scholarly value than collective textbooks. He agrees with Qiu Xieyou that individual authors should focus on specialized literary history (断代史 or 文体史) rather than comprehensive surveys, citing Chen Yinke's 《元白诗笺证稿》as a model.

8. **"Poetic life" (诗意人生)**: This concept comes not from Heidegger but from reading Chinese classical poetry. Mo argues that Chinese civilization uniquely avoided the dual obscurations of religious theology and metaphysical thinking, allowing Confucianism (positive engagement with life) and Daoism (transcendent freedom) to complement each other in achieving a poetic grasp of life's meaning. He cites Qu Yuan, Tao Yuanming, Li Bai, Du Fu, Su Shi, and Xin Qiji as exemplars of poetic lives.

9. **"Feeling" as the foundation of literary study**: Following Cheng Qianfan, Mo emphasizes that emotional response ("感") is the primary motivation for literary research. His ten years of rural reading during the Cultural Revolution, though without scholarly guidance or utilitarian purpose, provided profound emotional experiences—reading Du Fu's poetry under a roofless hut, reciting Li Yu's lyrics on rainy nights—that continue to shape his scholarship, reflected in works like 《莫砺锋诗话》and 《杜甫评传》.

10. **On Western scholars and methods**: Mo discusses his interactions with Harvard's Stephen Owen (宇文所安), whom he respects as the finest non-Chinese Western scholar of Chinese poetry, though he finds Chinese evaluations of Owen somewhat inflated. Mo wrote a critical review of Owen's 《初唐诗》and 《盛唐诗》, noting factual errors and disagreeing with Owen's judgments (e.g., Owen rates Wang Wei above Li Bai and Du Fu; Mo disagrees with Owen preferring "望" over "见" in Tao Yuanming's poem). Mo advocates pragmatic method use: "methods are valuable only if they solve problems" (寸铁可以杀人), warning against the "myth of methodology."

11. **Assessment of Republican-era scholarship**: Mo argues today's scholarship generally surpasses the Republican era, though that era produced unmatched individual masters (Wang Guowei, Zhang Taiyan, Liang Qichao). He discusses the "rewriting literary history" (重写文学史) movement, criticizing previous literary histories for overemphasizing socioeconomic background ("庸俗社会论") and using rote author-work listings ("作家作品论") instead of tracing literary development. He acknowledges the immense difficulty of truly rewriting literary history, including unresolved questions about periodization.

12. **Popularization work**: Mo entered popular education relatively late, through writing 《莫砺锋诗话》(2004), giving lectures on CCTV's "百家讲坛" (14 lectures on "诗歌唐朝," later compiled into 《莫砺锋说唐诗》, which sold 100,000 copies), and 《莫砺锋评说白居易》. His 《莫砺锋讲唐诗课》(2019) won the "China Good Book Award" (中国好书奖). He argues scholars have a duty to transmit culture to the public, following Confucius's example of "温故知新" and "述而不作." He believes academic research and popularization are mutually reinforcing.

The interview was edited by chendongdong and is filed under the Literature section (文学 > 语言学和文学学人与经典) of aisixiang.com.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"程先生去世前最放不下的是黄季刚先生日记的出版...程先生在人生的最后瞬间不问他本人全集的事，却念念不忘黄季刚先生的书。" — Cheng Qianfan's dying concern was Huang Kan's diary, not his own works, demonstrating his reverence for teachers. Also, in his will Cheng wrote: "所精心培养学生数人，极为优秀" (the students he carefully trained were extremely outstanding).
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://www.chinastory.cn/PCzwdbk/chinastory/wap/detail/20230630/1006000000039761688086003526176672_1.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article profiles Mo Lifeng (莫砺锋), a 74-year-old distinguished professor of ancient Chinese literature at Nanjing University, who recently retired from teaching after a storied career spanning 45 years. Born with a passion for science and engineering, Mo's dreams were shattered by the Cultural Revolution (the abolition of the college entrance exam), leading him to a decade of rural life as an educated youth (知青) during which he self-studied voraciously. After the 1977 restoration of the college entrance exam, he studied English at Anhui University, then entered Nanjing University's ancient literature program under the mentorship of renowned scholar Cheng Qianfan (程千帆), becoming the first PhD student in the Chinese department in 1982.

Key highlights of his career include: a 2002 lecture on Du Fu on CCTV's "Lecture Room" (百家讲坛) which launched his popularization of classical literature, authoring best-selling books (one printing 100,000 copies), and recent lectures in Sichuan (on Su Dongpo at Sansu Shrine and Du Fu at Du Fu Thatched Cottage) each drawing ~2 million online/offline viewers. He recently published two poetry books for elementary and middle school students.

The article also details Mo's personal philosophy and lifestyle: his study named "Ningdun Zhai" (宁钝斋, "Rather Be Dull Studio") reflecting his father's wish for him not to show off sharpness; his embrace of simplicity (he had no mobile phone until 2018, still takes the subway, and apologizes publicly when he wrongly scolds students); his view that reading classics offers "useless use" (无用之用) as spiritual nourishment in modern society; and his educational philosophy that "being a person is more important than scholarship" (比做学问更重要的是做人), warning against raising "refined egoists." He served briefly as department chair but resigned after ~16 months. He is currently dean of the Mei'an Academy (梅庵书院) at Nanjing University. On May 23, 2023, he delivered his "final class" and formally retired from teaching.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"比做学问更重要的是做人，如果没有学会做人，那学问做得再好也没有意义" (Being a person matters more than scholarship; if one hasn't learned to be a good person, no matter how good the scholarship, it is meaningless), "如果我们培养出来的学生都成为精致的利己主义者，我们的教育就失败了" (If our students become refined egoists, our education has failed), "无用之用，方为大用" (The use of the useless is the greatest use - quoting Zhuangzi), "莫砺锋每次谈及这个话题都会笑起来：'别忘了我姓莫，当年父亲起这个名字就是希望我不露锋芒。'" (Mo laughs whenever discussing his name: "Don't forget my surname is Mo [meaning 'do not']; my father named me hoping I would not show my edge"), "感谢南大的同学至今没有把我轰下讲坛，使我完整地走完了教学生涯" (Thank you to Nanjing University students for never driving me off the podium, allowing me to complete my teaching career)

--- SOURCE 1: 在学术研究中感受生命的活力——访葛晓音--报刊--中国作家网 ---
URL: https://www.chinawriter.com.cn/n1/2016/0810/c405176-28624277.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from 中国作家网 (China Writers Association website), featuring an interview with 葛晓音 (Ge Xiaoyin), a prominent professor of classical Chinese literature at Peking University. The interview was conducted by 梁海燕 and published in 文艺报 (Literary Gazette) on August 10, 2016.

**About the Scholar:** Ge Xiaoyin was born in Shanghai in August 1946. She entered Peking University's Chinese Department in 1963 (five-year program), but only completed two years of basic coursework before the Cultural Revolution interrupted her studies. After graduation, she spent 7 years in Xinjiang (including work at a farm in Hutubi County and teaching at a school in Changji) and later worked at a cultural center in Xinglong County, Hebei. In 1978, she was admitted to a special "refresher class" at Peking University (selected 25 out of 200 graduates of the 1963-1965 cohorts), and in 1979 began graduate studies under Professor 陈贻焮. She stayed at PKU, became a full professor in 1989, and has also taught at Tokyo University and Hong Kong Baptist University. She served as a National People's Congress deputy and currently serves as a CPPCC member. Her major works include 《汉唐文学的嬗变》《诗国高潮与盛唐文化》《先秦汉魏六朝诗歌体式研究》《八代诗史》《唐宋散文》《山水田园诗派研究》《古诗艺术探微》《唐诗宋词十五讲》.

**Key Themes from the Interview:**

1. **Research Approach:** Ge describes her scholarship as driven by old questions continuously generating new ones, rather than pre-designed research agendas. Her dissertation topic "初盛唐诗歌的发展" was deliberately broad, and subsequent research (on the 中唐古文运动, 北宋诗文革新, the "文儒" stratum of the 开元 era, poetry form/genre studies) all emerged from unresolved issues in earlier work. She spent 10 years (from 2002) completing 《先秦汉魏六朝诗歌体式研究》. She also notes the role of serendipity—e.g., discovering in Tokyo that 李峤's 《百咏》 was highly influential in Japan, which led to two major papers on Tang poetry popularization and 干谒 (self-recommendation) practices.

2. **On Method:** During the 1980s "new methodology" debates (including "三论"), Ge adopted an observational stance, arguing that methods should be judged by whether they solve problems. She wrote "吸取新方法要以传统研究方式为本" in 1985. She cites linguist 朱德熙's metaphor: "A method is like an axe—if an old axe can make good furniture, it's still a good axe." She maintains that Chinese classical poetry is not suited to wholesale application of Western poetics, citing discussions with Japanese scholar 松浦友久.

3. **On "自主设计" (Autonomous Design) in Chinese Scholarship:** Ge agrees Chinese scholars should develop their own research approaches but cautions against rushing to predictions. She emphasizes that Chinese scholars have advantages in linguistic nuance and cultural context that Western (and even Japanese) scholars lack, and advocates deeper integration of literary theory with creative writing practice. Traditional Chinese literary criticism uniquely combines poetic theory with creative practice, which should be better leveraged.

4. **On the Modern Value of Classical Literature Research:** Ge argues scholarship is a component of national culture and carries implications for national prestige. She recounts how a Japanese professor in the early 1980s offered to "teach" Chinese scholars because the Cultural Revolution had destroyed their scholarship, deeply shocking her elders. She cites the "无用之用就是大用" (the use of the useless is great use) principle from Zhuangzi. She gives vivid examples: in 1990 in San Francisco, she gave 14 lectures on Tang poetry to overseas Chinese in one month (a Chinese engineer told her he "felt like a Chinese person again"); in Japan, ordinary citizens held spontaneous poetry recitation meetings; in Shanghai and Beijing, public lectures on classical poetry regularly sell out. She quotes 王安石's 《游褒禅山记》 as her personal motto on perseverance. She also argues that contemporary writers need classical literary grounding or their work becomes "rootless wood and sourceless water."
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"我读书的目的是做学术研究，研究的快乐在于攻坚，越是艰难的问题，越能提供发现和创造的乐趣。在攻坚中能激发研究者的活跃思维，感受创造力的旺盛，学者也就获得了源源不断的生命活水。", "方法就好像一把斧子，如果用旧斧子能做出一套好的家具来，也同样是一把好斧子。你用新斧子做一套家具，人家也不会说你的斧子特别新，家具就特别好。——朱德熙", "一个民族如果把学术当作文化娱乐，这个国家的软实力就不得了了。", "1990年，我在美国旧金山讲唐诗……有一个工程师跟我讲：'今天听了你的演讲，我觉得自己是个中国人了。我在美国这么多年，我都不知道自己是什么人了。'", "现当代作家如果没有古代文学修养，写出来的东西就会成为无根之木、无源之水。"
</key_excerpts>
